   117	\begin{remark}
   118	Throughout this work, we will only consider projective strategies.
   119	So we will henceforth use the terms ``strategy" and ``symmetric strategy'' to refer exclusively to projective strategies and symmetric, projective strategies, respectively.
   120	
   121	In addition, we will spend the vast majority of this work dealing solely with symmetric strategies, as they are notationally simpler to work with.
   122	Much of this work will focus on proving~\Cref{thm:main-induction},
   123	a variant of our main theorem for symmetric strategies.
   124	Our main theorem for general strategies, \Cref{thm:main-formal} below, will be proven in \Cref{sec:induction} by a standard reduction to the symmetric case.
   125	We will only see these more cumbersome-to-write general strategies
   126	in this section, where we state \Cref{thm:main-formal},
   127	and in \Cref{sec:induction}, where we carry out the reduction.
   128	\end{remark}
   129	
   130	\begin{definition}[Good strategy]
   131	A strategy is $(\eps, \delta, \gamma)$-good if it
   132	passes the axis-parallel lines test with probability at least $1-\eps$,
   133	the self consistency test with probability at least~$1-\delta$,
   134	and the diagonal lines test with probability at least~$1-\gamma$.
   135	\end{definition}
   136	
   137	\begin{remark}\label{rem:good-strat-characterization}
   138	Using notation which will be introduced in \Cref{sec:comparing-measurements} below,
   139	a symmetric strategy is $(\eps, \delta, \gamma)$-good
   140	if and only if it satisfies the following three conditions.
   141	For $\bell$ and $\bu$ as in the axis-parallel lines test,
   142	\begin{equation*}
   143	A^u_a \ot I \simeq_{\eps} I \ot B^{\ell}_{[f(u)=a]},
   144	\quad
   145	\text{and}
   146	\quad
   147	A^u_a \ot I \simeq_{\delta} I \ot A^u_a.
   148	\end{equation*}
   149	And for $\bell$ and $\bu$ as in the diagonal lines test,
   150	\begin{equation*}
   151	A^u_a \ot I \simeq_{\gamma} I \ot L^{\ell}_{[f(u)=a]}.
   152	\end{equation*}
   153	\end{remark}
   154	
   155	\begin{notation}\label{not:conditioned-on-last-direction}
   156	Our proof will be via induction,
   157	i.e.\ proving soundness of the $(m+1,q,d)$-low individual degree test
   158	using the soundness of the $(m,q,d)$-low individual degree test.
   159	To do this, we will frequently use the axis-parallel line test in the specific case of $i = m+1$.
   160	Thus, it will be convenient to introduce the following notation.
   161	Let $(\psi, A, B, L)$ be a symmetric strategy for the $(m+1, q, d)$-low individual degree test,
   162	Then for each $u \in \F_q^m$ we will write $B^u_f$ as shorthand for $B^{\ell}_f$,
   163	where $\ell = \{(u, x) \mid x \in \F_q\}$.
   164	For a function $f:\ell \rightarrow \F_q$,
   165	we will also sometimes write $f(x)$ as shorthand for $f(u,x)$.
   166	\end{notation}
   167	
   168	\begin{definition}
   169	Consider the $(m,q,d)$-low individual degree test.
   170	For $j \in \{1, \ldots, m\}$,
   171	we refer to the \emph{$j$-restricted diagonal lines test}
   172	as the diagonal lines test conditioned on $\bi = j$.
   173	For example, in the $m$-restricted diagonal lines test,
   174	the line $\bell$ is simply a uniformly random line in $\F_q^m$.
   175	\end{definition}

item.text: The paper-gap note is unusually explicit about directionality: the exact transport needed downstream is the parsing pullback from a direct strategy to the seed-indexed game, while de-seeding an arbitrary seed-dependent strategy still has an open synchronicity obstruction. The new correlated-register construction goes in that difficult opposite direction, so I’m separating what it genuinely proves (per-question Born weights) from any implied game-value correspondence.

    11	
    12	The underlying game is `def:ld-game` in

    27	/-- Coefficient lists for a univariate polynomial of degree at most `c` in the
    28	direct scalar field. -/
    29	abbrev DirectDegPoly (D : DirectLdParams) (c : ℕ) :=
    30	  Fin (c + 1) → DirectScalarQ D
    31	
    32	/-- A direct line polynomial evaluates to `a` at `u` when `u` lies on the line
    33	and every parameter presenting `u` gives value `a`.  The universal clause
    34	keeps the zero-direction case explicit. -/
    35	def DirectEvaluatesTo {D : DirectLdParams} {c : ℕ} (line : DirectLineDesc D)
    36	    (f : DirectDegPoly D c) (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)
    37	    (a : DirectScalarQ D) : Prop :=
    38	  (∃ t : DirectScalarQ D, u = line.base + t • line.direction) ∧
    39	    ∀ t : DirectScalarQ D, u = line.base + t • line.direction →
    40	      evalCoefficient f t = a

    42	/-- Option-completed evaluation of a direct line polynomial.  `none` is an
    43	explicit outcome when the point does not determine an evaluation; no field
    44	value is used as a fallback. -/
    45	noncomputable def directEvalOpt {D : DirectLdParams} {c : ℕ}
    46	    (line : DirectLineDesc D) (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)
    47	    (f : DirectDegPoly D c) : Option (DirectScalarQ D) := by
    48	  classical
    49	  exact if h : ∃ a : DirectScalarQ D, DirectEvaluatesTo line f u a then
    50	    some (Classical.choose h)

   153	noncomputable def directLdWinPredicate (D : DirectLdParams) :
   154	    DirectLdQuestion D → DirectLdQuestion D →
   155	      DirectLdAnswer D → DirectLdAnswer D → Bool :=
   156	  open Classical in
   157	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   158	    if validDirectLdAnswer tA a && validDirectLdAnswer tB b then
   159	      match tA, tB, a, b with
   160	      | .point, .point, .pointVals u, .pointVals v => decide (u = v)
   161	      | .aline, .point, .alinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   162	          decide (directAlinePointCondition D xA xB f u)
   163	      | .point, .aline, .pointVals u, .alinePolys f =>
   164	          decide (directAlinePointCondition D xB xA f u)
   165	      | .dline, .point, .dlinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   166	          decide (directDlinePointCondition D xA xB f u)
   167	      | .point, .dline, .pointVals u, .dlinePolys f =>
   168	          decide (directDlinePointCondition D xB xA f u)
   169	      | .aline, .aline, .alinePolys f, .alinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   170	      | .dline, .dline, .dlinePolys f, .dlinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   171	      | _, _, _, _ => true
   172	    else false

   174	/-- The directly indexed low-degree game at an arbitrary positive dimension.
   175	It is an internal analysis game, not the conditionally linear verifier game
   176	`ldGame`. -/
   177	noncomputable def directLdGame (D : DirectLdParams) : Game where
   178	  QuestionA := DirectLdQuestion D
   179	  QuestionB := DirectLdQuestion D
   180	  AnswerA := DirectLdAnswer D
   181	  AnswerB := DirectLdAnswer D
   182	  μ := directLdQuestionDistribution D
   183	  μ_prob := directLdQuestionDistribution_isProbability D
   184	  decide := directLdWinPredicate D
   185	
   186	/-- The canonical point question associated with a geometric point. -/
   187	def directLdPointQuestionOf (D : DirectLdParams)
   188	    (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) : DirectLdQuestion D :=
   189	  (.point, ⟨u, D.firstIndex, 0⟩)
   190	
   191	/-- Total point-answer relabeling used in the direct soundness conclusion.
   192	Wrong-form answers are folded into the zero tuple, exactly as for
   193	`ldPointValuesOrZero`. -/
   194	def directLdPointValuesOrZero (D : DirectLdParams) :
   195	    DirectLdAnswer D → Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D
   196	  | .pointVals values => values
   197	  | .alinePolys _ => 0
   198	  | .dlinePolys _ => 0
   199	
   200	/-- A simultaneous tuple of bounded polynomials for the directly indexed
   201	game. -/
   202	noncomputable abbrev DirectPolyTuple (D : DirectLdParams) :=
   203	  Fin D.k → PolyIndex D.m (DirectScalarQ D) D.d
   204	
   205	/-- A polynomial-tuple POVM for the directly indexed game. -/
   206	noncomputable abbrev DirectPolyMeasTuple (D : DirectLdParams) (ι : Type*)
   207	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] :=
   208	  Measurement (DirectPolyTuple D) ι
   209	
   210	/-- Evaluate every component of a direct polynomial tuple at a point. -/
   211	def evalDirectPolyTupleAt {D : DirectLdParams}
   212	    (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) (g : DirectPolyTuple D) :
   213	    Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D :=
   214	  fun j => MvPolynomial.eval u (g j).1
   215	
   216	end

     5	/-!
     6	# Geometry for the directly indexed low-degree game
     7	
     8	This module defines the parameters, line carrier, and line-point distributions
     9	for the directly indexed low-degree game.
    10	
    11	## References
    12	
    13	The line-point distributions originate in
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-272`.
    15	The directly indexed repair is documented in
    16	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`.
    17	-/
    18	
    19	open scoped BigOperators
    20	
    21	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    22	
    23	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    24	open MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries
    25	open MIPStarRE.Quantum

    27	noncomputable section
    28	
    29	/-- Parameters for the directly indexed low-degree game.  Unlike `LdParams`,
    30	this directly indexed line-space construction has no divisibility field: its coordinate index is
    31	sampled from `Fin m` rather than encoded by fibers of `chiIndex`.
    32	
    33	This is the direct-index repair described in
    34	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`; it is not a second
    35	definition of the source verifier game. -/
    36	structure DirectLdParams where
    37	  q : ℕ
    38	  m : ℕ
    39	  d : ℕ
    40	  k : ℕ
    41	  hm : 1 ≤ m
    42	  hd : 1 ≤ d
    43	  hk : 1 ≤ k
    44	  hq : IsAdmissibleSize q
    45	
    46	/-- The canonical scalar model for directly indexed parameters. -/
    47	noncomputable def DirectLdParams.model (D : DirectLdParams) : FixedFieldModel D.q :=
    48	  fixedFieldModel D.q D.hq
    49	
    50	/-- The scalar field of a directly indexed low-degree game. -/
    51	abbrev DirectScalarQ (D : DirectLdParams) := D.model.K
    52	
    53	/-- The first coordinate, available because directly indexed dimensions are
    54	positive. -/
    55	def DirectLdParams.firstIndex (D : DirectLdParams) : Fin D.m :=
    56	  ⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one D.hm⟩
    57	
    58	instance (D : DirectLdParams) : Nonempty (Fin D.m) := ⟨D.firstIndex⟩
    59	
    60	/-- The direct game used at the extended dimension of the combining map.  Its
    61	field, degree, and simultaneity parameters are inherited from `P`, while its
    62	dimension is `2 * P.m + 2`; no divisibility assertion is introduced.
    63	
    64	The construction has dimension `2 * P.m + 2` without requiring
    65	`2 * P.m + 2 ∣ P.q`; it supplies the directly indexed line and coordinate
    66	spaces used in the dimension-extension argument of
    67	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1257-1293`.

    69	def AdmissibleParams.extendedDirectLd (P : AdmissibleParams) : DirectLdParams where

    71	  m := 2 * P.m + 2
    72	  d := P.d

    74	  hm := by omega
    75	  hd := P.hd
    76	  hk := by decide
    77	  hq := P.hq

    79	/-- A common random sample for the directly indexed question distribution.

    83	  index : Fin D.m

    90	/-- Decompose a direct sample into its point and the remaining independent

    93	    DirectLdSpace D ≃
    94	      (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) ×
    95	        (Fin D.m × (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) where
    96	  toFun sample := (sample.point, sample.index, sample.direction)
    97	  invFun sample := ⟨sample.1, sample.2.1, sample.2.2⟩

   153	/-- The base of a directly indexed description is fixed by its geometric

   340	theorem directDLinePointDist_prefix_zero (D : DirectLdParams) :
   341	    ∀ sample ∈ (directDLinePointDist D).support,
   342	      ∀ j : Fin D.m, j.val < sample.1.index.val →
   343	        sample.1.direction j = 0 := by
   344	  intro sample hsample j hj
   345	  rw [directDLinePointDist, Distribution.map_support,
   346	    uniformDistribution_support] at hsample
   347	  rcases Finset.mem_image.mp hsample with ⟨source, _, rfl⟩
   348	  exact DirectLineDesc.diagonal_prefix_zero
   349	    (directDLineDescOf D source) (by
   350	      simp [directDLineDescOf, DirectLineDesc.kind]) j hj

    18	/-- The SWAP reindexing on `ι × ι`: permutes the two tensor factors.
    19	`swapDensity M (i₁,i₂) (j₁,j₂) = M (i₂,i₁) (j₂,j₁)`. -/
    20	def swapDensity {ι : Type*} (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ι × ι)) :
    21	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ι × ι) :=
    22	  Matrix.of fun (ij : ι × ι) (kl : ι × ι) => M (ij.2, ij.1) (kl.2, kl.1)
    23	
    24	/-- `swapDensity` is equal to reindexing by the product-commutation equivalence. -/
    25	lemma swapDensity_eq_reindex {ι : Type*}
    26	    (X : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ι × ι)) :
    27	    swapDensity X = Matrix.reindex (Equiv.prodComm ι ι) (Equiv.prodComm ι ι) X := by
    28	  ext x y
    29	  rcases x with ⟨i₁, i₂⟩
    30	  rcases y with ⟨j₁, j₂⟩
    31	  rfl
    32	
    33	@[simp] lemma swapDensity_swapDensity {ι : Type*}
    34	    (X : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ι × ι)) :
    35	    swapDensity (swapDensity X) = X := by
    36	  ext x y
    37	  rcases x with ⟨i₁, i₂⟩
    38	  rcases y with ⟨j₁, j₂⟩
    39	  rfl
    40	
    41	@[simp] lemma swapDensity_add {ι : Type*}
    42	    (X Y : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ι × ι)) :
    43	    swapDensity (X + Y) = swapDensity X + swapDensity Y := by
    44	  ext x y
    45	  rcases x with ⟨i₁, i₂⟩
    46	  rcases y with ⟨j₁, j₂⟩
    47	  rfl
    48	
    49	@[simp] lemma swapDensity_smul {ι : Type*} (c : ℂ)
    50	    (X : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ι × ι)) :
    51	    swapDensity (c • X) = c • swapDensity X := by
    52	  ext x y
    53	  rcases x with ⟨i₁, i₂⟩
    54	  rcases y with ⟨j₁, j₂⟩
    55	  rfl

    57	/-- `swapDensity` preserves matrix multiplication. -/
    58	lemma swapDensity_mul {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    59	    (X Y : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ι × ι)) :
    60	    swapDensity (X * Y) = swapDensity X * swapDensity Y := by
    61	  classical
    62	  simpa [swapDensity_eq_reindex] using
    63	    (map_mul (Matrix.reindexAlgEquiv ℂ ℂ (Equiv.prodComm ι ι)) X Y)

    65	lemma swapDensity_opTensor {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    66	    (X Y : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι) :
    67	    swapDensity (opTensor X Y) = opTensor Y X := by
    68	  ext x y
    69	  rcases x with ⟨i₁, i₂⟩
    70	  rcases y with ⟨j₁, j₂⟩
    71	  simp [swapDensity, opTensor, mul_comm]

    73	lemma normalizedTrace_swapDensity {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    74	    (X : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ι × ι)) :
    75	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace (swapDensity X) = MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace X := by
    76	  simpa [swapDensity_eq_reindex] using
    77	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace_reindex (Equiv.prodComm ι ι) X

    79	theorem ev_swapDensity_of_density_fixed {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    80	    (ψ : QuantumState (ι × ι))
    81	    (hfix : swapDensity ψ.density = ψ.density)
    82	    (Z : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ι × ι)) :
    83	    ev ψ (swapDensity Z) = ev ψ Z := by
    84	  unfold ev
    85	  apply congrArg Complex.re
    86	  calc
    87	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace (ψ.density * swapDensity Z)
    88	      = MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace (swapDensity (ψ.density * Z)) := by
    89	          rw [swapDensity_mul]
    90	          simp [hfix]
    91	    _ = MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace (ψ.density * Z) :=
    92	          normalizedTrace_swapDensity _

    94	theorem ev_opTensor_swap_of_density_fixed {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    95	    (ψ : QuantumState (ι × ι))
    96	    (hfix : swapDensity ψ.density = ψ.density)
    97	    (X Y : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι) :
    98	    ev ψ (opTensor X Y) = ev ψ (opTensor Y X) := by
    99	  rw [show opTensor Y X = swapDensity (opTensor X Y) by
   100	    rw [swapDensity_opTensor]]
   101	  exact (ev_swapDensity_of_density_fixed ψ hfix (opTensor X Y)).symm

   103	theorem qBipartiteMatchMass_symm_of_density_fixed {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   104	    (ψ : QuantumState (ι × ι))
   105	    (hfix : swapDensity ψ.density = ψ.density)
   106	    {Outcome : Type*} [Fintype Outcome]
   107	    (A B : SubMeas Outcome ι) :
   108	    qBipartiteMatchMass ψ A B = qBipartiteMatchMass ψ B A := by
   109	  unfold qBipartiteMatchMass
   110	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
   111	  intro a _
   112	  exact ev_opTensor_swap_of_density_fixed ψ hfix (A.outcome a) (B.outcome a)

   114	theorem qBipartiteConsDefect_symm_of_density_fixed {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   115	    (ψ : QuantumState (ι × ι))
   116	    (hfix : swapDensity ψ.density = ψ.density)
   117	    {Outcome : Type*} [Fintype Outcome]
   118	    (A B : SubMeas Outcome ι) :
   119	    qBipartiteConsDefect ψ A B = qBipartiteConsDefect ψ B A := by
   120	  simp [qBipartiteConsDefect,
   121	    qBipartiteMatchMass_symm_of_density_fixed ψ hfix,
   122	    ev_opTensor_swap_of_density_fixed ψ hfix]

   124	theorem consRel_symm_of_density_fixed {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   125	    (ψ : QuantumState (ι × ι))
   126	    (hfix : swapDensity ψ.density = ψ.density)
   127	    {Question Outcome : Type*} [Fintype Outcome]
   128	    (𝒟 : Distribution Question)
   129	    (A B : IdxSubMeas Question Outcome ι)
   130	    (δ : Error) :
   131	    ConsRel ψ 𝒟 A B δ → ConsRel ψ 𝒟 B A δ := by
   132	  intro ⟨h⟩
   133	  constructor
   134	  unfold bipartiteConsError at *
   135	  calc
   136	    avgOver 𝒟 (fun q => qBipartiteConsDefect ψ (B q) (A q))
   137	      = avgOver 𝒟 (fun q => qBipartiteConsDefect ψ (A q) (B q)) := by
   138	          apply avgOver_congr
   139	          intro q
   140	          symm
   141	          exact qBipartiteConsDefect_symm_of_density_fixed ψ hfix (A q) (B q)
   142	    _ ≤ δ := h

   144	/-- Permutation-invariance for a bipartite state on `ι × ι`.
   145	
   146	The primary datum is that the density operator is fixed by the SWAP reindexing,
   147	`swapDensity ψ.density = ψ.density`.  We also cache the frequently used
   148	one-sided expectation consequence
   149	`ev ψ (leftTensor M) = ev ψ (rightTensor M)`.
   150	This matches the symmetric-strategy construction used in the paper
   151	(Section 3) and exposes enough symmetry to swap fully bipartite
   152	consistency expressions. -/
   153	structure PermInvState {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   154	    (ψ : QuantumState (ι × ι)) : Prop where
   155	  /-- The density operator is fixed by the SWAP reindexing. -/
   156	  density_swap : swapDensity ψ.density = ψ.density
   157	  /-- Swapping tensor factors preserves one-sided expectation values. -/
   158	  swap_ev : ∀ (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι),
   159	    ev ψ (leftTensor (ι₂ := ι) M) =
   160	      ev ψ (rightTensor (ι₁ := ι) M)

   162	/-- Direct outcome-level covariance for axis-parallel-line measurements.
   163	
   164	Rebasing a line question by `t` and reparametrizing an outcome polynomial by
   165	the same translation leaves the corresponding projector unchanged. -/
   166	def AxisParallelMeasurementReparamInvariant (params : Parameters)
   167	    [FieldModel params.q] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   168	    (M : IdxProjMeas (AxisParallelLine params) (AxisLinePolynomial params) ι) : Prop :=
   169	  ∀ (ℓ : AxisParallelLine params) (t : Fq params) (f : AxisLinePolynomial params),
   170	    (M (ℓ.rebaseAt t)).outcome (AxisLinePolynomial.reparamAt f t) =
   171	      (M ℓ).outcome f

   173	/-- Direct outcome-level covariance for diagonal-line measurements.
   174	
   175	Rebasing a line question by `t` and reparametrizing an outcome polynomial by
   176	the same translation leaves the corresponding projector unchanged. -/
   177	def DiagonalMeasurementReparamInvariant (params : Parameters)
   178	    [FieldModel params.q] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   179	    (M : IdxProjMeas (DiagonalLine params) (DiagonalLinePolynomial params) ι) : Prop :=
   180	  ∀ (ℓ : DiagonalLine params) (t : Fq params) (f : DiagonalLinePolynomial params),
   181	    (M (ℓ.rebaseAt t)).outcome (DiagonalLinePolynomial.reparamAt f t) =
   182	      (M ℓ).outcome f
   183	
   184	/-- Reparametrization invariance for diagonal-line measurements: evaluating a
   185	rebased line at `zeroCoord` agrees outcome-wise with evaluating the original
   186	line at the rebasing parameter.
   187	
   188	At the answer level, the geometric identity is
   189	`DiagonalLinePolynomial.reparamAt_apply_zero`. This predicate is stronger: it
   190	asserts that the *measurement family itself* is covariant under rebasing the
   191	question index. -/
   192	def DiagonalEvaluationReparamInvariant (params : Parameters)
   193	    [FieldModel params.q] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   194	    (M : IdxProjMeas (DiagonalLine params) (DiagonalLinePolynomial params) ι) : Prop :=
   195	  ∀ (ℓ : DiagonalLine params) (t a : Fq params),
   196	    (postprocess ((M (DiagonalLine.rebaseAt ℓ t)).toSubMeas) (· zeroCoord)).outcome a =
   197	      (postprocess ((M ℓ).toSubMeas) (fun f => f t)).outcome a

   211	/-- Transport an axis-parallel-line measurement along rebasing of the line
   212	question by translating its polynomial outcomes. -/
   213	noncomputable def transportMeasurement {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
   214	    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   215	    (M : ProjMeas (AxisLinePolynomial params) ι) (t : Fq params) :
   216	    ProjMeas (AxisLinePolynomial params) ι :=
   217	  ProjMeas.transport (AxisLinePolynomial.reparamAtEquiv (params := params) t) M
   218	
   219	/-- Evaluating a transported axis-line measurement at `zeroCoord` agrees with
   220	reading the original measurement at the rebasing parameter. -/
   221	theorem transportMeasurement_postprocess_zero
   222	    {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
   223	    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   224	    (M : ProjMeas (AxisLinePolynomial params) ι) (t a : Fq params) :
   225	    (postprocess (transportMeasurement (params := params) M t).toSubMeas
   226	        (· zeroCoord)).outcome a =
   227	      (postprocess M.toSubMeas (fun f => f t)).outcome a := by
   228	  have h :=
   229	    SubMeas.postprocess_transport
   230	      (e := AxisLinePolynomial.reparamAtEquiv (params := params) t)
   231	      (A := M.toSubMeas)
   232	      (f := fun g : AxisLinePolynomial params => g zeroCoord)
   233	  simpa [transportMeasurement, AxisLinePolynomial.reparamAtEquiv,
   234	    AxisLinePolynomial.reparamAt_apply_zero, addCoord, zeroCoord] using
   235	    congrArg (fun A => A.outcome a) h
   236	
   237	end AxisParallelLine

   289	/-- Transport-level axis-parallel covariance implies direct outcome covariance. -/
   290	theorem AxisParallelMeasurementTransportInvariant.toMeasurementReparamInvariant
   291	    {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   292	    {M : IdxProjMeas (AxisParallelLine params) (AxisLinePolynomial params) ι}

   298	  have h := congrArg (fun N => N.outcome
   299	    (AxisLinePolynomial.reparamAtEquiv (params := params) t f)) (hM ℓ t)
   300	  simpa only [AxisParallelLine.transportMeasurement, ProjMeas.transport,

   211	
   212	/-- The coefficient-tuple answer alphabet of the low-degree game.  Polynomial
   213	answers are representatives with exactly the coefficient lengths printed in
   214	the paper, as required by `def:ld-win-predicate` (blueprint
   215	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`; paper
   216	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   217	-/
   218	inductive LdAnswer (P : LdParams) where
   219	  | pointVals (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P)
   220	  | alinePolys (a : Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   221	  | dlinePolys (a : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   222	  deriving DecidableEq
   223	
   224	/-- A finite sum code used only to provide the answer alphabet's `Fintype`
   225	instance; the public constructors are those of `def:ld-win-predicate`,
   226	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   227	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   228	-/
   229	abbrev LdAnswerCode (P : LdParams) :=
   230	  (Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) ⊕
   231	    ((Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P) ⊕
   232	      (Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P))
   233	
   234	/-- The constructor-preserving code equivalence for `LdAnswer` (Lean-only
   235	finite-carrier infrastructure for `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   236	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   237	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   238	-/
   239	noncomputable def ldAnswerEquiv (P : LdParams) :
   240	    LdAnswer P ≃ LdAnswerCode P where
   241	  toFun
   242	    | .pointVals a => .inl a
   243	    | .alinePolys a => .inr (.inl a)
   244	    | .dlinePolys a => .inr (.inr a)
   245	  invFun
   246	    | .inl a => .pointVals a
   247	    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePolys a
   248	    | .inr (.inr a) => .dlinePolys a
   249	  left_inv := by intro x; cases x <;> rfl
   250	  right_inv := by
   251	    intro x
   252	    cases x with
   253	    | inl a => rfl
   254	    | inr x =>
   255	        cases x with
   256	        | inl a => rfl
   257	        | inr a => rfl
   258	
   259	instance (P : LdParams) : Inhabited (LdAnswer P) :=
   260	  ⟨.pointVals (fun _ => 0)⟩
   261	
   262	noncomputable instance (P : LdParams) : Fintype (LdAnswer P) :=
   263	  Fintype.ofEquiv (LdAnswerCode P) (ldAnswerEquiv P).symm
   264	
   265	/-- Evaluation of a coefficient tuple at a field element.  This is the
   266	representative convention used by the line answers in `def:ld-win-predicate`,
   267	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   268	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   269	-/
   270	def evalCoefficient {K : Type*} [Semiring K] {n : ℕ}
   271	    (c : Fin n → K) (t : K) : K :=
   272	  ∑ i : Fin n, c i * t ^ i.val
   273	
   274	/-- Check that an answer has the constructor prescribed by its question type;
   275	Lean encoding of the rejection clause in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   276	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   277	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   278	-/
   279	def validLdAnswer {P : LdParams} (t : LdType) (a : LdAnswer P) : Bool :=
   280	  match t, a with
   281	  | .point, .pointVals _ => true
   282	  | .aline, .alinePolys _ => true
   283	  | .dline, .dlinePolys _ => true
   284	  | _, _ => false
   285	
   286	/-- The axis-parallel line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   287	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   288	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   289	-/
   290	def alinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
   291	    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   292	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   293	  -- Universal quantification follows the zero-direction convention in
   294	  -- `rem:ld-win-zero-direction`.
   295	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   296	    point.point = line.point + t • coordinateDirection (chiIndex P line.seed) →
   297	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   298	
   299	/-- The diagonal line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   300	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   301	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   302	-/
   303	def dlinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
   304	    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   305	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   306	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   307	    point.point = line.point + t • line.direction →
   308	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   309	
   310	/-- The low-degree consistency predicate, rejecting answers of the wrong
   311	constructor shape.  This is `def:ld-win-predicate` in
   312	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   313	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   314	-/
   315	noncomputable def ldWinPredicate (P : LdParams) :
   316	    LdQuestion P → LdQuestion P → LdAnswer P → LdAnswer P → Bool :=
   317	  open Classical in
   318	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   319	      if validLdAnswer tA a && validLdAnswer tB b then
   320	        match tA, tB, a, b with
   321	        | .point, .point, .pointVals u, .pointVals v => decide (u = v)
   322	        | .aline, .point, .alinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   323	            decide (alinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   324	        | .point, .aline, .pointVals u, .alinePolys f =>
   325	            decide (alinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   326	        | .dline, .point, .dlinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   327	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   328	        | .point, .dline, .pointVals u, .dlinePolys f =>
   329	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   330	        | .aline, .aline, .alinePolys f, .alinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   331	        | .dline, .dline, .dlinePolys f, .dlinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   332	        | _, _, _, _ => true
   333	      else false
   334	
   335	/-- The low-degree game packaged as a `Game`.  This is `def:ld-game` in
   336	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, paper origin
   337	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   338	-/
   339	noncomputable def ldGame (P : LdParams) : Game where
   340	  QuestionA := LdQuestion P
   341	  QuestionB := LdQuestion P
   342	  AnswerA := LdAnswer P
   343	  AnswerB := LdAnswer P
   344	  μ := ldQuestionDistribution P
   345	  μ_prob := by sorry
   346	  decide := ldWinPredicate P
   347	
   348	end
   349	
   350	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

    18	/-- The SWAP reindexing on `ι × ι`: permutes the two tensor factors.
    19	`swapDensity M (i₁,i₂) (j₁,j₂) = M (i₂,i₁) (j₂,j₁)`. -/
    20	def swapDensity {ι : Type*} (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ι × ι)) :
    21	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ι × ι) :=
    22	  Matrix.of fun (ij : ι × ι) (kl : ι × ι) => M (ij.2, ij.1) (kl.2, kl.1)
    23	
    24	/-- `swapDensity` is equal to reindexing by the product-commutation equivalence. -/
    25	lemma swapDensity_eq_reindex {ι : Type*}
    26	    (X : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ι × ι)) :
    27	    swapDensity X = Matrix.reindex (Equiv.prodComm ι ι) (Equiv.prodComm ι ι) X := by
    28	  ext x y
    29	  rcases x with ⟨i₁, i₂⟩
    30	  rcases y with ⟨j₁, j₂⟩
    31	  rfl
    32	
    33	@[simp] lemma swapDensity_swapDensity {ι : Type*}
    34	    (X : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ι × ι)) :
    35	    swapDensity (swapDensity X) = X := by
    36	  ext x y
    37	  rcases x with ⟨i₁, i₂⟩
    38	  rcases y with ⟨j₁, j₂⟩
    39	  rfl
    40	
    41	@[simp] lemma swapDensity_add {ι : Type*}
    42	    (X Y : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ι × ι)) :
    43	    swapDensity (X + Y) = swapDensity X + swapDensity Y := by
    44	  ext x y
    45	  rcases x with ⟨i₁, i₂⟩
    46	  rcases y with ⟨j₁, j₂⟩
    47	  rfl
    48	
    49	@[simp] lemma swapDensity_smul {ι : Type*} (c : ℂ)
    50	    (X : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ι × ι)) :
    51	    swapDensity (c • X) = c • swapDensity X := by
    52	  ext x y
    53	  rcases x with ⟨i₁, i₂⟩
    54	  rcases y with ⟨j₁, j₂⟩
    55	  rfl
    56	
    57	/-- `swapDensity` preserves matrix multiplication. -/
    58	lemma swapDensity_mul {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    59	    (X Y : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ι × ι)) :
    60	    swapDensity (X * Y) = swapDensity X * swapDensity Y := by
    61	  classical
    62	  simpa [swapDensity_eq_reindex] using
    63	    (map_mul (Matrix.reindexAlgEquiv ℂ ℂ (Equiv.prodComm ι ι)) X Y)
    64	
    65	lemma swapDensity_opTensor {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    66	    (X Y : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι) :
    67	    swapDensity (opTensor X Y) = opTensor Y X := by
    68	  ext x y
    69	  rcases x with ⟨i₁, i₂⟩
    70	  rcases y with ⟨j₁, j₂⟩
    71	  simp [swapDensity, opTensor, mul_comm]

    73	lemma normalizedTrace_swapDensity {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    74	    (X : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ι × ι)) :
    75	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace (swapDensity X) = MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace X := by
    76	  simpa [swapDensity_eq_reindex] using
    77	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace_reindex (Equiv.prodComm ι ι) X

    79	theorem ev_swapDensity_of_density_fixed {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    80	    (ψ : QuantumState (ι × ι))
    81	    (hfix : swapDensity ψ.density = ψ.density)
    82	    (Z : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ι × ι)) :
    83	    ev ψ (swapDensity Z) = ev ψ Z := by
    84	  unfold ev
    85	  apply congrArg Complex.re
    86	  calc
    87	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace (ψ.density * swapDensity Z)
    88	      = MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace (swapDensity (ψ.density * Z)) := by
    89	          rw [swapDensity_mul]
    90	          simp [hfix]
    91	    _ = MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace (ψ.density * Z) :=
    92	          normalizedTrace_swapDensity _

    94	theorem ev_opTensor_swap_of_density_fixed {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    95	    (ψ : QuantumState (ι × ι))
    96	    (hfix : swapDensity ψ.density = ψ.density)
    97	    (X Y : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι) :
    98	    ev ψ (opTensor X Y) = ev ψ (opTensor Y X) := by
    99	  rw [show opTensor Y X = swapDensity (opTensor X Y) by
   100	    rw [swapDensity_opTensor]]
   101	  exact (ev_swapDensity_of_density_fixed ψ hfix (opTensor X Y)).symm

   103	theorem qBipartiteMatchMass_symm_of_density_fixed {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   104	    (ψ : QuantumState (ι × ι))
   105	    (hfix : swapDensity ψ.density = ψ.density)
   106	    {Outcome : Type*} [Fintype Outcome]
   107	    (A B : SubMeas Outcome ι) :
   108	    qBipartiteMatchMass ψ A B = qBipartiteMatchMass ψ B A := by
   109	  unfold qBipartiteMatchMass
   110	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
   111	  intro a _
   112	  exact ev_opTensor_swap_of_density_fixed ψ hfix (A.outcome a) (B.outcome a)

   114	theorem qBipartiteConsDefect_symm_of_density_fixed {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   115	    (ψ : QuantumState (ι × ι))
   116	    (hfix : swapDensity ψ.density = ψ.density)
   117	    {Outcome : Type*} [Fintype Outcome]
   118	    (A B : SubMeas Outcome ι) :
   119	    qBipartiteConsDefect ψ A B = qBipartiteConsDefect ψ B A := by
   120	  simp [qBipartiteConsDefect,
   121	    qBipartiteMatchMass_symm_of_density_fixed ψ hfix,
   122	    ev_opTensor_swap_of_density_fixed ψ hfix]

   124	theorem consRel_symm_of_density_fixed {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   125	    (ψ : QuantumState (ι × ι))
   126	    (hfix : swapDensity ψ.density = ψ.density)
   127	    {Question Outcome : Type*} [Fintype Outcome]
   128	    (𝒟 : Distribution Question)
   129	    (A B : IdxSubMeas Question Outcome ι)
   130	    (δ : Error) :
   131	    ConsRel ψ 𝒟 A B δ → ConsRel ψ 𝒟 B A δ := by
   132	  intro ⟨h⟩
   133	  constructor
   134	  unfold bipartiteConsError at *
   135	  calc
   136	    avgOver 𝒟 (fun q => qBipartiteConsDefect ψ (B q) (A q))
   137	      = avgOver 𝒟 (fun q => qBipartiteConsDefect ψ (A q) (B q)) := by
   138	          apply avgOver_congr
   139	          intro q
   140	          symm
   141	          exact qBipartiteConsDefect_symm_of_density_fixed ψ hfix (A q) (B q)
   142	    _ ≤ δ := h

   144	/-- Permutation-invariance for a bipartite state on `ι × ι`.
   145	
   146	The primary datum is that the density operator is fixed by the SWAP reindexing,
   147	`swapDensity ψ.density = ψ.density`.  We also cache the frequently used
   148	one-sided expectation consequence
   149	`ev ψ (leftTensor M) = ev ψ (rightTensor M)`.
   150	This matches the symmetric-strategy construction used in the paper
   151	(Section 3) and exposes enough symmetry to swap fully bipartite
   152	consistency expressions. -/
   153	structure PermInvState {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   154	    (ψ : QuantumState (ι × ι)) : Prop where
   155	  /-- The density operator is fixed by the SWAP reindexing. -/
   156	  density_swap : swapDensity ψ.density = ψ.density
   157	  /-- Swapping tensor factors preserves one-sided expectation values. -/
   158	  swap_ev : ∀ (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι),
   159	    ev ψ (leftTensor (ι₂ := ι) M) =
   160	      ev ψ (rightTensor (ι₁ := ι) M)

   162	/-- Direct outcome-level covariance for axis-parallel-line measurements.
   163	
   164	Rebasing a line question by `t` and reparametrizing an outcome polynomial by
   165	the same translation leaves the corresponding projector unchanged. -/
   166	def AxisParallelMeasurementReparamInvariant (params : Parameters)
   167	    [FieldModel params.q] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   168	    (M : IdxProjMeas (AxisParallelLine params) (AxisLinePolynomial params) ι) : Prop :=
   169	  ∀ (ℓ : AxisParallelLine params) (t : Fq params) (f : AxisLinePolynomial params),
   170	    (M (ℓ.rebaseAt t)).outcome (AxisLinePolynomial.reparamAt f t) =
   171	      (M ℓ).outcome f
   172	
   173	/-- Direct outcome-level covariance for diagonal-line measurements.
   174	
   175	Rebasing a line question by `t` and reparametrizing an outcome polynomial by
   176	the same translation leaves the corresponding projector unchanged. -/
   177	def DiagonalMeasurementReparamInvariant (params : Parameters)
   178	    [FieldModel params.q] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   179	    (M : IdxProjMeas (DiagonalLine params) (DiagonalLinePolynomial params) ι) : Prop :=
   180	  ∀ (ℓ : DiagonalLine params) (t : Fq params) (f : DiagonalLinePolynomial params),
   181	    (M (ℓ.rebaseAt t)).outcome (DiagonalLinePolynomial.reparamAt f t) =
   182	      (M ℓ).outcome f
   183	
   184	/-- Reparametrization invariance for diagonal-line measurements: evaluating a
   185	rebased line at `zeroCoord` agrees outcome-wise with evaluating the original
   186	line at the rebasing parameter.
   187	
   188	At the answer level, the geometric identity is
   189	`DiagonalLinePolynomial.reparamAt_apply_zero`. This predicate is stronger: it
   190	asserts that the *measurement family itself* is covariant under rebasing the
   191	question index. -/
   192	def DiagonalEvaluationReparamInvariant (params : Parameters)
   193	    [FieldModel params.q] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   194	    (M : IdxProjMeas (DiagonalLine params) (DiagonalLinePolynomial params) ι) : Prop :=
   195	  ∀ (ℓ : DiagonalLine params) (t a : Fq params),
   196	    (postprocess ((M (DiagonalLine.rebaseAt ℓ t)).toSubMeas) (· zeroCoord)).outcome a =
   197	      (postprocess ((M ℓ).toSubMeas) (fun f => f t)).outcome a
   198	
   199	/-- Reparametrization invariance for axis-parallel-line measurements: evaluating a
   200	rebased line at `zeroCoord` agrees outcome-wise with evaluating the original
   201	line at the rebasing parameter. -/
   202	def AxisParallelEvaluationReparamInvariant (params : Parameters)
   203	    [FieldModel params.q] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   204	    (M : IdxProjMeas (AxisParallelLine params) (AxisLinePolynomial params) ι) : Prop :=

   445	/-- Transport covariance for diagonal-line measurements whose answers are the
   446	paper-level line functions. -/
   447	def DiagonalAnswerMeasurementTransportInvariant (params : Parameters)
   448	    [FieldModel params.q] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   449	    (M : IdxProjMeas (DiagonalLine params) (DiagonalLineAnswer params) ι) : Prop :=
   450	  ∀ (ℓ : DiagonalLine params) (t : Fq params),

   453	
   454	/-- Diagonal-line measurements with paper-level function answers, bundled with

    71	An important class of strategies are those which are \emph{symmetric}.
    72	In this case, the bipartite state $\ket{\psi}$ Alice and Bob share is symmetric.
    73	Furthermore, for any question Alice and Bob receive, they apply the same measurement to their share of the state.
    74	This means that rather than, for example, keeping track of a separate points measurement for Alice and Bob,
    75	we can use a single measurement to refer to both of their strategies,
    76	and similarly for the axis-parallel lines and diagonal lines measurements.
    77	This is formalized in the following definition, where we also consider strategies which are projective.
    78	
    79	\begin{definition}[Symmetric, projective strategy]
    80	A \emph{symmetric, projective strategy} for the $(m,q, d)$-low individual degree test
    81	is a tuple $(\psi, A, B, L)$ defined as follows.
    82	\begin{itemize}
    83	\item[$\circ$] $\ket{\psi} \in \calH \ot \calH$ is a bipartite, permutation-invariant state.
    84	\item[$\circ$] $A = \{A^u_a\}$ contains a matrix for each $u \in \F_q^m$ and $a \in \F_q$.
    85				For each $u$, $A^u$ is a projective measurement on~$\calH$.
    86	\item[$\circ$] $B = \{B^{\ell}_f\}$ contains a matrix for each axis-parallel line~$\ell$ in $\F_q^m$
    87				and univariate degree-$d$ polynomial $f:\ell\rightarrow \F_q$.
    88				For each $\ell$, $B^{\ell}$ is a projective measurement on~$\calH$.
    89	\item[$\circ$] $L = \{L^{\ell}_f\}$ contains a matrix for each line~$\ell$ in $\F_q^m$
    90				and univariate degree-$md$ polynomial $f:\ell\rightarrow \F_q$.
    91				For each $\ell$, $L^{\ell}$ is a projective measurement on~$\calH$.
    92	\end{itemize}
    93	\end{definition}
    94	
    95	We can also consider more general strategies which are no longer assumed to be symmetric.
    96	In this case, Players~$\mathrm{A}$ and~$\mathrm{B}$ each have their own versions of the measurements~$A$, $B$, and~$L$.
    97	
    98	\begin{definition}[General projective strategy]
    99	A \emph{projective strategy} for the $(m,q, d)$-low individual degree test
   100	is a tuple $(\psi, A^{\mathrm{A}},B^{\mathrm{A}},L^{\mathrm{A}},A^{\mathrm{B}},B^{\mathrm{B}},L^{\mathrm{B}})$ defined as follows.
   101	\begin{itemize}
   102	\item[$\circ$] $\ket{\psi} \in \calH_{\mathrm{A}} \ot \calH_{\mathrm{B}}$ is a bipartite state.
   103	\end{itemize}
   104	Furthermore, for each~$w \in \{\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}\}$:
   105	\begin{itemize}
   106	\item[$\circ$] $A^{w} = \{A^{w,u}_a\}$ contains a matrix for each $u \in \F_q^m$ and $a \in \F_q$.
   107				For each $u$, $A^{w,u}$ is a projective measurement on~$\calH_{w}$.
   108	\item[$\circ$] $B^{w} = \{B^{w,\ell}_f\}$ contains a matrix for each axis-parallel line~$\ell$ in $\F_q^m$
   109				and univariate degree-$d$ polynomial $f:\ell\rightarrow \F_q$.
   110				For each $\ell$, $B^{w,\ell}$ is a projective measurement on~$\calH_{w}$.
   111	\item[$\circ$] $L^w = \{L^{w,\ell}_f\}$ contains a matrix for each line~$\ell$ in $\F_q^m$
   112				and univariate degree-$md$ polynomial $f:\ell\rightarrow \F_q$.
   113				For each $\ell$, $L^{w,\ell}$ is a projective measurement on~$\calH_{w}$.
   114	\end{itemize}
   115	\end{definition}

   117	\begin{remark}
   118	Throughout this work, we will only consider projective strategies.
   119	So we will henceforth use the terms ``strategy" and ``symmetric strategy'' to refer exclusively to projective strategies and symmetric, projective strategies, respectively.
   120	
   121	In addition, we will spend the vast majority of this work dealing solely with symmetric strategies, as they are notationally simpler to work with.
   122	Much of this work will focus on proving~\Cref{thm:main-induction},
   123	a variant of our main theorem for symmetric strategies.
   124	Our main theorem for general strategies, \Cref{thm:main-formal} below, will be proven in \Cref{sec:induction} by a standard reduction to the symmetric case.
   125	We will only see these more cumbersome-to-write general strategies
   126	in this section, where we state \Cref{thm:main-formal},
   127	and in \Cref{sec:induction}, where we carry out the reduction.
   128	\end{remark}

   130	\begin{definition}[Good strategy]
   131	A strategy is $(\eps, \delta, \gamma)$-good if it
   132	passes the axis-parallel lines test with probability at least $1-\eps$,
   133	the self consistency test with probability at least~$1-\delta$,
   134	and the diagonal lines test with probability at least~$1-\gamma$.
   135	\end{definition}
   136	
   137	\begin{remark}\label{rem:good-strat-characterization}
   138	Using notation which will be introduced in \Cref{sec:comparing-measurements} below,
   139	a symmetric strategy is $(\eps, \delta, \gamma)$-good
   140	if and only if it satisfies the following three conditions.
   141	For $\bell$ and $\bu$ as in the axis-parallel lines test,
   142	\begin{equation*}
   143	A^u_a \ot I \simeq_{\eps} I \ot B^{\ell}_{[f(u)=a]},
   144	\quad
   145	\text{and}
   146	\quad
   147	A^u_a \ot I \simeq_{\delta} I \ot A^u_a.
   148	\end{equation*}
   149	And for $\bell$ and $\bu$ as in the diagonal lines test,
   150	\begin{equation*}
   151	A^u_a \ot I \simeq_{\gamma} I \ot L^{\ell}_{[f(u)=a]}.
   152	\end{equation*}
   153	\end{remark}

     5	
     6	Diagonal-line geometry and rebasing operations.
     7	
     8	## References
     9	
    10	- `references/ldt-paper/test_definition.tex`
    11	- `blueprint/src/chapter/ch02_test.tex`
    12	-/
    13	
    14	namespace MIPStarRE.LDT
    15	
    16	/-- A genuinely affine diagonal line in `F_q^m`. -/
    17	structure DiagonalLine (params : Parameters) where
    18	  base : Point params
    19	  direction : Point params
    20	
    21	deriving instance DecidableEq, Inhabited for DiagonalLine
    22	
    23	namespace DiagonalLine
    24	
    25	/-- The canonical affine parameterization `t ↦ base + t · direction`. -/
    26	def pointAt {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    27	    (ℓ : DiagonalLine params) : Fq params → Point params :=
    28	  fun t => addPoint ℓ.base (smulPoint t ℓ.direction)
    29	
    30	/-- The support of the nonzero coordinates of a direction vector. -/
    31	noncomputable def nonzeroDirectionSupport {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    32	    (v : Point params) : Finset (Fin params.m) :=
    33	  Finset.univ.filter fun i => v i ≠ zeroCoord
    34	
    35	/-- The least nonzero coordinate of a direction vector, when one exists. -/
    36	noncomputable def firstNonzeroCoord? {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    37	    (v : Point params) : Option (Fin params.m) :=
    38	  open Classical in
    39	  let s := nonzeroDirectionSupport (params := params) v
    40	  if hs : s.Nonempty then some (s.min' hs) else none
    41	
    42	/-- Normalize a direction vector so its first nonzero coordinate becomes `1`. -/
    43	noncomputable def normalizeDirection {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    44	    (v : Point params) : Point params :=
    45	  open Classical in
    46	  match firstNonzeroCoord? (params := params) v with
    47	    | none => zeroPoint
    48	    | some i => smulPoint (invCoord (v i)) v
    49	
    50	/-- Canonical geometric diagonal line through `u` in direction `v`.
    51	
    52	For nonzero `v`, we normalize by the first nonzero coordinate and shift the
    53	base point so that this pivot coordinate is `0`. The degenerate `v = 0` case is
    54	kept as the singleton line through `u`. -/
    55	noncomputable def throughPointDirection {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    56	    (u v : Point params) : DiagonalLine params :=
    57	  open Classical in
    58	  match firstNonzeroCoord? (params := params) v with
    59	    | none => { base := u, direction := zeroPoint }
    60	    | some i =>
    61	        let w := normalizeDirection (params := params) v
    62	        let t := u i
    63	        { base := fun j => subCoord (u j) (mulCoord t (w j))
    64	          direction := w }
    65	
    66	/-- Affine parameter of the sampled point on the canonical diagonal line through
    67	`u` in direction `v`. -/
    68	noncomputable def sampleParameter {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    69	    (u v : Point params) : Fq params :=
    70	  open Classical in
    71	  match firstNonzeroCoord? (params := params) v with
    72	    | none => zeroCoord
    73	    | some i => u i
    74	
    75	@[simp] theorem throughPoint_pointAt_sampleParameter {params : Parameters}
    76	    [FieldModel params.q] (u : Point params) (i : Fin params.m) :
    77	    (AxisParallelLine.throughPoint (params := params) u i).pointAt
    78	        (AxisParallelLine.sampleParameter (params := params) u i) = u := by
    79	  funext j
    80	  by_cases h : j = i
    81	  · subst h
    82	    unfold AxisParallelLine.pointAt AxisParallelLine.throughPoint
    83	    simp [AxisParallelLine.sampleParameter, addCoord, zeroCoord]
    84	  · simp [AxisParallelLine.throughPoint, AxisParallelLine.pointAt, h]
    85	
    86	@[simp] theorem throughPointDirection_pointAt_sampleParameter {params : Parameters}
    87	    [FieldModel params.q] (u v : Point params) :
    88	    (DiagonalLine.throughPointDirection (params := params) u v).pointAt
    89	        (DiagonalLine.sampleParameter (params := params) u v) = u := by
    90	  classical
    91	  unfold DiagonalLine.throughPointDirection DiagonalLine.sampleParameter
    92	  split
    93	  · funext j
    94	    simp [DiagonalLine.pointAt, addPoint, smulPoint, zeroPoint,
    95	      zeroCoord, addCoord, mulCoord]
    96	  · rename_i i
    97	    funext j
    98	    simp [DiagonalLine.pointAt, addPoint, smulPoint, subCoord, addCoord, mulCoord]
    99	
   100	/-- Rebase a diagonal line so that the old point `ℓ.pointAt t` becomes the new base point. -/
   101	def rebaseAt {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
   102	    (ℓ : DiagonalLine params) (t : Fq params) : DiagonalLine params where
   103	  base := ℓ.pointAt t
   104	  direction := ℓ.direction
   105	
   106	@[simp] theorem rebaseAt_pointAt_zero {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
   107	    (ℓ : DiagonalLine params) (t : Fq params) :
   108	    (rebaseAt ℓ t).pointAt zeroCoord = ℓ.pointAt t := by
   109	  ext i
   110	  simp [rebaseAt, pointAt, addPoint, smulPoint, addCoord, mulCoord, zeroCoord]
   111	
   112	theorem rebaseAt_pointAt {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
   113	    (ℓ : DiagonalLine params) (t s : Fq params) :
   114	    (rebaseAt ℓ t).pointAt s = ℓ.pointAt (addCoord t s) := by
   115	  ext i
   116	  simp only [pointAt, addPoint, addCoord, rebaseAt, smulPoint, mulCoord, decode_encodeScalar]
   117	  rw [← encode_decodeScalar (ℓ.base i)]
   118	  congr 1
   119	  ring_nf
   120	
   121	@[simp] theorem rebaseAt_zero {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
   122	    (ℓ : DiagonalLine params) :
   123	    rebaseAt ℓ zeroCoord = ℓ := by
   124	  cases ℓ with
   125	  | mk base direction =>
   126	      change
   127	        ({ base :=
   128	             ({ base := base, direction := direction } : DiagonalLine params).pointAt zeroCoord,
   129	           direction := direction } : DiagonalLine params) =
   130	        ({ base := base, direction := direction } : DiagonalLine params)
   131	      congr
   132	      funext i
   133	      simp [pointAt, addPoint, smulPoint, addCoord, mulCoord, zeroCoord]
   134	
   135	theorem rebaseAt_rebase {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
   136	    (ℓ : DiagonalLine params) (t s : Fq params) :
   137	    rebaseAt (rebaseAt ℓ t) s = rebaseAt ℓ (addCoord t s) := by
   138	  cases ℓ with
   139	  | mk base direction =>
   140	      change
   141	        ({ base :=
   142	             (rebaseAt
   143	               ({ base := base, direction := direction } : DiagonalLine params) t).pointAt s,
   144	           direction := direction } : DiagonalLine params) =
   145	        ({ base :=
   146	             ({ base := base, direction := direction } : DiagonalLine params).pointAt
   147	               (addCoord t s),
   148	           direction := direction } : DiagonalLine params)
   149	      exact congrArg
   150	        (fun b => ({ base := b, direction := direction } : DiagonalLine params))
   151	        (rebaseAt_pointAt { base := base, direction := direction } t s)
   152	
   153	/-- Embed a diagonal line into the slice at height `x`, keeping the new coordinate fixed. -/
   154	def appendAtHeight (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]
   155	    (ℓ : DiagonalLine params) (x : Fq params) : DiagonalLine params.next where
   156	  base := appendPoint params ℓ.base x
   157	  direction := appendPoint params ℓ.direction zeroCoord
   158	
   159	@[simp] theorem appendAtHeight_rebaseAt {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
   160	    (ℓ : DiagonalLine params) (t x : Fq params) :
   161	    appendAtHeight params (rebaseAt ℓ t) x =
   162	      rebaseAt (appendAtHeight params ℓ x) t := by
   163	  cases ℓ with
   164	  | mk base direction =>
   165	      change
   166	        ({ base := appendPoint params (addPoint base (smulPoint t direction)) x,
   167	           direction := appendPoint params direction zeroCoord } : DiagonalLine params.next) =
   168	        ({ base := addPoint (appendPoint params base x)
   169	             (smulPoint t (appendPoint params direction zeroCoord)),
   170	           direction := appendPoint params direction zeroCoord } : DiagonalLine params.next)
   171	      congr
   172	      funext i
   173	      by_cases hi : i.1 < params.m
   174	      · simp only [appendPoint, addPoint, smulPoint, addCoord, mulCoord, hi, ↓reduceDIte]
   175	        rfl
   176	      · simp only [appendPoint, hi, ↓reduceDIte, addPoint, addCoord, smulPoint, mulCoord,
   177	          zeroCoord, decode_encodeScalar]
   178	        rw [← encode_decodeScalar x]
   179	        congr 1
   180	        calc
   181	          decodeScalar x = decodeScalar x + decodeScalar t * (0 : Scalar params) := by ring
   182	          _ = decodeScalar (encodeScalar (decodeScalar x)) +
   183	                decodeScalar t * decodeScalar (encodeScalar 0) := by
   184	              rw [show decodeScalar (encodeScalar (decodeScalar x)) = decodeScalar x from
   185	                  decode_encodeScalar (decodeScalar x),
   186	                show decodeScalar (encodeScalar (0 : Scalar params)) = (0 : Scalar params) from
   187	                  decode_encodeScalar (0 : Scalar params)]
   188	
   189	end DiagonalLine
   190	
   191	end MIPStarRE.LDT

     5	
     6	Polynomial answer types attached to axis-parallel and diagonal lines.
     7	
     8	## References
     9

    14	namespace MIPStarRE.LDT
    15	
    16	/-- A coded function has low individual degree when it is represented by an actual
    17	multivariate polynomial over the chosen field model whose degree in each variable is at
    18	most `d`. -/
    19	def HasLowIndividualDegree (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]
    20	    (g : Point params → Fq params) : Prop :=
    21	  ∃ p : PolynomialModel params,
    22	    (∀ i, MvPolynomial.degreeOf i p ≤ params.d) ∧
    23	      g = evalPolynomialModel params p
    24	
    25	/-- A coded univariate function has degree at most `bound` when it is represented by
    26	an actual polynomial over the chosen field model of degree at most `bound`. -/
    27	def HasUnivariateDegreeAtMost (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]
    28	    (bound : ℕ) (f : Fq params → Fq params) : Prop :=
    29	  ∃ p : LinePolynomialModel params,
    30	    p.natDegree ≤ bound ∧
    31	      f = evalLinePolynomialModel params p
    32	
    33	/-- Composing with the degree-one translation `C a + X` preserves `natDegree`
    34	bounds.  Shared degree bookkeeping for the `reparamAt` reparametrizations
    35	below. -/
    36	theorem natDegree_comp_C_add_X_le {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    37	    (p : LinePolynomialModel params) (a : Scalar params) {n : ℕ}
    38	    (hp : p.natDegree ≤ n) :
    39	    (p.comp (_root_.Polynomial.C a + _root_.Polynomial.X)).natDegree ≤ n :=
    40	  le_trans (_root_.Polynomial.natDegree_comp_le)
    41	    (by rw [add_comm, _root_.Polynomial.natDegree_X_add_C, Nat.mul_one]; exact hp)
    42	
    43	/-- Axis-parallel line answers are genuine univariate degree-`d` polynomials. -/
    44	structure AxisLinePolynomial (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q] where
    45	  poly : LinePolynomialModel params
    46	  degreeBounded : poly.natDegree ≤ params.d
    47	
    48	noncomputable instance {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q] :
    49	    Inhabited (AxisLinePolynomial params) :=
    50	  ⟨{ poly := 0
    51	     degreeBounded := _root_.Polynomial.natDegree_zero.trans_le (Nat.zero_le _) }⟩
    52	
    53	namespace AxisLinePolynomial
    54	
    55	/-- Evaluation of an axis-line answer on the line parameter. -/
    56	noncomputable def toFun {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    57	    (f : AxisLinePolynomial params) : Fq params → Fq params :=
    58	  evalLinePolynomialModel params f.poly
    59	
    60	noncomputable instance {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q] :
    61	    CoeFun (AxisLinePolynomial params) (fun _ => Fq params → Fq params) :=
    62	  ⟨AxisLinePolynomial.toFun⟩
    63	
    64	/-- A degree-zero axis-line answer is a constant univariate polynomial.
    65	
    66	Lean-only helper for the degree-zero branch of `thm:ld-pasting`; the source
    67	context is `references/ldt-paper/ld-pasting.tex:12-55`, where the boundary
    68	case `d = 0` must be handled without adding `0 < d` to the theorem. -/
    69	theorem eq_C_coeff_zero_of_degree_zero {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    70	    (f : AxisLinePolynomial params) (hd : params.d = 0) :
    71	    f.poly = _root_.Polynomial.C (f.poly.coeff 0) := by
    72	  exact _root_.Polynomial.eq_C_of_natDegree_eq_zero
    73	    (Nat.eq_zero_of_le_zero (f.degreeBounded.trans (by simp [hd])))
    74	
    75	/-- A degree-zero axis-line answer has the same value at all line parameters.
    76	
    77	Lean-only helper for the degree-zero branch of `thm:ld-pasting`; this is the
    78	vertical-line analogue of `Polynomial.apply_eq_apply_of_degree_zero`. -/
    79	theorem apply_eq_apply_of_degree_zero {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    80	    (f : AxisLinePolynomial params) (hd : params.d = 0) (t s : Fq params) :
    81	    f t = f s := by
    82	  unfold AxisLinePolynomial.toFun evalLinePolynomialModel
    83	  rw [eq_C_coeff_zero_of_degree_zero f hd]
    84	  simp
    85	
    86	@[ext] theorem ext {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    87	    {f g : AxisLinePolynomial params} (hpoly : f.poly = g.poly) : f = g := by
    88	  cases f with
    89	  | mk polyf hpolyf =>
    90	      cases g with
    91	      | mk polyg hpolyg =>
    92	          cases hpoly
    93	          congr

    95	/-- Reparametrize an axis-line answer by translating the line parameter. -/
    96	noncomputable def reparamAt {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    97	    (f : AxisLinePolynomial params) (t : Fq params) : AxisLinePolynomial params where
    98	  poly := f.poly.comp (_root_.Polynomial.C (decodeScalar t) + _root_.Polynomial.X)
    99	  degreeBounded := natDegree_comp_C_add_X_le f.poly (decodeScalar t) f.degreeBounded

   102	    (f : AxisLinePolynomial params) (t s : Fq params) :
   103	    reparamAt f t s = f (addCoord t s) := by

   127	theorem reparamAt_reparamAt {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
   128	    (f : AxisLinePolynomial params) (t s : Fq params) :
   129	    reparamAt (reparamAt f t) s = reparamAt f (addCoord t s) := by
   130	  refine AxisLinePolynomial.ext ?_
   131	  change
   132	    (f.poly.comp (_root_.Polynomial.C (decodeScalar t) + _root_.Polynomial.X)).comp
   133	        (_root_.Polynomial.C (decodeScalar s) + _root_.Polynomial.X) =
   134	      f.poly.comp (_root_.Polynomial.C (decodeScalar (addCoord t s)) + _root_.Polynomial.X)
   135	  rw [_root_.Polynomial.comp_assoc]
   136	  simp [addCoord, add_left_comm, add_comm]

   138	/-- Reparametrization by translation is an equivalence on axis-line answers. -/
   139	noncomputable def reparamAtEquiv {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
   140	    (t : Fq params) : AxisLinePolynomial params ≃ AxisLinePolynomial params where
   141	  toFun := fun f => reparamAt f t
   142	  invFun := fun f => reparamAt f (subCoord zeroCoord t)
   143	  left_inv := fun f => (reparamAt_reparamAt f t (subCoord zeroCoord t)).trans
   144	    ((congrArg (reparamAt f) (addCoord_subCoord_right zeroCoord t)).trans (reparamAt_zero f))
   145	  right_inv := fun f => (reparamAt_reparamAt f (subCoord zeroCoord t) t).trans
   146	    ((congrArg (reparamAt f) (addCoord_subCoord_left zeroCoord t)).trans (reparamAt_zero f))

   153	  funext t

   224	/-- Reparametrize a diagonal-line answer by translating the line parameter.
   225	
   226	Concretely, the underlying univariate polynomial `f.poly` (over `Scalar params` in
   227	the chosen field model) is precomposed with `X + C (decodeScalar t)`, i.e. the
   228	coefficients are shifted using genuine *field* addition on `Scalar params` — not
   229	the `Fin q` arithmetic on `Fq params`. Transporting back through `encodeScalar`
   230	gives the answer-level identity `reparamAt f t s = f (addCoord t s)` (see
   231	`reparamAt_apply`), where `addCoord` is field addition lifted through the coding
   232	`FieldModel.equiv`. Composition with a degree-one polynomial preserves the
   233	`natDegree ≤ params.m * params.d` bound.
   234	
   235	This is the answer-level geometric fact behind rebasing a diagonal line at
   236	parameter `t`: the old parameter `addCoord t s` becomes the new parameter `s`. -/
   237	noncomputable def reparamAt {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
   238	    (f : DiagonalLinePolynomial params) (t : Fq params) : DiagonalLinePolynomial params where
   239	  poly := f.poly.comp (_root_.Polynomial.C (decodeScalar t) + _root_.Polynomial.X)
   240	  degreeBounded := natDegree_comp_C_add_X_le f.poly (decodeScalar t) f.degreeBounded

   243	    (f : DiagonalLinePolynomial params) (t s : Fq params) :
   244	    reparamAt f t s = f (addCoord t s) := by
   245	  simp [reparamAt, DiagonalLinePolynomial.toFun, evalLinePolynomialModel, addCoord]

   248	    (f : DiagonalLinePolynomial params) (t : Fq params) :
   249	    reparamAt f t zeroCoord = f t := by
   250	  simp [reparamAt_apply, addCoord, zeroCoord]
   251	
   252	@[simp] theorem reparamAt_zero {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
   253	    (f : DiagonalLinePolynomial params) :
   254	    reparamAt f zeroCoord = f := by
   255	  refine DiagonalLinePolynomial.ext ?_
   256	  simp [reparamAt, zeroCoord]
   257	
   258	@[simp] theorem reparamAt_default {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
   259	    (t : Fq params) :
   260	    reparamAt (default : DiagonalLinePolynomial params) t = default := by
   261	  simpa [default, instInhabitedDiagonalLinePolynomial] using
   262	    (show
   263	      reparamAt ({ poly := 0, degreeBounded := by simp } : DiagonalLinePolynomial params) t =
   264	        ({ poly := 0, degreeBounded := by simp } : DiagonalLinePolynomial params) by
   265	        refine DiagonalLinePolynomial.ext ?_
   266	        simp [reparamAt])
   267	
   268	theorem reparamAt_reparamAt {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
   269	    (f : DiagonalLinePolynomial params) (t s : Fq params) :
   270	    reparamAt (reparamAt f t) s = reparamAt f (addCoord t s) := by
   271	  refine DiagonalLinePolynomial.ext ?_
   272	  change
   273	    (f.poly.comp (_root_.Polynomial.C (decodeScalar t) + _root_.Polynomial.X)).comp
   274	        (_root_.Polynomial.C (decodeScalar s) + _root_.Polynomial.X) =
   275	      f.poly.comp (_root_.Polynomial.C (decodeScalar (addCoord t s)) + _root_.Polynomial.X)
   276	  rw [_root_.Polynomial.comp_assoc]
   277	  simp [addCoord, add_left_comm, add_comm]
   278	
   279	/-- Reparametrization by translation is an equivalence on diagonal-line answers. -/
   280	noncomputable def reparamAtEquiv {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
   281	    (t : Fq params) : DiagonalLinePolynomial params ≃ DiagonalLinePolynomial params where
   282	  toFun := fun f => reparamAt f t
   283	  invFun := fun f => reparamAt f (subCoord zeroCoord t)
   284	  left_inv := fun f => (reparamAt_reparamAt f t (subCoord zeroCoord t)).trans
   285	    ((congrArg (reparamAt f) (addCoord_subCoord_right zeroCoord t)).trans (reparamAt_zero f))
   286	  right_inv := fun f => (reparamAt_reparamAt f (subCoord zeroCoord t) t).trans
   287	    ((congrArg (reparamAt f) (addCoord_subCoord_left zeroCoord t)).trans (reparamAt_zero f))
   288	
   289	/-- The stored polynomial really witnesses the advertised degree bound. -/
   290	theorem hasUnivariateDegreeAtMost {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
   291	    (f : DiagonalLinePolynomial params) :
   292	    HasUnivariateDegreeAtMost params (params.m * params.d) f := by
   293	  refine ⟨f.poly, f.degreeBounded, ?_⟩
   294	  funext t
   295	  rfl
   296	
   297	/-- Extend a diagonal-line answer to the slice at height `x`. -/
   298	def appendAtHeight (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]
   299	    (f : DiagonalLinePolynomial params) (_x : Fq params) : DiagonalLinePolynomial params.next where
   300	  poly := f.poly
   301	  degreeBounded := le_trans f.degreeBounded (Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ (Nat.le_succ _))
   302	
   303	/-- Slice extension commutes with translating the line parameter on diagonal-line answers. -/
   304	@[simp] theorem appendAtHeight_reparamAt {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
   305	    (f : DiagonalLinePolynomial params) (t x : Fq params) :
   306	    appendAtHeight params (reparamAt f t) x =
   307	      reparamAt (appendAtHeight params f x) t := by
   308	  apply DiagonalLinePolynomial.ext
   309	  rfl
   310	
   311	/-- The inverse reparametrization equivalence commutes with slice extension on
   312	diagonal-line answers. -/
   313	@[simp] theorem reparamAtEquiv_symm_appendAtHeight
   314	    {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
   315	    (f : DiagonalLinePolynomial params) (t x : Fq params) :
   316	    ((reparamAtEquiv (params := params.next) t).symm
   317	        (appendAtHeight params f x)) =
   318	      appendAtHeight params (((reparamAtEquiv (params := params) t).symm) f) x := by
   319	  apply DiagonalLinePolynomial.ext
   320	  rfl
   321	
   322	/-- Restrict a diagonal-line answer in `m + 1` variables to the slice at height `x`.
   323	This interface now makes the stronger slice-wise degree requirement explicit. -/
   324	def restrictAtHeight (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]
   325	    (f : DiagonalLinePolynomial params.next) (_x : Fq params)
   326	    (hdegree : f.poly.natDegree ≤ params.m * params.d) : DiagonalLinePolynomial params where
   327	  poly := f.poly
   328	  degreeBounded := hdegree
   329	
   330	end DiagonalLinePolynomial

   332	/-! ## Paper-level diagonal-line answers -/
   333	
   334	/-- Paper-level diagonal-line answers as functions on the line parameter.
   335	
   336	The existing `DiagonalLinePolynomial` alphabet records a degree bound on the
   337	univariate line polynomial.  For the slice restriction in
   338	`inductive_step.tex`, lines 436--455, the paper uses the underlying line
   339	function: restricting a slice-preserving ambient line is total at the function
   340	level, while it is not total on the current degree-bounded polynomial subtype. -/
   341	abbrev DiagonalLineAnswer (params : Parameters) := Fq params → Fq params
   342	
   343	namespace DiagonalLineAnswer
   344	
   345	/-- Reparametrize a paper-level diagonal-line answer by translating the line parameter. -/
   346	def reparamAt {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
   347	    (f : DiagonalLineAnswer params) (t : Fq params) : DiagonalLineAnswer params :=
   348	  fun s => f (addCoord t s)
   349	
   350	@[simp] theorem reparamAt_apply {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
   351	    (f : DiagonalLineAnswer params) (t s : Fq params) :
   352	    reparamAt f t s = f (addCoord t s) :=
   353	  rfl
   354	
   355	@[simp] theorem reparamAt_zero {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
   356	    (f : DiagonalLineAnswer params) :
   357	    reparamAt f zeroCoord = f := by
   358	  funext s
   359	  simp [reparamAt, addCoord, zeroCoord]

   474	
   475	This parallel structure is the target shape for the restriction redesign in
   476	Section 6: restricting an ambient diagonal line to a slice is total for function
   477	answers, unlike the current degree-bounded `DiagonalLinePolynomial` alphabet. -/
   478	structure AnswerSymStrat (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]
   479	    (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] where
   480	  state : QuantumState (ι × ι)
   481	  permInvState : PermInvState state
   482	  densityFixed : swapDensity state.density = state.density
   483	  isNormalized : state.IsNormalized
   484	  pointMeasurement : IdxProjMeas (Point params) (Fq params) ι
   485	  axisParallelMeasurement : AxisParallelCovariantMeasurement params ι

   488	/-- Paper-local symmetric strategy data.
   489	
   490	The line-measurement fields are bundled as transport-covariant wrappers:
   491	rebasing the question index is required to agree with transporting the
   492	projective measurement along the corresponding answer reparametrization
   493	equivalence. This is stronger than the older evaluation-level formulas
   494	at `zeroCoord`, but those formulas remain available as derived lemmas via
   495	`AxisParallelCovariantMeasurement.reparamInvariant` and
   496	`DiagonalCovariantMeasurement.reparamInvariant`.
   497	
   498	The `isNormalized` field records that the bipartite state's density
   499	operator has normalized trace `1`. For pure states, this coincides
   500	with the usual unit-vector condition (`⟨ψ|ψ⟩ = 1`) used in the paper.
   501	Bundling normalization with the strategy avoids threading a
   502	`state.IsNormalized` hypothesis through every downstream consumer
   503	(pasting cascade, `triangleSub` users, self-improvement helpers). -/
   504	structure SymStrat (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]
   505	    (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] where
   506	  state : QuantumState (ι × ι)  -- bipartite state on ℋ ⊗ ℋ
   507	  permInvState : PermInvState state
   508	  densityFixed : swapDensity state.density = state.density
   509	  isNormalized : state.IsNormalized
   510	  pointMeasurement : IdxProjMeas (Point params) (Fq params) ι
   511	  axisParallelMeasurement : AxisParallelCovariantMeasurement params ι
   512	  diagonalMeasurement : DiagonalCovariantMeasurement params ι
   513	
   514	-- NOTE: no global `Inhabited` instance for `SymStrat`; constructing default
   515	-- projective measurement families is non-canonical and requires additional
   516	-- assumptions on outcome types.
   517	
   518	/-- Encoded samples `(u, i)` for the axis-parallel lines test.
   519	The paper samples a random point `u ∈ F_q^m` and a coordinate
   520	`i ∈ {1, …, m}`. In Lean, `Fin params.m` represents the 0-indexed
   521	coordinates `{0, …, m - 1}`, corresponding to the paper's 1-indexed
   522	choice. The sample forms the axis-parallel line through `u` in that
   523	coordinate direction. -/
   524	abbrev AxisParallelTestSample (params : Parameters) :=
   525	  Point params × Fin params.m
   526	
   527	/-- Extend restricted direction coordinates to a full direction vector.
   528	For restriction index `j` (0-indexed), the first `j + 1` coordinates
   529	are the given free coordinates and the remaining are zero.
   530	This matches the paper's convention that `v` has its last `m − i`
   531	coordinates zero, where `i = j + 1`. -/
   532	def extendRestrictedDirection {params : Parameters}
   533	    [FieldModel params.q] (j : Fin params.m)
   534	    (freeCoords : Fin (j.val + 1) → Fq params) :
   535	    Point params :=
   536	  fun k =>
   537	    if h : k.val ≤ j.val then
   538	      freeCoords ⟨k.val, Nat.lt_succ_of_le h⟩
   539	    else zeroCoord

   541	/-- Encoded samples `(u, freeCoords)` for the `j`-restricted diagonal
   542	lines test. The base point `u ∈ F_q^m` and the free coordinates of
   543	the restricted direction (first `j + 1` coordinates; rest are zero).
   544	The full diagonal test averages over `j ∈ {0, …, m − 1}`. -/
   545	abbrev RestrictedDiagonalSample (params : Parameters)
   546	    (j : Fin params.m) :=
   547	  Point params × (Fin (j.val + 1) → Fq params)
   548	
   549	/-- The restricted diagonal sample space is nonempty. -/
   550	instance restrictedDiagonalSampleNonempty (params : Parameters) (j : Fin params.m) :
   551	    Nonempty (RestrictedDiagonalSample params j) :=
   552	  inferInstance

   555	point measurement. -/

   557	    {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]

   561	  fun s => (pointMeasurement s.1).toSubMeas
