Claude Code agents should also read\n`CLAUDE.md` for Claude-specific notes.\n\n## Project Overview\n\nThis repository is a Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization project for mathematics\naround $MIP^* = RE$. It is the **local-only continuation** of\n[LionSR/MIPStarRE](https://github.com/LionSR/MIPStarRE): the inherited track is\nthe **low individual degree test (LDT)** paper (arXiv:2009.12982); the active\ntrack is the **quantum Pauli basis test (QPBT)** from *MIP\\*=RE*\n(arXiv:2001.04383, primary) and *NEEXP in MIP\\** (arXiv:1904.05870, secondary).\n\nCI, review, and auto-fix **execute locally**; issues, PRs, their evidence and\nmerges live on GitHub (`Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A`), reached only through\n`local/bin/gh_common.py`. Read `local/README.md` and `local/DESIGN.md` before\ndoing workflow actions; the `## Local Operations` section below summarizes the\nrules.\n\nKey locations:\n\n- `references/qpbt-paper/` — per-section TeX mirror of MIP\\*=RE\n  (arXiv:2001.04383); the QPBT lives in\n  `08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex` and\n  `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex`\n- `references/neexp-paper/` — per-section TeX mirror of NEEXP in MIP\\*\n  (arXiv:1904.05870); secondary source\n  (`07_a_self_test_for_the_pauli_basis.tex`)\n- `references/ldt-paper/` — in-repo TeX source mirror for LDT\n- `blueprint/src/` — active LaTeX blueprint with Lean cross-references\n  (`\\lean{}`, `\\leanok`)\n- `MIPStarRE/` — Lean codebase matching the blueprint\n- `audits/` — dated audit reports, scouting notes, and repair plans\n- `local/`, `results/telemetry/` — the local workflow layer\n\nA legacy 2111 tensor track exists under `blueprint/legacy/` — do not modify it.\n\n**Canonical source hierarchy** (use in this order):\n\n1. `references/` paper mirrors — TeX source of the papers\n2. `blueprint/src/chapter/` — active LaTeX blueprint\n3. `MIPStarRE/` — Lean scaffold\n\nAlways read the paper source before formalizing or proving a statement. The\npaper contains the precise mathematical definitions, theorem statements, and\nproof strategies that the Lean code must faithfully represent. When stuck on a\nsorry site or proof, go back to the original paper TeX source — the answer is\nalmost always there. Do not guess or try random tactics without first\nunderstanding the paper's proof strategy.\n\n## Repository Layout\n\n```\nMIPStarRE/\n├── Quantum/               # Reusable matrix / measurement infrastructure\n│   ├── FiniteMatrix.lean  # Op d, normalizedTrace, tauNormSq, IsProj, ...\n│   └── Measurement.lean   # POVM, measurement types\n└── LDT/                   # Low individual degree test (13 submodules)\n    ├── Basic/             # Parameters, operators, distributions, submeasurements\n    ├── Test/              # Test definitions & main theorem\n    ├── Preliminaries/\n    ├── MakingMeasurementsProjective/\n    ├── MainInductionStep/\n    ├── ExpansionHypercubeGraph/\n    ├── GlobalVariance/\n    ├── SelfImprovement/\n    ├── CommutativityPoints/\n    ├── Commutativity/\n    └── Pasting/\n```\n\nEach LDT submodule typically has `Defs.lean` and `Theorems.lean`. Root imports\nflow: `MIPStarRE.lean` → `Quantum` + `LDT` → all submodules.\n\n## Quick Start — Build and Check Commands\n\nRun commands from the repository root unless noted otherwise.\n\n### First-time setup\n\n```bash\nlake exe cache get\nlake build\nscripts/install_git_hooks.sh\nscripts/install_git_hooks.sh --check\n```\n\nRun the hook check in every fresh worktree before preparing a PR.  The hooks\nmove fast statement-integrity, proof-debt, changed-file Lean, and blueprint-sync\nchecks to the local workflow so CI is not spent on preventable statement drift.\n\n### Full project build (CI-equivalent)\n\n```bash\nlake build\n```\n\n### Fast single-file type-check (default iteration loop)\n\n```bash\nlake env lean MIPStarRE/LDT/SelfImprovement/Defs.lean\n```\n\n### Check for proof holes in one file\n\n```bash\nrg -n \"sorry|axiom\" MIPStarRE/LDT/SelfImprovement/Defs.lean || true\n```\n\n### Check for proof holes in the whole project\n\n```bash\nrg -n \"sorry|axiom\" MIPStarRE\n```\n\n### Declaration checker\n\n```bash\nlake exe checkdecls blueprint/lean_decls\n```\n\nUse this when blueprint declaration lists need to match Lean declarations.\n\n### Blueprint build\n\n```bash\nleanblueprint pdf    # PDF output\nleanblueprint web    # HTML output (use as default for quick checks)\n```\n\nIn CI, blueprint linting effectively runs `leanblueprint web` from `blueprint/`.\n\n### What counts as a single test\n\nThis repository does not have a conventional unit-test suite. The closest\nsingle-test commands are:\n\n- **Lean work**: `lake env lean path/to/File.lean` and\n  `rg -n \"sorry|axiom\" path/to/File.lean || true`\n- **Blueprint work**: `leanblueprint web`\n- **Whole-repo verification**: `lake build` and\n  `lake exe checkdecls blueprint/lean_decls`\n\n### Recommended validation sequence\n\nFor a Lean file change:\n\n1. Type-check the edited file with `lake env lean ...`\n2. Scan that file for `sorry|axiom`\n3. If the change affects imports or shared declarations, run `lake build`\n\nFor blueprint changes:\n\n1. Run `leanblueprint web`\n2. If declaration links changed, run `lake exe checkdecls blueprint/lean_decls`\n\n## Toolchain\n\n- **Lean**: v4.31.0 (from `lean-toolchain`)\n- **Mathlib**: v4.31.0 (from `lakefile.toml`)\n\nImportant `lakefile.toml` options:\n\n- `relaxedAutoImplicit = false` — declare all variables explicitly\n- `pp.unicode.fun = true`\n- `weak.linter.mathlibStandardSet = true`\n- `maxSynthPendingDepth = 3`\n\n## Proof-Filling Order\n\nSections must be filled in this dependency order:\n\n1. Sections 3–4: test setup and preliminaries\n2. Section 5: making measurements projective\n3. Sections 7–8: expansion and global variance\n4. Section 9: self-improvement\n5. Sections 10–11: commutativity\n6. Section 12: pasting\n7. Section 6: main induction wrapper\n\nDo not start from the final theorem and guess intermediate facts.\n\n## Faithful Formalization Policy\n\nA declaration is a formalization of a paper theorem only when its public Lean\nstatement matches the cited paper statement, up to faithful formal encoding.\nChanging a Lean theorem away from the corresponding statement in\n`references/ldt-paper/` is strongly discouraged and should occur only when a\nfaithful formal encoding or a documented mathematical necessity requires it.\nThis applies to every declaration advertised as a formalization of a paper\nresult, not only to theorems currently undergoing repair.  The check is on the\nhypotheses as well as the conclusion.  A theorem whose\nconclusion has the right shape but whose assumptions include an extra\nload-bearing bridge input or hypotheses bundle is a conditional theorem, not\nthe paper theorem.\nThe project goal is to eliminate such conditional bridges, not to normalize\nthem as permanent infrastructure.\n\nIf the only available Lean theorem has extra assumptions, the blueprint must\nnot mark the source-labelled paper entry as matched by that theorem.  Either\nleave the source-labelled entry without `\\leanok`, or state the restricted or\nconditional result as a separate Lean-only blueprint entry whose hypotheses are\ndisplayed explicitly.  A scope-restricted theorem may be marked `\\leanok` only\nagainst a blueprint statement that explicitly states the restriction; it must\nnot be presented as the unrestricted source theorem.\n\nWhen a stricter-hypothesis Lean theorem is the only available version near a\nsource theorem, the discrepancy must have a paper-gap note or tracking issue.\nThe note should identify the missing hypothesis, explain why it is not part of\nthe cited statement, and state the plan for eliminating the restriction,\nderiving it internally, or moving the result out of the source-labelled route.\n\nThis rule applies especially to declarations named after paper labels such as\n`mainFormal`, `selfImprovement`, `mainInduction`, or other theorem names linked\nfrom the blueprint by `\\lean{...}` and `\\leanok`.\n\nBefore editing any theorem tagged with a paper label (`thm:*`, `lem:*`,\n`prop:*`):\n\n1. Read the corresponding statement in `references/ldt-paper/`.\n2. Preserve the public Lean theorem statement, except for hypotheses that are\n   genuinely part of the faithful encoding of the paper's domain.\n3. Do not add bridge inputs, residual packages, repair hypotheses, producer\n   assumptions, generic hypotheses or assumptions bundles, or arbitrary\n   implication hypotheses to the paper theorem.\n4. If a missing intermediate fact is needed, first state that fact as a named\n   lemma or theorem to be proved from the paper hypotheses.\n5. Do not add a conditional helper merely to keep a file compiling.  A\n   conditional helper may remain temporarily only when the proof content it\n   preserves is mathematically useful, the source-faithful theorem remains\n   visible, and the helper has a paper-gap note, a named construction theorem\n   or proof-obligation target, and an explicit discharge or deletion plan.  Its\n   name must show that it is conditional without making the assumption look like\n   an acceptable source hypothesis, for example\n   `mainFormal_ofInternalObligations`, `selfImprovementFromObligations`, or a\n   name ending in `_ofObligations`.\n6. Do not point a source-labelled blueprint theorem to the conditional helper\n   with `\\leanok`.\n\nWhen reviewing an existing bridge, residual, repair, producer, or package\nhypothesis, first try to recover any genuine proof content from its construction\nand turn that content into a source-faithful lemma.  If the bridge does not\nactually follow from the paper hypotheses, do not preserve the paper theorem as\na strengthened statement.  Restore the paper-aligned theorem statement and leave\nthe missing proof obligation explicit, even if that means reintroducing a\ntracked `sorry` during a repair PR.\n\nSome side conditions are not deviations: positivity needed to define a\ndivision, nonemptiness of a finite type, decidability instances, field-model\ninstances, and similar boundary hypotheses may be faithful encodings of\nassumptions that the paper leaves implicit.  These should still be reviewed and\ndocumented if they are mathematically load-bearing.  The forbidden pattern is\ndifferent: moving an unproved step of the proof into the theorem statement, such\nas a `BridgeHypotheses`, `Input`, `Residual`, `Package`, `RepairInput`,\n`Producer`, generic `Hypotheses`, or generic `Assumptions` assumption that the\npaper theorem does not assume.  These assumptions\nshould not be introduced merely to keep a file compiling or to avoid a `sorry`;\nthey require explicit mathematical justification and a planned discharge.\n\nFor the current LDT final theorem, `mainFormal` is reserved for the statement of\n`\\Cref{thm:main-formal}`: from a projective strategy passing the low individual\ndegree test, it produces the three final consistency conclusions.  A theorem\nwith an extra hypothesis such as\n`hbaseBridge : ... → MainFormalRepairedBridgeHypotheses ...` is temporary\nscaffolding at best; it must not be the declaration advertised as\n`thm:main-formal`.  The corresponding paper-aligned version should remain\nvisible, even if its proof is temporarily unfinished during repair.\n\nEvery agent changing a paper-labelled theorem must finish with a statement\nintegrity audit:\n\n- paper assumptions;\n- Lean assumptions;\n- paper conclusion;\n- Lean conclusion;\n- verdict: exact, faithful boundary hypotheses, extra assumptions, weakened\n  conclusion, or strengthened conclusion.\n\n### Paper-realignment mode\n\nWhen a theorem, definition, or hypothesis field has already drifted away from\n`references/ldt-paper/`, a repair PR may temporarily reintroduce `sorry` in\norder to restore the source-faithful statement.  In this mode, statement\nfaithfulness is the first invariant: keeping a divergent proof intact merely to\navoid `sorry` preserves a theorem that the paper does not state.\n\nPaper-realignment mode is narrow.  It applies only to edits whose purpose is to\nremove wrong hypotheses, delete divergent fields, restore a paper theorem\nstatement, or replace a conditional theorem by a paper-facing statement plus a\nnamed proof obligation.  Such a PR must:\n\n1. cite the paper passage by label or line range in the relevant docstring;\n2. cite the paper-gap note or tracking issue that records the divergence;\n3. identify every introduced or retained `sorry` and the construction theorem,\n   proof-obligation theorem, or source-faithful lemma expected to discharge it;\n4. avoid unrelated refactors, notation changes, or proof-engineering churn.\n\nDuring paper realignment, every restated definition, hypothesis field, or\npaper-facing theorem must have a docstring that lets a reviewer tell whether\nthe statement is present in the paper or is a Lean-only proof obligation.  A\nname such as `Bridge`, `Residual`, `Repair`, `Package`, `Input`, or `Producer`\nis not by itself a mathematical source citation.\n\n### Unfaithful dependency markers\n\nA theorem or lemma is **unfaithful** when its proof relies on a hypothesis,\nhelper, bridge, residual, repair input, or conditional theorem that is known not\nto follow from the cited paper statement.  This includes the case where the\npublic theorem statement is source-shaped but the proof calls a conditional\nhelper whose load-bearing hypothesis is not yet derived from the paper\nhypotheses.\n\nSuch a declaration must carry a docstring section beginning with\n`**Unfaithful:**`.  The marker must name the load-bearing deviation, cite the\npaper-gap note or issue that documents it, and state the planned discharge.  A\nminimal form is:\n\n```text\n**Unfaithful:** This proof currently relies on `<hypothesis or helper>`,\nwhich is not derived from `<paper label or line range>`.  Documented in\n`docs/paper-gaps/<note>.tex` or issue `#N`.  Elimination: prove\n`<construction theorem>` from the paper hypotheses.\n```\n\nThe marker propagates through dependencies: a theorem whose proof transitively\nuses an unfaithful declaration is itself unfaithful until the dependency is\nreplaced by a source-faithful proof.  Remove the marker only when the cited\ndeviation has been discharged.\n\nNot every discrepancy requires the full `**Unfaithful:**` marker.  If the paper\nhas a local typo, a documented numerical strengthening, or a genuine scope\nrestriction, use a lighter docstring marker such as `**Local fix:**` or\n`**Scope restriction:**`, citing the relevant paper-gap note.  These lighter\nmarkers are for mathematically correct local corrections; `**Unfaithful:**` is\nreserved for load-bearing assumptions or proof steps still missing from the\npaper hypotheses.\n\n## Code Conventions\n\n### Imports\n\n- Keep imports at the top of the file\n- One import per line\n- Follow existing local import style\n- Prefer the smallest correct import set, but do not churn imports unnecessarily\n- Preserve re-export-file structure: `MIPStarRE.lean`, `MIPStarRE/LDT.lean`\n- Before adding a new import, check whether the needed declaration already\n  comes from an existing local re-export import\n\n### File structure\n\nEvery `.lean` file must have:\n\n1. imports\n2. a module docstring starting with `/-!` (title, main definitions, references)\n3. namespace / opens / variables\n4. declarations\n\n### Formatting\n\n- **Line length**: max 100 characters\n- **Spacing**: spaces around `:` and `:=`\n- **`by` placement**: at end of the preceding line (`... := by`), never on its\n  own line\n- **Indentation**: 2 spaces for proof body; 4 spaces for continuation of\n  theorem statement\n- **Top-level commands**: flush-left\n- Avoid orphaned parentheses. Prefer readable multiline formatting over dense\n  tactic blocks.\n\n### Naming conventions\n\nFollow Mathlib naming plus project-local conventions:\n\n- Theorems / proofs / proposition-valued terms: `snake_case`\n- Structures / inductives / classes / Prop names / Type names: `UpperCamelCase`\n- Functions / non-Prop terms: `lowerCamelCase`\n- Use American English spelling in declaration names\n\nProject-preferred variable names:\n\n- `q` — alphabet size / finite field order\n- `n`, `m` — dimensions\n- `σ` — strategies\n- `P` — projective measurements\n- `G` — graphs (hypercube expansion)\n\nFor full details, see the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_naming` and `MATHLIB_style` references.\n\n### Types and signatures\n\n- Give explicit types for declaration arguments\n- Give explicit return types for definitions\n- Do not rely on auto-implicit variables (forbidden by `relaxedAutoImplicit`)\n- Prefer existing project structures and Mathlib-compatible types over ad hoc\n  wrappers\n- Be skeptical of scaffolding that compiles but cannot support real proofs later\n\n### Documentation\n\nRequired:\n\n- **Module docstrings** for every file — `/-! # Title ... ## References ... -/`\n- **Docstrings** on every `def`, `structure`, `class`, and significant `theorem`\n- Mathematical prose in Lean docstrings and comments should follow\n  `docs/mathematical_language.md`\n\nWhen formalizing a statement from the blueprint, add corresponding `\\lean{...}`\nand `\\leanok` tags in the relevant `blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex` file.\n\n## Proof Engineering\n\n### Search before proving\n\n- Prefer existing Mathlib lemmas\n- Reuse local API from `Quantum/` and `LDT/Basic/`\n- Use file-local helper lemmas only when they genuinely reduce duplication\n- Scout Mathlib first: `exact?`, `apply?`, `#find?`, grep Mathlib source\n- See `audits/` for chapter-by-chapter Mathlib dependency analysis\n\n### Mathlib integration\n\nThe project depends heavily on Mathlib for finite-dimensional complex matrices,\nHermitian/PSD operators, and spectral theory. When proving lemmas:\n\n- Reuse existing Mathlib lemmas rather than reproving\n- Prefer Mathlib types over custom definitions\n- Do not re-declare standard Mathlib lemmas (e.g., custom matrix transpose\n  lemmas when `Matrix.transpose_*` exists)\n\nFor a pedagogical register of external lemmas not explained in the paper,\nsee `docs/external-lemmas-pedagogy.md`. This includes Schwartz–Zippel,\nFourier orthogonality, Cauchy–Schwarz for approximate measurements, CFC,\nand external result statements (Polishchuk–Spielman, Raz–Safra).\n\nFor the policy on temporary conditional scaffolding and blueprint\nsynchronization, see `docs/formalization-patterns.md`.\n\n### Validation ladder\n\n1. `lake env lean path/to/File.lean`\n2. `lake build`\n\nDo not jump straight to full builds for every small edit.\n\n### Lean-specific advice\n\n- Prefer small, composable lemmas over giant fragile proofs\n- Reuse `SubMeas`, `Measurement`, tensor-placement, PSD, and trace lemmas\n  already in the repo\n- Check `docs/api_surface.md` for useful obligation-closing lemmas\n- If changing statements, confirm against paper and blueprint first\n- Never add axioms or weaken statements without explicit justification\n\n## Mathematical Documentation Style\n\nWrite repository prose for mathematicians and mathematical physicists. Prefer a\nclear, precise, and unhurried expository style: introduce the object under\ndiscussion, state the mathematical relation being used, distinguish hypotheses\nfrom conclusions, and avoid informal process language when a standard\nmathematical phrase is available.\n\nWhen writing docstrings, audit notes, PR descriptions, or blueprint-adjacent\ncomments, use terminology from the standard mathematical literature, the LDT\npaper, and the local formalization. Do not invent slang or private shorthand for\nmathematical objects. The goal is prose that a third-party reader can understand\nwithout having read the agent conversation that produced the change.\n\n### Paper-gap notes\n\nFor the proof-gap terminology used to distinguish source theorems, internal\nproof obligations, and conditional helpers, follow\n`docs/paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex`.  For documentation of discrepancies\nbetween the cited paper, the blueprint, and Lean, follow\n`docs/paper-gaps/policy.tex`. In particular, such notes should be\nmathematical prose for mathematicians and mathematical physicists who have not\nread the issue discussion: introduce notation, state the cited assertion,\nisolate the calculation or logical obstruction, compare with the blueprint and\nLean statement, and give a clear verdict. If Lean uses a Mathlib result or\nconstruction not present in the cited argument, explain that replacement\npedagogically before naming the formal declaration. If the cited assertion is\nfalse and a counterexample is available, explain the counterexample in prose and\nuse any Lean declaration only as verification.\n\n## Proof Integrity\n\n### Blockers (must be resolved before merge)\n\nSee the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and `docs/project_conventions.md` for the full catalog.\n\n**Direct proof holes**: `sorry`, `admit`\n\n**Kernel / type system bypasses**: `native_decide`, `unsafeCast`, `unsafeCoerce`,\n`lcProof`, `ofReduceBool`, `ofReduceNat`\n\n**Axiom smuggling**: unjustified `axiom` declarations\n\n**Circular reasoning**: proofs that assume the statement being proved as a local\nhypothesis, or helper lemmas that essentially restate the main goal.\n\n**Castle-in-the-air (ungrounded proofs)**: custom re-declarations of standard\nMathlib lemmas; `axiom` or `sorry`-based helpers for facts already in Mathlib;\nchains of custom lemmas that never bottom out in Mathlib or Lean core.\n\n**Scaffolding that blocks real formalization**: definitions or theorem statements\nthat do not faithfully represent the actual mathematics, making them impossible\nto connect to real Mathlib-based proofs. Ask: *Can a real proof be built on top\nof this?*\n\n### Warnings\n\nPlaceholder tactics (`exact?`, `apply?`, `library_search`) should be replaced\nwith concrete results. Debug artifacts (`dbg_trace`, `#check`, `#eval`,\n`#print`) should be removed from proof files. See the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference for\nthe full warning catalog.\n\n### Anti-patterns\n\nSubtler proof-evasion patterns that pass kernel-level checks yet still fail to\nprove the claimed mathematics are catalogued in `docs/anti_patterns.md`:\nconclusion-shaped hypotheses, definitional sleight-of-hand, zero-fallback\nbranches, trivial default witnesses, Mathlib-bypass castles, and external\n`*Statement` smuggles. Reviewers should consult this file alongside\nthe lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and `docs/project_conventions.md`.\n\n## PR and Commit Conventions\n\nPRs are GitHub pull requests (opened by `local/bin/pr_open.py`, merged by\n`local/bin/pr_merge.py`); `#N` in PR bodies and commit messages is the GitHub\nissue number. Titles, bodies, and commit rules below are unchanged from the\nparent project.\n\n### PR title format\n\n```\ntype(scope): short description\n```\n\n| Type       | When to use                                      |\n|------------|--------------------------------------------------|\n| `feat`     | New definition, lemma, theorem, or module         |\n| `fix`      | Bug fix (broken proof, wrong identifier, etc.)    |\n| `refactor` | Restructuring without changing API surface        |\n| `docs`     | Documentation or blueprint changes only           |\n| `style`    | Formatting, naming, or docstring cleanup only     |\n| `ci`       | CI/CD workflow changes                            |\n| `chore`    | Dependency bumps, linting, toolchain updates      |\n\n**Scope** is a shortened module path: `LDT/SelfImprovement`, `Quantum`,\n`blueprint`, etc. Omit the `MIPStarRE/` prefix.\n\n### PR body template\n\nEvery PR body must contain three sections:\n\n```markdown\n### Motivation\n- Why this change is needed. Cite the issue and paper/blueprint location.\n\n### Description\n- State precisely what changed.\n\n### Testing\n- What was verified and how (e.g., `lake build`, `rg -n \"sorry|axiom\"`).\n\n---\nAddresses #N\n```\n\nUse `Addresses #N` (keeps the issue open) or `Closes #N` (auto-closes on merge).\n\n### Commit messages\n\n- **Imperative mood** in the subject line (\"Add\", not \"Added\")\n- Subject under 72 characters\n- When squash-merging, the commit message should match the PR title format\n\n## Review Process\n\nEvery PR touching Lean code is reviewed by a dedicated local reviewer session\n(`local/bin/review.sh`, dispatched after green local CI; a session never\nreviews its own diff) against these criteria:\n\n1. **Proof correctness** — No unexplained `sorry`. No `axiom` unless discussed.\n2. **Mathlib style** — Follow the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_naming` and `MATHLIB_doc` references.\n3. **Paper terminology** — Public Lean names and documentation should use\n   terminology from the paper and blueprint. See `docs/mathematical_language.md`.\n4. **Linter hygiene** — Fix warnings, don't mask them with broad\n   `set_option linter.<name> false` blocks.\n5. **Type safety** — No universe mismatches, coercion problems.\n6. **Performance** — Avoid expensive tactics on large types.\n7. **Modularity** — Are new lemmas general enough to be reused?\n8. **Documentation** — Every new `def` and major `theorem` must have a docstring.\n9. **Blueprint sync and paper origin** — Add `\\lean{}` and `\\leanok` tags for\n   formalized statements only when the Lean statement matches the source.\n   Record formalization-only auxiliary lemmas explicitly.\n10. **Scaffolding integrity** — Verify scaffolding aligns with Mathlib.\n11. **Statement drift** — Compare source-labelled theorem statements with the\n   paper and flag new hypotheses, weakened conclusions, changed quantifier\n   order, altered error parameters, or bridge/residual packages moving toward\n   a paper theorem.\n12. **Proof-evasion anti-patterns** — Review against `docs/anti_patterns.md`.\n\nFor full details, see `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` and the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_pr-review` reference.\n\n## Blueprint and Documentation Work\n\nIf modifying blueprint material:\n\n- Keep chapter structure under `blueprint/src/chapter/`\n- Ensure `leanblueprint web` succeeds\n- Keep Lean declaration references valid\n- Sync theorem labels with Lean names\n- Add `\\lean{LeanDeclName}` and `\\leanok` tags for formalized statements\n\nFor blueprint style conventions, see `docs/blueprint_style_guide.md`.\n\nFor temporary conditional scaffolding and the `\\lean{}`/`\\leanok` tagging\nstrategy, see `docs/formalization-patterns.md`.\n\n## Agent Rule Sources\n\nChecked in this repository snapshot:\n\n- No `.cursorrules`\n- No     53	/--

    83	/--
    84	The tensor-product strategy of `def:tensor-product-strategy` in

    88	structure Strategy (G : Game) where
    89	  ιA : Type
    90	  ιB : Type
    91	  [ιAFintype : Fintype ιA]
    92	  [ιBFintype : Fintype ιB]
    93	  [ιADecidableEq : DecidableEq ιA]
    94	  [ιBDecidableEq : DecidableEq ιB]
    95	  ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)
    96	  ψ_norm : ‖ψ‖ = 1
    97	  A : G.QuestionA → Measurement G.AnswerA ιA
    98	  B : G.QuestionB → Measurement G.AnswerB ιB
    99	
   100	attribute [instance] Strategy.ιAFintype Strategy.ιBFintype
   101	  Strategy.ιADecidableEq Strategy.ιBDecidableEq
   102	
   103	/-- The rectangular tensor placement used in strategy probabilities.  This is
   104	the finite-matrix realization of `def:tensor-product-strategy`, blueprint
   105	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:61-69`; paper origin
   106	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.
   107	-/
   108	def heteroKron {ιA ιB : Type*} (A : Op ιA) (B : Op ιB) : Op (ιA × ιB) :=
   109	  Matrix.kronecker A B
   110	
   111	/- The Euclidean linear map is the shared action used by the value and distance
   112	functionals.  Keeping it at the Euclidean-space level avoids accidentally
   113	using the function-space supremum norm of `Matrix.mulVec`. -/
   114	/-- Apply a finite matrix to a Euclidean-space state.  This is the Hilbert-space
   115	action underlying `def:tensor-product-value`, paper
   116	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`. -/
   117	noncomputable def applyOperatorToState {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   118	    (M : Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι :=
   119	  Matrix.toEuclideanLin M ψ
   120	
   121	/-- The Born weight of an answer pair for a strategy.  Lean-only support for
   122	`def:tensor-product-value`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, paper
   123	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:40-48`. -/
   124	noncomputable def outcomeWeight {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   125	    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB) (a : G.AnswerA) (b : G.AnswerB) : ℝ :=
   126	  let M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=
   127	    heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b)
   128	  let acted := applyOperatorToState M S.ψ
   129	  (inner ℂ S.ψ acted).re
   130	
   131	/-- Alice's marginal Born weight for an answer at a fixed question. -/
   132	noncomputable def aliceOutcomeWeight {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   133	    (x : G.QuestionA) (a : G.AnswerA) : ℝ :=
   134	  let M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=
   135	    heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) 1
   136	  (inner ℂ S.ψ (applyOperatorToState M S.ψ)).re
   137	
   138	/-- Bob's marginal Born weight for an answer at a fixed question. -/
   139	noncomputable def bobOutcomeWeight {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   140	    (y : G.QuestionB) (b : G.AnswerB) : ℝ :=
   141	  let M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=
   142	    heteroKron 1 ((S.B y).effect b)
   143	  (inner ℂ S.ψ (applyOperatorToState M S.ψ)).re
   144	
   145	/-- The Born weight of a decidable event on the two answers at fixed questions. -/
   146	noncomputable def outcomeEventWeight {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   147	    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB)
   148	    (E : G.AnswerA → G.AnswerB → Prop) [DecidableRel E] : ℝ :=
   149	  ∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB,
   150	    if E a b then outcomeWeight S x y a b else 0
   151	
   152	/-- The marginal Born weight of a decidable event on Alice's answer. -/
   153	noncomputable def aliceEventWeight {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   154	    (x : G.QuestionA) (E : G.AnswerA → Prop) [DecidablePred E] : ℝ :=
   155	  ∑ a : G.AnswerA, if E a then aliceOutcomeWeight S x a else 0
   156	
   157	/-- The marginal Born weight of a decidable event on Bob's answer. -/
   158	noncomputable def bobEventWeight {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   159	    (y : G.QuestionB) (E : G.AnswerB → Prop) [DecidablePred E] : ℝ :=
   160	  ∑ b : G.AnswerB, if E b then bobOutcomeWeight S y b else 0
   161	
   162	/-- Every answer-pair Born weight is nonnegative.  This is formalization-only
   163	support for the probability expression in `def:tensor-product-value`. -/
   164	theorem outcomeWeight_nonneg {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   165	    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB) (a : G.AnswerA) (b : G.AnswerB) :
   166	    0 ≤ outcomeWeight S x y a b := by
   167	  unfold outcomeWeight applyOperatorToState heteroKron
   168	  exact
   169	    (Matrix.isPositive_toEuclideanLin_iff.mpr
   170	      (Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mp
   171	        (kronecker_nonneg ((S.A x).pos a) ((S.B y).pos b)))).re_inner_nonneg_right S.ψ
   172	
   173	/-- The Born weights of all answer pairs at fixed questions sum to one.  This
   174	is formalization-only support for the POVM normalization implicit in
   175	`def:tensor-product-value`. -/
   176	theorem outcomeWeight_sum_eq_one {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   177	    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB) :
   178	    ∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB, outcomeWeight S x y a b = 1 := by
   179	  have hsum :
   180	      (∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB,
   181	        heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b)) =
   182	          (1 : Op (S.ιA × S.ιB)) := by
   183	    ext i j
   184	    simp only [Matrix.sum_apply, heteroKron, Matrix.kronecker,
   185	      Matrix.kroneckerMap_apply]
   186	    simp_rw [← Finset.mul_sum, ← Finset.sum_mul]
   187	    rw [show (∑ a : G.AnswerA, (S.A x).effect a i.1 j.1) =
   188	        (1 : Op S.ιA) i.1 j.1 by
   189	      simpa only [Matrix.sum_apply] using congrFun (congrFun (S.A x).sum_eq_one i.1) j.1]
   190	    rw [show (∑ b : G.AnswerB, (S.B y).effect b i.2 j.2) =
   191	        (1 : Op S.ιB) i.2 j.2 by
   192	      simpa only [Matrix.sum_apply] using congrFun (congrFun (S.B y).sum_eq_one i.2) j.2]
   193	    exact congrFun (congrFun
   194	      (Matrix.one_kronecker_one (m := S.ιA) (n := S.ιB) (α := ℂ)) i) j
   195	  calc
   196	    ∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB, outcomeWeight S x y a b =
   197	        (inner ℂ S.ψ
   198	          (applyOperatorToState
   199	            (∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB,
   200	              heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b)) S.ψ)).re := by
   201	          simp [outcomeWeight, applyOperatorToState]
   202	    _ = (inner ℂ S.ψ (applyOperatorToState 1 S.ψ)).re := by rw [hsum]
   203	    _ = 1 := by
   204	      simp [applyOperatorToState, S.ψ_norm]

   206	/-- Summing over Bob's answers gives Alice's marginal Born weight. -/
   207	theorem sum_outcome_weight_right {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   208	    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB) (a : G.AnswerA) :
   209	    (∑ b : G.AnswerB, outcomeWeight S x y a b) = aliceOutcomeWeight S x a := by
   210	  have hsum :
   211	      (∑ b : G.AnswerB, heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b)) =
   212	        heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) 1 := by
   213	    ext i j
   214	    simp only [Matrix.sum_apply, heteroKron, Matrix.kronecker,
   215	      Matrix.kroneckerMap_apply]
   216	    rw [← Finset.mul_sum]
   217	    rw [show (∑ b : G.AnswerB, (S.B y).effect b i.2 j.2) =
   218	        (1 : Op S.ιB) i.2 j.2 by
   219	      simpa only [Matrix.sum_apply] using congrFun (congrFun (S.B y).sum_eq_one i.2) j.2]
   220	  calc
   221	    (∑ b : G.AnswerB, outcomeWeight S x y a b) =
   222	        (inner ℂ S.ψ
   223	          (applyOperatorToState
   224	            (∑ b : G.AnswerB,
   225	              heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b)) S.ψ)).re := by
   226	          simp [outcomeWeight, applyOperatorToState]
   227	    _ = (inner ℂ S.ψ
   228	        (applyOperatorToState (heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) 1) S.ψ)).re := by
   229	      rw [hsum]
   230	    _ = aliceOutcomeWeight S x a := rfl
   231	
   232	/-- Summing over Alice's answers gives Bob's marginal Born weight. -/
   233	theorem sum_outcome_weight_left {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   234	    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB) (b : G.AnswerB) :
   235	    (∑ a : G.AnswerA, outcomeWeight S x y a b) = bobOutcomeWeight S y b := by
   236	  have hsum :
   237	      (∑ a : G.AnswerA, heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b)) =
   238	        heteroKron 1 ((S.B y).effect b) := by
   239	    ext i j
   240	    simp only [Matrix.sum_apply, heteroKron, Matrix.kronecker,
   241	      Matrix.kroneckerMap_apply]
   242	    rw [← Finset.sum_mul]
   243	    rw [show (∑ a : G.AnswerA, (S.A x).effect a i.1 j.1) =
   244	        (1 : Op S.ιA) i.1 j.1 by
   245	      simpa only [Matrix.sum_apply] using congrFun (congrFun (S.A x).sum_eq_one i.1) j.1]
   246	  calc
   247	    (∑ a : G.AnswerA, outcomeWeight S x y a b) =
   248	        (inner ℂ S.ψ
   249	          (applyOperatorToState
   250	            (∑ a : G.AnswerA,
   251	              heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b)) S.ψ)).re := by
   252	          simp [outcomeWeight, applyOperatorToState]
   253	    _ = (inner ℂ S.ψ
   254	        (applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 ((S.B y).effect b)) S.ψ)).re := by
   255	      rw [hsum]
   256	    _ = bobOutcomeWeight S y b := rfl

   258	/-- Every answer event has nonnegative Born weight. -/
   259	theorem outcome_event_weight_nonneg {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   260	    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB)
   261	    (E : G.AnswerA → G.AnswerB → Prop) [DecidableRel E] :
   262	    0 ≤ outcomeEventWeight S x y E := by
   263	  unfold outcomeEventWeight
   264	  exact Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => Finset.sum_nonneg fun b _ => by
   265	    split_ifs
   266	    · exact outcomeWeight_nonneg S x y a b
   267	    · exact le_rfl
   268	
   269	/-- An answer event depending only on Alice has its Alice marginal weight. -/
   270	theorem outcome_event_weight_left_eq {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   271	    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB)
   272	    (E : G.AnswerA → Prop) [DecidablePred E] :
   273	    outcomeEventWeight S x y (fun a _ => E a) = aliceEventWeight S x E := by
   274	  unfold outcomeEventWeight aliceEventWeight
   275	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   276	  intro a _
   277	  by_cases ha : E a
   278	  · simp [ha, sum_outcome_weight_right S x y a]
   279	  · simp [ha]
   280	
   281	/-- An answer event depending only on Bob has its Bob marginal weight. -/
   282	theorem outcome_event_weight_right_eq {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   283	    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB)
   284	    (E : G.AnswerB → Prop) [DecidablePred E] :
   285	    outcomeEventWeight S x y (fun _ b => E b) = bobEventWeight S y E := by
   286	  unfold outcomeEventWeight bobEventWeight
   287	  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   288	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   289	  intro b _
   290	  by_cases hb : E b
   291	  · simp [hb, sum_outcome_weight_left S x y b]
   292	  · simp [hb]
   293	
   294	/-- Inclusion of answer events implies the corresponding Born-weight inequality. -/
   295	theorem outcome_event_weight_mono {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   296	    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB)
   297	    (E F : G.AnswerA → G.AnswerB → Prop) [DecidableRel E] [DecidableRel F]
   298	    (hEF : ∀ a b, E a b → F a b) :
   299	    outcomeEventWeight S x y E ≤ outcomeEventWeight S x y F := by
   300	  unfold outcomeEventWeight
   301	  apply Finset.sum_le_sum
   302	  intro a _
   303	  apply Finset.sum_le_sum
   304	  intro b _
   305	  by_cases hE : E a b
   306	  · simp [hE, hEF a b hE]
   307	  · simp only [hE, ↓reduceIte]
   308	    split_ifs
   309	    · exact outcomeWeight_nonneg S x y a b
   310	    · exact le_rfl

   312	/--
   313	The tensor-product value, expressed as the distribution average of the Born
   314	probabilities.  This is `def:tensor-product-value` in
   315	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, with paper origin
   316	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:40-57`.
   317	-/
   318	noncomputable def Strategy.value {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) : ℝ :=
   319	  avgOver G.μ (fun xy =>
   320	    ∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB,
   321	      if G.decide xy.1 xy.2 a b then outcomeWeight S xy.1 xy.2 a b else 0)
   322	
   323	/--
   324	The tensor-product game value as a conditional supremum over all finite
   325	strategies.  The `sSup (Set.range ...)` form is the csSup formulation requested
   326	for `def:tensor-product-value`, blueprint
   327	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, paper origin
   328	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:40-57`; attainment is
   329	intentionally not asserted here.

     3	/-!
     4	# Finite-dimensional state transformations
     5	
     6	This file defines the tensor and reindexing operations used for strategy
     7	distance, Magic Square rigidity, and the qudit-to-qubit isomorphism. See
     8	blueprint chapters 11--13 and the declaration-level references below.
     9	-/
    10	
    11	open scoped Matrix
    12	
    13	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    14	
    15	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    16	
    17	/-- Conjugation by the local isometries in `thm:ms-rigidity` and
    18	`lem:pauli-binary`; blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:222-244` and
    19	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:710-741`, paper
    20	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:620-652` and
    21	`04_preliminaries.tex:1163-1208`. -/
    22	noncomputable def conjIsometry {ι ι' : Type*}
    23	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι']
    24	    (φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ ι')
    25	    (M : Op ι) : Op ι' :=
    26	  let U : Matrix ι' ι ℂ := Matrix.toEuclideanLin.symm φ.toLinearMap
    27	  U * M * Uᴴ
    28	
    29	/-- Coordinate transport used by `def:strategy-distance`, blueprint
    30	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:228-237`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:273-285`. -/
    31	noncomputable def reindexState {ι ι' : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    32	    [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι'] (e : ι ≃ ι')
    33	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι' :=
    34	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι' ℂ).symm
    35	    (fun j => (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ ψ) (e.symm j))
    36	
    37	/-- Apply the two independent local isometries of `thm:ms-rigidity`; blueprint
    38	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:222-244`, paper
    39	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:620-652`. -/
    40	noncomputable def isometryTensor
    41	    {ιA ιB κA κB : Type*}
    42	    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    43	    [Fintype κA] [DecidableEq κA] [Fintype κB] [DecidableEq κB]
    44	    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κA)
    45	    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κB)
    46	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) :
    47	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (κA × κB) :=
    48	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv (κA × κB) ℂ).symm
    49	    (fun p =>
    50	      ∑ i : ιA, ∑ j : ιB,
    51	        ((EuclideanSpace.equiv κA ℂ)
    52	            (φA ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ιA ℂ).symm (Pi.single i 1))) p.1) *
    53	          ((EuclideanSpace.equiv κB ℂ)
    54	            (φB ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ιB ℂ).symm (Pi.single j 1))) p.2) *

     3	/-!
     4	# Block-diagonal finite matrix operators
     5	
     6	This module contains block-diagonal trace and positive-semidefinite order facts
     7	for finite complex matrices.  The canonical SDP block algebra in Section 9 uses
     8	these lemmas to compare the paper's block form with Mathlib's
     9	`Matrix.blockDiagonal`.
    10	-/
    11	
    12	open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder Matrix.Norms.Elementwise
    13	open WithLp
    14	
    15	namespace Matrix
    16	
    17	/-- A block-diagonal matrix is the sum of its blocks tensored with the
    18	coordinate projections on the block index. -/
    19	theorem blockDiagonal_eq_sum_kronecker_diagonal {o m : Type*}
    20	    [Fintype o] [DecidableEq o] [Finite m] (B : o → Matrix m m ℂ) :
    21	    Matrix.blockDiagonal B =
    22	      ∑ b : o, Matrix.kronecker (B b)
    23	        (Matrix.diagonal fun c : o => if c = b then (1 : ℂ) else 0) := by
    24	  classical
    25	  letI : Fintype m := Fintype.ofFinite m
    26	  ext x y
    27	  rcases x with ⟨i, bx⟩
    28	  rcases y with ⟨j, cy⟩
    29	  rw [Matrix.sum_apply]
    30	  by_cases hxy : bx = cy
    31	  · subst cy
    32	    simp [Matrix.blockDiagonal_apply, Matrix.kronecker, Matrix.kroneckerMap_apply]
    33	  · simp [Matrix.blockDiagonal_apply, Matrix.kronecker, Matrix.kroneckerMap_apply, hxy]
    34	
    35	/-- `Matrix.blockDiagonal` as a linear map.
    36	
    37	Mathlib provides `Matrix.blockDiagonalAddMonoidHom` and
    38	`Matrix.blockDiagonal_smul`; this declaration packages these two facts in the
    39	linear form needed by finite-dimensional block SDP arguments. -/
    40	def blockDiagonalLinearMap (R : Type*) (m n o α : Type*)
    41	    [Semiring R] [DecidableEq o] [AddCommMonoid α] [Module R α] :
    42	    (o → Matrix m n α) →ₗ[R] Matrix (m × o) (n × o) α where
    43	  toFun := Matrix.blockDiagonal
    44	  map_add' := Matrix.blockDiagonal_add
    45	  map_smul' := Matrix.blockDiagonal_smul
    46	
    47	@[simp]
    48	theorem blockDiagonalLinearMap_apply (R : Type*) (m n o α : Type*)
    49	    [Semiring R] [DecidableEq o] [AddCommMonoid α] [Module R α]
    50	    (B : o → Matrix m n α) :
    51	    Matrix.blockDiagonalLinearMap R m n o α B = Matrix.blockDiagonal B :=
    52	  rfl
    53	
    54	/-- A block-diagonal complex matrix is positive semidefinite when all of its
    55	diagonal blocks are positive semidefinite. -/
    56	theorem blockDiagonal_nonneg {o m : Type*}
    57	    [Finite o] [DecidableEq o] [Finite m]
    58	    (B : o → Matrix m m ℂ) (hB : ∀ b, 0 ≤ B b) :
    59	    0 ≤ Matrix.blockDiagonal B := by
    60	  classical
    61	  letI : Fintype o := Fintype.ofFinite o
    62	  letI : Fintype m := Fintype.ofFinite m
    63	  rw [Matrix.blockDiagonal_eq_sum_kronecker_diagonal B]
    64	  exact Finset.sum_nonneg fun b _ =>
    65	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.kronecker_nonneg (hB b) (by
    66	      refine Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mpr ?_
    67	      exact Matrix.PosSemidef.diagonal <| by
    68	        intro c
    69	        by_cases hc : c = b <;> simp [hc])
    70	
    71	/-- A block-diagonal complex matrix is positive semidefinite exactly when each
    72	of its diagonal blocks is positive semidefinite. -/
    73	theorem blockDiagonal_nonneg_iff {o m : Type*}
    74	    [Finite o] [DecidableEq o] [Finite m]
    75	    (B : o → Matrix m m ℂ) :
    76	    0 ≤ Matrix.blockDiagonal B ↔ ∀ b, 0 ≤ B b := by
    77	  classical
    78	  letI : Fintype o := Fintype.ofFinite o
    79	  letI : Fintype m := Fintype.ofFinite m
    80	  constructor
    81	  · intro hB b
    82	    refine Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mpr ?_
    83	    let e : m → m × o := fun i => (i, b)
    84	    have hsub :
    85	        ((Matrix.blockDiagonal B).submatrix e e).PosSemidef :=
    86	      (Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mp hB).submatrix e
    87	    have hEq : (Matrix.blockDiagonal B).submatrix e e = B b := by
    88	      ext i j
    89	      simp [e, Matrix.blockDiagonal_apply_eq]
    90	    simpa [hEq] using hsub
    91	  · exact Matrix.blockDiagonal_nonneg B
    92	
    93	end Matrix

   309	          intro a ha

   318	          refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
   319	          intro a ha
   320	          simp [fiber, ha]

    29	/-- Relabel a matrix measurement along an equivalence of outcome alphabets. -/
    30	noncomputable def matrixMeasurementTransport

    53	theorem matrixMeasurementTransport_isProjective

    65	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    66	    [Fintype block] [DecidableEq block]

   108	    MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (blockDiagonalMeasurement M) := by
   109	  intro a

   117	    exact (hM r a).isIdempotentElem.eq

   125	/-! ## The correlated residue state -/
   126	
   127	/-- The normalized maximally correlated state on the common seed-fiber
   128	residue. -/
   129	noncomputable def seedResidueAncilla (L : LdParams) :
   130	    EuclideanSpace ℂ
   131	      (Fin (L.q / L.m) × Fin (L.q / L.m)) := by
   132	  letI : Nonempty (Fin (L.q / L.m)) :=
   133	    Fin.pos_iff_nonempty.mp L.seedFiberCard_pos
   134	  exact eprState (Fin (L.q / L.m))
   135	
   136	/-- The seed-residue ancilla has unit norm. -/
   137	theorem seedResidueAncilla_norm (L : LdParams) :
   138	    ‖seedResidueAncilla L‖ = 1 := by
   139	  letI : Nonempty (Fin (L.q / L.m)) :=
   140	    Fin.pos_iff_nonempty.mp L.seedFiberCard_pos
   141	  exact eprState_norm (Fin (L.q / L.m))
   142	
   143	/-- Reindexing Euclidean coordinates along an equivalence preserves norm. -/
   144	theorem reindexState_norm_eq
   145	    {iota kappa : Type*}
   146	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   147	    [Fintype kappa] [DecidableEq kappa]
   148	    (e : iota ≃ kappa) (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ iota) :
   149	    ‖reindexState e psi‖ = ‖psi‖ := by
   150	  rw [← sq_eq_sq₀ (norm_nonneg _) (norm_nonneg _)]
   151	  rw [EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq, EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq]
   152	  change (∑ j : kappa, ‖psi (e.symm j)‖ ^ 2) = ∑ i : iota, ‖psi i‖ ^ 2
   153	  exact e.symm.sum_comp (fun i => ‖psi i‖ ^ 2)
   154	
   155	/-- The coordinate tensor of two Euclidean vectors has the product norm. -/
   156	theorem vecTensor_norm_eq
   157	    {iota kappa : Type*}
   158	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   159	    [Fintype kappa] [DecidableEq kappa]
   160	    (u : EuclideanSpace ℂ iota) (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ kappa) :
   161	    ‖vecTensor u v‖ = ‖u‖ * ‖v‖ := by
   162	  rw [← sq_eq_sq₀ (norm_nonneg _) (mul_nonneg (norm_nonneg _) (norm_nonneg _))]
   163	  rw [EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq, mul_pow, EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq,
   164	    EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq]
   165	  change (∑ p : iota × kappa, ‖u p.1 * v p.2‖ ^ 2) =
   166	    (∑ i : iota, ‖u i‖ ^ 2) * ∑ j : kappa, ‖v j‖ ^ 2
   167	  simp only [norm_mul, mul_pow]
   168	  rw [← Finset.univ_product_univ, Finset.sum_product, Finset.sum_mul]
   169	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   170	  intro i hi
   171	  rw [Finset.mul_sum]
   172	
   173	/-- Tensor the original strategy state with the maximally correlated residue
   174	state and shuffle the factors back into the two local carriers. -/
   175	noncomputable def seedFiberLiftedState
   176	    {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) (L : LdParams) :
   177	    EuclideanSpace ℂ
   178	      ((S.ιA × Fin (L.q / L.m)) × (S.ιB × Fin (L.q / L.m))) :=
   179	  reindexState prodShuffle (vecTensor S.ψ (seedResidueAncilla L))
   180	
   181	/-- The correlated seed-fiber lift preserves normalization of the strategy
   182	state. -/
   183	theorem seedFiberLiftedState_norm
   184	    {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) (L : LdParams) :
   185	    ‖seedFiberLiftedState S L‖ = 1 := by
   186	  rw [seedFiberLiftedState, reindexState_norm_eq, vecTensor_norm_eq,
   187	    S.ψ_norm, seedResidueAncilla_norm, one_mul]
   188	
   189	/-! ## From the seed-indexed game to the direct game -/
   190	
   191	/-- The seed-indexed question selected in one residue block of a direct
   192	question.  Applying `ldCL` ensures that irrelevant ambient coordinates are
   193	canonicalized exactly as in the source game. -/
   194	noncomputable def seededLdQuestion (L : LdParams)
   195	    (q : DirectLdQuestion L.toDirectLdParams)
   196	    (residue : Fin (L.q / L.m)) : LdQuestion L :=
   197	  (q.1, ldCL L q.1 (ldSpaceOfDirectResidue L q.2 residue))
   198	
   199	/-- Dilate a strategy for the seed-indexed low-degree game to the directly
   200	indexed game.  The two local carriers receive correlated copies of the seed
   201	residue, and each measurement is block diagonal in that residue. -/
   202	noncomputable def ldStrategyToDirect (L : LdParams)
   203	    (S : Strategy (ldGame L)) : Strategy (directLdGame L.toDirectLdParams) where
   204	  ιA := S.ιA × Fin (L.q / L.m)
   205	  ιB := S.ιB × Fin (L.q / L.m)
   206	  ψ := seedFiberLiftedState S L
   207	  ψ_norm := seedFiberLiftedState_norm S L
   208	  A q := blockDiagonalMeasurement fun residue =>
   209	    matrixMeasurementTransport (ldDirectAnswerEquiv L)
   210	      (S.A (seededLdQuestion L q residue))
   211	  B q := blockDiagonalMeasurement fun residue =>
   212	    matrixMeasurementTransport (ldDirectAnswerEquiv L)
   213	      (S.B (seededLdQuestion L q residue))
   214	
   215	/-- Projectivity is preserved by the correlated seed-fiber dilation. -/
   216	theorem ldStrategyToDirect_isProjective (L : LdParams)
   217	    (S : Strategy (ldGame L)) (hS : S.IsProjective) :
   218	    (ldStrategyToDirect L S).IsProjective := by
   219	  constructor
   220	  · intro q
   221	    apply blockDiagonalMeasurement_isProjective
   222	    intro residue
   223	    apply matrixMeasurementTransport_isProjective
   224	    exact hS.1 (seededLdQuestion L q residue)
   225	  · intro q
   226	    apply blockDiagonalMeasurement_isProjective
   227	    intro residue
   228	    apply matrixMeasurementTransport_isProjective
   229	    exact hS.2 (seededLdQuestion L q residue)
   230	
   231	@[simp] theorem ldStrategyToDirect_A_effect (L : LdParams)
   232	    (S : Strategy (ldGame L))
   233	    (q : DirectLdQuestion L.toDirectLdParams)
   234	    (answer : DirectLdAnswer L.toDirectLdParams) :
   235	    ((ldStrategyToDirect L S).A q).effect answer =
   236	      Matrix.blockDiagonal fun residue =>
   237	        (S.A (seededLdQuestion L q residue)).effect
   238	          ((ldDirectAnswerEquiv L).symm answer) :=
   239	  rfl
   240	
   241	@[simp] theorem ldStrategyToDirect_B_effect (L : LdParams)
   242	    (S : Strategy (ldGame L))
   243	    (q : DirectLdQuestion L.toDirectLdParams)
   244	    (answer : DirectLdAnswer L.toDirectLdParams) :
   245	    ((ldStrategyToDirect L S).B q).effect answer =
   246	      Matrix.blockDiagonal fun residue =>
   247	        (S.B (seededLdQuestion L q residue)).effect
   248	          ((ldDirectAnswerEquiv L).symm answer) :=
   249	  rfl
   250	
   251	/-- A direct question reconstructed in a residue block parses back to its
   252	canonical direct form. -/
   253	theorem parse_seededLdQuestion (L : LdParams)
   254	    (q : DirectLdQuestion L.toDirectLdParams)
   255	    (residue : Fin (L.q / L.m)) :
   256	    parseLdQuestion L (seededLdQuestion L q residue) =
   257	      (q.1, directLdMap L.toDirectLdParams q.1 q.2) := by
   258	  exact parseLdQuestion_ldCL_ofDirectResidue L q.1 q.2 residue
   259	
   260	/-- Coordinate formula for the correlated residue lift. -/
   261	theorem seedFiberLiftedState_apply
   262	    {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) (L : LdParams)
   263	    (i : S.ιA) (j : S.ιB)
   264	    (r s : Fin (L.q / L.m)) :
   265	    seedFiberLiftedState S L ((i, r), (j, s)) =
   266	      if r = s then
   267	        S.ψ (i, j) * (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card (Fin (L.q / L.m)) : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹

   269	  letI : Nonempty (Fin (L.q / L.m)) :=
   270	    Fin.pos_iff_nonempty.mp L.seedFiberCard_pos

     3	/-!
     4	# Matrix-valued measurements for the MIP*=RE project
     5	
     6	This file provides the matrix-valued measurement layer used by the LDT formalization.
     7	
     8	## Main definitions
     9	
    10	* `Submeasurement` — a family of PSD matrices summing to at most the identity.
    11	* `Measurement` — a family of PSD matrices summing to exactly the identity.
    12	* `Submeasurement.postprocess` — data-processed submeasurements via answer relabeling.
    13	* `Measurement.postprocess` — the paper's postprocessing proposition for complete POVMs.
    14	* `inconsistency` — the off-diagonal mass `∑_{a ≠ b} τ(M_a N_b)`.
    15	* `diagOverlap` — the diagonal mass `∑_a τ(M_a N_a)`.
    16	
    17	## References
    18	
    19	This file builds the project's finite-dimensional measurement layer on top of
    20	the normalized-trace and positive-operator facts in `MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix`
    21	for the quantum formalization in `references/ldt-paper/`.
    22	-/
    23	
    24	open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder
    25	
    26	namespace MIPStarRE.Quantum
    27	
    28	/-! ## Submeasurements and measurements -/
    29	
    30	/--
    31	A submeasurement on a finite answer type `α` is a family of PSD matrices
    32	`M : α → Op d` with `∑ a, M a ≤ 1`.
    33	-/
    34	structure Submeasurement (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] where
    35	  /-- The effect operators. -/
    36	  effect : α → Op d
    37	  /-- Each effect is positive semidefinite. -/
    38	  pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ effect a
    39	  /-- The effects sum to at most the identity. -/
    40	  sum_le_one : ∑ a, effect a ≤ 1
    41	
    42	/--
    43	A measurement is a submeasurement whose effects sum exactly to the identity.
    44	-/
    45	structure Measurement (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    46	    extends Submeasurement α d where
    47	  /-- The effects sum to the identity. -/
    48	  sum_eq_one : ∑ a, effect a = 1
    49	
    50	/-! ## Totals and postprocessing -/
    51	
    52	namespace Submeasurement
    53	
    54	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    55	variable {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
    56	
    57	/-! ### Totals and postprocessing -/
    58	
    59	/-- The total operator `∑ a, M_a`. -/
    60	noncomputable def total (M : Submeasurement α d) : Op d :=
    61	  ∑ a, M.effect a
    62	
    63	/--
    64	Data processing: relabel the answer set by `f : α → β`, summing the effects over
    65	fibers.
    66	-/
    67	noncomputable def postprocess [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    68	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) : Submeasurement β d where
    69	  effect b := ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
    70	  pos b := Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => M.pos a
    71	  sum_le_one := by
    72	    calc
    73	      ∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
    74	          = ∑ a, M.effect a := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect
    75	      _ ≤ 1 := M.sum_le_one
    76	
    77	/-- Restatement of `sum_le_one` in terms of the named total operator. -/
    78	theorem total_le_one (M : Submeasurement α d) :
    79	    M.total ≤ 1 := by
    80	  simpa [total] using M.sum_le_one
    81	
    82	/-- Postprocessing preserves the sum of all effects. -/
    83	theorem postprocess_sum_eq [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    84	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) :
    85	    ∑ a, M.effect a = ∑ b, (M.postprocess f).effect b :=
    86	  (Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect).symm
    87	
    88	/-- Postprocessing preserves the named total operator. -/
    89	theorem postprocess_total [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    90	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) :
    91	    (M.postprocess f).total = M.total := by
    92	  simpa [total] using (M.postprocess_sum_eq f).symm
    93	
    94	end Submeasurement
    95	
    96	namespace Measurement
    97	
    98	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    99	variable {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
   100	
   101	/--
   102	Build a complete measurement from effects whose sum is exactly the identity.
   103	
   104	This constructor keeps the equality proof as the primary hypothesis and derives
   105	the inherited submeasurement inequality automatically.  It is useful at paper
   106	sites that are explicitly POVMs rather than relaxed sub-POVMs.
   107	-/
   108	def ofSumEqOne (effect : α → Op d) (pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ effect a)
   109	    (sum_eq_one : ∑ a, effect a = 1) : Measurement α d where
   110	  effect := effect
   111	  pos := pos
   112	  sum_le_one := le_of_eq sum_eq_one
   113	  sum_eq_one := sum_eq_one
   114	
   115	/-- The named total of a complete measurement is the identity. -/
   116	theorem total_eq_one (M : Measurement α d) :
   117	    M.total = 1 :=
   118	  M.sum_eq_one
   119	
   120	/--
   121	Postprocess a complete measurement by relabeling outcomes.
   122	
   123	This formalizes `references/ldt-paper/preliminaries.tex:169--180`: regrouping
   124	the effects along the fibers of `f` preserves the total operator, so a POVM
   125	remains a POVM after postprocessing.
   126	-/
   127	noncomputable def postprocess [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   128	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) : Measurement β d where
   129	  toSubmeasurement := M.toSubmeasurement.postprocess f
   130	  sum_eq_one := by
   131	    calc
   132	      ∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
   133	          = ∑ a, M.effect a := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect
   134	      _ = 1 := M.sum_eq_one
   135	
   136	@[simp] theorem postprocess_effect [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   137	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) (b : β) :
   138	    (M.postprocess f).effect b =
   139	      ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a :=
   140	  rfl
   141	
   142	@[simp] theorem postprocess_to_submeasurement [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   143	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) :
   144	    (M.postprocess f).toSubmeasurement = M.toSubmeasurement.postprocess f :=
   145	  rfl
   146	
   147	end Measurement
   148	
   149	/-! ## Overlap definitions -/
   150	
   151	section Overlap
   152	
   153	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
   154	variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   155	
   156	/-- The off-diagonal overlap mass `∑_{a ≠ b} τ(M_a N_b)`. -/
   157	noncomputable def inconsistency (M N : α → Op d) : ℂ :=
   158	  ∑ a, ∑ b ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun b => b ≠ a), normalizedTrace (M a * N b)
   159	
   160	/-- The diagonal overlap mass `∑_a τ(M_a N_a)`. -/
   161	noncomputable def diagOverlap (M N : α → Op d) : ℂ :=
   162	  ∑ a, normalizedTrace (M a * N a)
   163	
   164	end Overlap
   165	
   166	end MIPStarRE.Quantum

   101	/--
   102	Build a complete measurement from effects whose sum is exactly the identity.
   103	
   104	This constructor keeps the equality proof as the primary hypothesis and derives
   105	the inherited submeasurement inequality automatically.  It is useful at paper
   106	sites that are explicitly POVMs rather than relaxed sub-POVMs.
   107	-/
   108	def ofSumEqOne (effect : α → Op d) (pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ effect a)
   109	    (sum_eq_one : ∑ a, effect a = 1) : Measurement α d where
   110	  effect := effect
   111	  pos := pos
   112	  sum_le_one := le_of_eq sum_eq_one
   113	  sum_eq_one := sum_eq_one
   114	
   115	/-- The named total of a complete measurement is the identity. -/
   116	theorem total_eq_one (M : Measurement α d) :
   117	    M.total = 1 :=
   118	  M.sum_eq_one
   119	
   120	/--
   121	Postprocess a complete measurement by relabeling outcomes.
   122	
   123	This formalizes `references/ldt-paper/preliminaries.tex:169--180`: regrouping
   124	the effects along the fibers of `f` preserves the total operator, so a POVM
   125	remains a POVM after postprocessing.
   126	-/
   127	noncomputable def postprocess [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   128	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) : Measurement β d where
   129	  toSubmeasurement := M.toSubmeasurement.postprocess f
   130	  sum_eq_one := by
   131	    calc
   132	      ∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
   133	          = ∑ a, M.effect a := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect
   134	      _ = 1 := M.sum_eq_one
   135	
   136	@[simp] theorem postprocess_effect [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   137	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) (b : β) :
   138	    (M.postprocess f).effect b =
   139	      ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a :=
   140	  rfl

   143	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) :
   144	    (M.postprocess f).toSubmeasurement = M.toSubmeasurement.postprocess f :=

+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.DirectLowDegree.Transport.Correspondence
+
+/-!
+# Question and answer transport for the directly indexed low-degree game
+
+This module reads mature low individual degree questions as canonical direct
+questions and rebases direct answers to the mature line parametrization.
+
+Points and lines are decoded with the coordinate order reversed
+(`directPointEquiv`), so that the suffix-zero direction restriction of the
+mature diagonal test becomes the prefix-zero restriction of the direct game.
+A mature diagonal line reveals no coordinate index, whereas a direct diagonal
+question carries one.  The transported question uses the *leading index* of
+the decoded direction, the least coordinate at which the direction is
+nonzero.  Under the direct sampler, this is the index attached to the sampled
+direction exactly when the direction is nonzero at the sampled index
+(`directDiagonalIndexOf_prefixProjection`), an event of conditional
+probability `1 - 1/q`; on the mature side, the leading index of a decoded
+`j`-restricted direction is `Fin.rev j` exactly when its pivot coordinate is
+nonzero (`directDiagonalIndexOf_extendRestrictedDirection`).  Diagonal answers
+on zero-direction lines are read as the constant polynomial carrying their
+value at the base point, following `rem:ld-win-zero-direction`.
+
+## References
+
+- `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:230-272`
+- `references/ldt-paper/test_definition.tex:49-65`
+- `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:120-121`
+- `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`
+-/
+
+open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder
+
+namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
+
+open MIPStarRE.LDT
+open MIPStarRE.Quantum
+
+noncomputable section
+
+/-! ## Canonical line rebasing for the mature LDT interface -/
+
+/-- A chosen affine parameter expressing a point relative to its canonical
+line representative. -/
+noncomputable def directLineRepParameter
+    {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ} (v u : Fin m → K) : K :=
+  Classical.choose (mem_linePoints_lineRepMap v u)
+
+/-- The chosen canonical rebase parameter reconstructs the original point. -/
+theorem directLineRepParameter_spec
+    {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ} (v u : Fin m → K) :
+    u = lineRepMap v u + directLineRepParameter v u • v :=
+  Classical.choose_spec (mem_linePoints_lineRepMap v u)
+
+/-- Canonical line representatives are unchanged by translation along their
+direction. -/
+theorem lineRepMap_add_smul
+    {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
+    (v u : Fin m → K) (t : K) :
+    lineRepMap v (u + t • v) = lineRepMap v u := by
+  let W : Submodule K (Fin m → K) := Submodule.span K ({v} : Set (Fin m → K))
+  have hv : v ∈ W := Submodule.subset_span (Set.mem_singleton v)
+  have hzero : lineRepMap v v = 0 := by
+    simp [lineRepMap, canonicalProjOfKernel, W, LinearMap.comp_apply,
+      Submodule.projectionOnto_apply_of_mem_right
+        (isCompl_registerSubmodule_canonicalComplement W).symm hv]
+  simp [map_add, map_smul, hzero]
+
+/-- For a nonzero direction, the canonical rebase parameter is unique. -/
+theorem directLineRepParameter_eq_of_nonzero
+    {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
+    {v u : Fin m → K} (hv : v ≠ 0) {t : K}
+    (ht : u = lineRepMap v u + t • v) :
+    directLineRepParameter v u = t := by
+  have hfun : directLineRepParameter v u • v = t • v := by
+    apply add_left_cancel (a := lineRepMap v u)
+    exact (directLineRepParameter_spec v u).symm.trans ht
+  obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ : ∃ i, v i ≠ 0 := by
+    by_contra h
+    apply hv
+    funext i
+    simpa using not_exists.mp h i
+  have hcoord := congrFun hfun i
+  simp only [Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul] at hcoord
+  exact mul_right_cancel₀ hi hcoord
+
+/-- Translating a point on a nonzero line adds the translation to its
+canonical rebase parameter. -/
+theorem directLineRepParameter_add_smul
+    {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
+    {v u : Fin m → K} (hv : v ≠ 0) (t : K) :
+    directLineRepParameter v (u + t • v) =
+      directLineRepParameter v u + t := by
+  apply directLineRepParameter_eq_of_nonzero hv
+  rw [lineRepMap_add_smul]
+  calc
+    u + t • v =
+        (lineRepMap v u + directLineRepParameter v u • v) + t • v := by
+      rw [← directLineRepParameter_spec v u]
+    _ = lineRepMap v u + (directLineRepParameter v u + t) • v := by
+      module
+
+/-! ## The leading index of a direction -/
+
+/-- The coordinates at which a direct direction vector is nonzero. -/
+def directionSupport (D : DirectLdParams) (v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) :
+    Finset (Fin D.m) :=
+  open Classical in
+  Finset.univ.filter fun j => v j ≠ 0
+
+theorem mem_directionSupport (D : DirectLdParams)
+    (v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) (j : Fin D.m) :
+    j ∈ directionSupport D v ↔ v j ≠ 0 := by
+  simp [directionSupport]
+
+/-- The leading index of a direction: the least coordinate at which it is
+nonzero, or the last coordinate for the zero direction.  Every coordinate
+before the leading index vanishes, so a direction is the prefix projection of
+itself at its leading index, and the pair (leading index, direction) is a
+canonical direct diagonal sample.  It is the direct index of the sample
+whenever the sampled direction is nonzero at the sampled index. -/
+noncomputable def directDiagonalIndexOf (D : DirectLdParams)
+    (v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) : Fin D.m :=
+  open Classical in
+  if h : (directionSupport D v).Nonempty then (directionSupport D v).min' h
+  else Fin.rev D.firstIndex
+
+/-- Coordinates before the leading index vanish. -/
+theorem directDiagonalIndexOf_prefix_zero (D : DirectLdParams)
+    (v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) :
+    ∀ j : Fin D.m, j.val < (directDiagonalIndexOf D v).val → v j = 0 := by
+  classical
+  intro j hj
+  by_contra hne
+  have hmem : j ∈ directionSupport D v := (mem_directionSupport D v j).mpr hne
+  have hnonempty : (directionSupport D v).Nonempty := ⟨j, hmem⟩
+  have hle : directDiagonalIndexOf D v ≤ j := by
+    unfold directDiagonalIndexOf
+    rw [dif_pos hnonempty]
+    exact Finset.min'_le _ _ hmem
+  exact absurd (Fin.lt_def.mpr hj) (not_lt.mpr hle)
+
+/-- A direction vanishing before `i` and nonzero at `i` has leading index
+`i`. -/
+theorem directDiagonalIndexOf_eq (D : DirectLdParams)
+    {v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D} {i : Fin D.m}
+    (hzero : ∀ j : Fin D.m, j.val < i.val → v j = 0) (hi : v i ≠ 0) :
+    directDiagonalIndexOf D v = i := by
+  classical
+  have hmem : i ∈ directionSupport D v := (mem_directionSupport D v i).mpr hi
+  have hnonempty : (directionSupport D v).Nonempty := ⟨i, hmem⟩
+  unfold directDiagonalIndexOf
+  rw [dif_pos hnonempty]
+  apply le_antisymm
+  · exact Finset.min'_le _ _ hmem
+  · apply Finset.le_min'
+    intro j hj
+    by_contra hlt
+    exact (mem_directionSupport D v j).mp hj
+      (hzero j (Fin.lt_def.mp (not_le.mp hlt)))
+
