    29	/-- Parameters for the directly indexed low-degree game.  Unlike `LdParams`,
    30	this directly indexed line-space construction has no divisibility field: its coordinate index is
    31	sampled from `Fin m` rather than encoded by fibers of `chiIndex`.
    32	
    33	This is the direct-index repair described in
    34	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`; it is not a second
    35	definition of the source verifier game. -/
    36	structure DirectLdParams where
    37	  q : ℕ
    38	  m : ℕ
    39	  d : ℕ
    40	  k : ℕ
    41	  hm : 1 ≤ m
    42	  hd : 1 ≤ d
    43	  hk : 1 ≤ k
    44	  hq : IsAdmissibleSize q
    45	
    46	/-- The canonical scalar model for directly indexed parameters. -/
    47	noncomputable def DirectLdParams.model (D : DirectLdParams) : FixedFieldModel D.q :=
    48	  fixedFieldModel D.q D.hq
    49	
    50	/-- The scalar field of a directly indexed low-degree game. -/
    51	abbrev DirectScalarQ (D : DirectLdParams) := D.model.K
    52	
    53	/-- The first coordinate, available because directly indexed dimensions are
    54	positive. -/
    55	def DirectLdParams.firstIndex (D : DirectLdParams) : Fin D.m :=
    56	  ⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one D.hm⟩
    57	
    58	instance (D : DirectLdParams) : Nonempty (Fin D.m) := ⟨D.firstIndex⟩
    59	
    60	/-- The direct game used at the extended dimension of the combining map.  Its
    61	field, degree, and simultaneity parameters are inherited from `P`, while its
    62	dimension is `2 * P.m + 2`; no divisibility assertion is introduced.
    63	
    64	The construction has dimension `2 * P.m + 2` without requiring
    65	`2 * P.m + 2 ∣ P.q`; it supplies the directly indexed line and coordinate
    66	spaces used in the dimension-extension argument of
    67	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1257-1293`.
    68	-/
    69	def AdmissibleParams.extendedDirectLd (P : AdmissibleParams) : DirectLdParams where
    70	  q := P.q
    71	  m := 2 * P.m + 2
    72	  d := P.d
    73	  k := 1
    74	  hm := by omega
    75	  hd := P.hd
    76	  hk := by decide
    77	  hq := P.hq
    78	
    79	/-- A common random sample for the directly indexed question distribution.
    80	The point, coordinate index, and unrestricted direction are mutually uniform. -/
    81	structure DirectLdSpace (D : DirectLdParams) where
    82	  point : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D
    83	  index : Fin D.m
    84	  direction : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D
    85	  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype
    86	
    87	instance (D : DirectLdParams) : Nonempty (DirectLdSpace D) :=
    88	  ⟨⟨0, D.firstIndex, 0⟩⟩
    89	
    90	/-- Decompose a direct sample into its point and the remaining independent
    91	coordinates. -/
    92	private def directLdSpacePointEquiv (D : DirectLdParams) :
    93	    DirectLdSpace D ≃
    94	      (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) ×
    95	        (Fin D.m × (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) where
    96	  toFun sample := (sample.point, sample.index, sample.direction)
    97	  invFun sample := ⟨sample.1, sample.2.1, sample.2.2⟩
    98	  left_inv sample := by cases sample; rfl
    99	  right_inv sample := by cases sample; rfl
   100	
   101	/-- Decompose a direct sample into its stored index and the remaining
   102	independent coordinates. -/
   103	private def directLdSpaceIndexEquiv (D : DirectLdParams) :
   104	    DirectLdSpace D ≃
   105	      Fin D.m ×
   106	        ((Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) ×
   107	          (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) where
   108	  toFun sample := (sample.index, sample.point, sample.direction)
   109	  invFun sample := ⟨sample.2.1, sample.1, sample.2.2⟩
   110	  left_inv sample := by cases sample; rfl
   111	  right_inv sample := by cases sample; rfl
   112	
   113	/-- Zero the coordinates preceding the directly sampled prefix index. -/
   114	def directPrefixProjection {D : DirectLdParams} (i : Fin D.m)
   115	    (v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D :=
   116	  fun j => if j.val < i.val then 0 else v j
   117	
   118	/-- Canonical line descriptions whose coordinate index is stored directly.
   119	Coordinates are numbered from zero, so `index = i` represents coordinate
   120	`i + 1` in the paper. -/
   121	inductive DirectLineDesc (D : DirectLdParams) where
   122	  | axis (base : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) (index : Fin D.m)
   123	      (baseFixed : lineRepMap (coordinateDirection index) base = base)
   124	  | diagonal (base : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) (index : Fin D.m)
   125	      (direction : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)
   126	      (baseFixed : lineRepMap direction base = base)
   127	      (prefixZero : ∀ j : Fin D.m, j.val < index.val → direction j = 0)
   128	  deriving DecidableEq
   129	
   130	/-- The kind of a directly indexed line. -/
   131	def DirectLineDesc.kind {D : DirectLdParams} : DirectLineDesc D → LineKind
   132	  | .axis _ _ _ => .axis
   133	  | .diagonal _ _ _ _ _ => .diagonal
   134	
   135	/-- The coordinate index stored in a directly indexed line. -/
   136	def DirectLineDesc.index {D : DirectLdParams} : DirectLineDesc D → Fin D.m
   137	  | .axis _ index _ => index
   138	  | .diagonal _ index _ _ _ => index
   139	
   140	/-- The canonical base point of a directly indexed line. -/
   141	def DirectLineDesc.base {D : DirectLdParams} :
   142	    DirectLineDesc D → Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D
   143	  | .axis base _ _ => base
   144	  | .diagonal base _ _ _ _ => base
   145	
   146	/-- The geometric direction of a directly indexed line. -/
   147	def DirectLineDesc.direction {D : DirectLdParams} (line : DirectLineDesc D) :
   148	    Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D :=
   149	  match line with
   150	  | .axis _ index _ => coordinateDirection index
   151	  | .diagonal _ _ direction _ _ => direction
   152	
   153	/-- The base of a directly indexed description is fixed by its geometric
   154	direction. -/
   155	theorem DirectLineDesc.base_fixed {D : DirectLdParams} (line : DirectLineDesc D) :
   156	    lineRepMap line.direction line.base = line.base := by
   157	  cases line with
   158	  | axis base index baseFixed => exact baseFixed
   159	  | diagonal base index direction baseFixed prefixZero => exact baseFixed
   160	
   161	/-- Every directly indexed diagonal description retains its prefix-zero
   162	invariant. -/
   163	theorem DirectLineDesc.diagonal_prefix_zero {D : DirectLdParams}
   164	    (line : DirectLineDesc D) (hline : line.kind = .diagonal) :
   165	    ∀ j : Fin D.m, j.val < line.index.val → line.direction j = 0 := by
   166	  cases line with
   167	  | axis base index baseFixed => simp [DirectLineDesc.kind] at hline
   168	  | diagonal base index direction baseFixed prefixZero => exact prefixZero
   169	
   170	/-- The point set represented by a directly indexed line. -/
   171	noncomputable def DirectLineDesc.pointSet {D : DirectLdParams}
   172	    (line : DirectLineDesc D) : Set (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) :=
   173	  linePoints line.base line.direction
   174	
   175	/-- Turn a direct sample into its canonical axis-line description. -/
   176	noncomputable def directALineDescOf (D : DirectLdParams)
   177	    (sample : DirectLdSpace D) : DirectLineDesc D :=
   178	  let direction := coordinateDirection sample.index
   179	  let base := lineRepMap direction sample.point
   180	  .axis base sample.index (lineRepMap_apply_self direction sample.point)
   181	
   182	/-- Turn a direct sample into its canonical diagonal-line description. -/
   183	noncomputable def directDLineDescOf (D : DirectLdParams)
   184	    (sample : DirectLdSpace D) : DirectLineDesc D :=
   185	  let direction := directPrefixProjection sample.index sample.direction
   186	  let base := lineRepMap direction sample.point
   187	  .diagonal base sample.index direction
   188	    (lineRepMap_apply_self direction sample.point) (by
   189	      intro j hj
   190	      change directPrefixProjection sample.index sample.direction j = 0
   191	      rw [directPrefixProjection, if_pos hj])
   192	
   193	/-- The axis-line/point law with a directly sampled coordinate index. -/
   194	noncomputable def directALinePointDist (D : DirectLdParams) :
   195	    Distribution (DirectLineDesc D × (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) :=
   196	  (uniformDistribution (DirectLdSpace D)).map fun sample =>
   197	    (directALineDescOf D sample, sample.point)
   198	
   199	/-- The diagonal-line/point law with a directly sampled prefix index. -/
   200	noncomputable def directDLinePointDist (D : DirectLdParams) :
   201	    Distribution (DirectLineDesc D × (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) :=
   202	  (uniformDistribution (DirectLdSpace D)).map fun sample =>
   203	    (directDLineDescOf D sample, sample.point)
   204	
   205	/-- The equal mixture of the directly indexed axis and diagonal line-point
   206	laws.  This is the replacement for the otherwise undefined extended-dimension
   207	instance used at paper
   208	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1020-1116`. -/
   209	noncomputable def directLinePointDist (D : DirectLdParams) :
   210	    Distribution (DirectLineDesc D × (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) :=
   211	  Distribution.mix (1 / 2) (by norm_num) (by norm_num)
   212	    (directALinePointDist D) (directDLinePointDist D)
   213	
   214	/-- The directly indexed axis-line/point law is probabilistic. -/
   215	theorem directALinePointDist_isProbability (D : DirectLdParams) :
   216	    (directALinePointDist D).IsProbability := by
   217	  exact (uniformDistribution_isProbability (DirectLdSpace D)).map _
   218	
   219	/-- The directly indexed diagonal-line/point law is probabilistic. -/
   220	theorem directDLinePointDist_isProbability (D : DirectLdParams) :
   221	    (directDLinePointDist D).IsProbability := by
   222	  exact (uniformDistribution_isProbability (DirectLdSpace D)).map _
   223	
   224	/-- The directly indexed line-point mixture is probabilistic. -/
   225	theorem directLinePointDist_isProbability (D : DirectLdParams) :
   226	    (directLinePointDist D).IsProbability := by
   227	  exact Distribution.mix_isProbability _ _ _
   228	    (directALinePointDist_isProbability D) (directDLinePointDist_isProbability D)
   229	    (by norm_num) (by norm_num)
   230	
   231	/-- A point differs from its canonical line representative by a scalar
   232	multiple of the line direction.  This is the canonical incidence lemma of
   233	`def:line-representative`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:497-517`
   234	(the decomposition establishing incidence is at lines 507-509), shared by
   235	the line-point laws and the strategy transport. -/
   236	theorem mem_linePoints_lineRepMap {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
   237	    (v u : Fin m → K) : u ∈ linePoints (lineRepMap v u) v := by
   238	  let W : Submodule K (Fin m → K) := Submodule.span K ({v} : Set (Fin m → K))
   239	  let T : Submodule K (Fin m → K) :=
   240	    registerSubmodule K (canonicalComplement W)
   241	  have hdiff : u - lineRepMap v u ∈ W := by
   242	    simpa [lineRepMap, canonicalProjOfKernel, W, T, LinearMap.comp_apply] using
   243	      (Submodule.sub_projection_mem
   244	        (isCompl_registerSubmodule_canonicalComplement W).symm u)
   245	  rcases Submodule.mem_span_singleton.mp hdiff with ⟨t, ht⟩
   246	  refine ⟨t, ?_⟩
   247	  rw [ht]
   248	  abel

   250	/-- The point and stored-index marginals of the direct axis-line law are
   251	uniform.  This is a direct-index analogue of `lem:alnf`, required by
   252	the repair described in `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`;
   253	the source distribution is at
   254	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-257`.
   255	-/
   256	theorem directALinePointDist_point_index_marginal_uniform (D : DirectLdParams) :
   257	    (directALinePointDist D).map Prod.snd =
   258	        uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) ∧
   259	      (directALinePointDist D).map (fun sample => sample.1.index) =
   260	        uniformDistribution (Fin D.m) := by
   261	  constructor
   262	  · unfold directALinePointDist
   263	    rw [distribution_map_map_of_isProbability
   264	      (uniformDistribution (DirectLdSpace D))
   265	      (uniformDistribution_isProbability (DirectLdSpace D))]
   266	    simpa [Function.comp_def] using
   267	      (uniformDistribution_map_fst_of_equiv
   268	        (e := directLdSpacePointEquiv D)
   269	        (f := fun sample : DirectLdSpace D => sample.point) (by intro; rfl))
   270	  · unfold directALinePointDist
   271	    rw [distribution_map_map_of_isProbability
   272	      (uniformDistribution (DirectLdSpace D))
   273	      (uniformDistribution_isProbability (DirectLdSpace D))]
   274	    simpa [Function.comp_def, directALineDescOf, DirectLineDesc.index] using
   275	      (uniformDistribution_map_fst_of_equiv
   276	        (e := directLdSpaceIndexEquiv D)
   277	        (f := fun sample : DirectLdSpace D => sample.index) (by intro; rfl))
   278	
   279	/-- Every sampled direct axis line contains its paired point.  This is the
   280	Direct-index incidence obligation corresponding to `lem:alnf` and
   281	the repair in `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`. -/
   282	theorem directALinePointDist_mem_line (D : DirectLdParams) :
   283	    ∀ sample ∈ (directALinePointDist D).support,
   284	      sample.2 ∈ sample.1.pointSet := by
   285	  intro sample hsample
   286	  rw [directALinePointDist, Distribution.map_support,
   287	    uniformDistribution_support] at hsample
   288	  rcases Finset.mem_image.mp hsample with ⟨source, _, rfl⟩
   289	  simpa [directALineDescOf, DirectLineDesc.pointSet,
   290	    DirectLineDesc.base, DirectLineDesc.direction] using
   291	    (mem_linePoints_lineRepMap
   292	      (coordinateDirection source.index) source.point)

   294	/-- The point and stored-index marginals of the direct diagonal-line law are

   298	theorem directDLinePointDist_point_index_marginal_uniform (D : DirectLdParams) :

   300	        uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) ∧
   301	      (directDLinePointDist D).map (fun sample => sample.1.index) =
   302	        uniformDistribution (Fin D.m) := by
   303	  constructor
   304	  · unfold directDLinePointDist
   305	    rw [distribution_map_map_of_isProbability
   306	      (uniformDistribution (DirectLdSpace D))
   307	      (uniformDistribution_isProbability (DirectLdSpace D))]
   308	    simpa [Function.comp_def] using

   311	        (f := fun sample : DirectLdSpace D => sample.point) (by intro; rfl))
   312	  · unfold directDLinePointDist
   313	    rw [distribution_map_map_of_isProbability
   314	      (uniformDistribution (DirectLdSpace D))
   315	      (uniformDistribution_isProbability (DirectLdSpace D))]
   316	    simpa [Function.comp_def, directDLineDescOf, DirectLineDesc.index] using

   321	/-- Every sampled direct diagonal line contains its paired point.  This is the

   323	theorem directDLinePointDist_mem_line (D : DirectLdParams) :

    27	/-- Coefficient lists for a univariate polynomial of degree at most `c` in the
    28	direct scalar field. -/
    29	abbrev DirectDegPoly (D : DirectLdParams) (c : ℕ) :=
    30	  Fin (c + 1) → DirectScalarQ D
    31	
    32	/-- A direct line polynomial evaluates to `a` at `u` when `u` lies on the line
    33	and every parameter presenting `u` gives value `a`.  The universal clause
    34	keeps the zero-direction case explicit. -/
    35	def DirectEvaluatesTo {D : DirectLdParams} {c : ℕ} (line : DirectLineDesc D)
    36	    (f : DirectDegPoly D c) (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)
    37	    (a : DirectScalarQ D) : Prop :=
    38	  (∃ t : DirectScalarQ D, u = line.base + t • line.direction) ∧
    39	    ∀ t : DirectScalarQ D, u = line.base + t • line.direction →
    40	      evalCoefficient f t = a
    41	
    42	/-- Option-completed evaluation of a direct line polynomial.  `none` is an
    43	explicit outcome when the point does not determine an evaluation; no field
    44	value is used as a fallback. -/
    45	noncomputable def directEvalOpt {D : DirectLdParams} {c : ℕ}
    46	    (line : DirectLineDesc D) (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)
    47	    (f : DirectDegPoly D c) : Option (DirectScalarQ D) := by
    48	  classical
    49	  exact if h : ∃ a : DirectScalarQ D, DirectEvaluatesTo line f u a then
    50	    some (Classical.choose h)
    51	  else none

    53	/-- The typed question alphabet of the directly indexed game. -/
    54	abbrev DirectLdQuestion (D : DirectLdParams) := LdType × DirectLdSpace D

    56	/-- Canonicalize a common direct sample for one question type.  Irrelevant
    57	coordinates are fixed, so point questions reveal no sampled line index and
    58	axis-line questions reveal no diagonal direction. -/
    59	noncomputable def directLdMap (D : DirectLdParams) :
    60	    LdType → DirectLdSpace D → DirectLdSpace D
    61	  | .point, sample => ⟨sample.point, D.firstIndex, 0⟩
    62	  | .aline, sample =>
    63	      let direction := coordinateDirection sample.index
    64	      ⟨lineRepMap direction sample.point, sample.index, 0⟩
    65	  | .dline, sample =>
    66	      let direction := directPrefixProjection sample.index sample.direction
    67	      ⟨lineRepMap direction sample.point, sample.index, direction⟩

    69	/-- The directly indexed question distribution.  It has the same uniform
    70	ordered type-pair branches as `ldQuestionDistribution`, but its common sample
    71	contains an actual coordinate index rather than a field seed. -/
    72	noncomputable def directLdQuestionDistribution (D : DirectLdParams) :
    73	    Distribution (DirectLdQuestion D × DirectLdQuestion D) :=
    74	  (uniformDistribution ((LdType × LdType) × DirectLdSpace D)).map fun sample =>
    75	    ((sample.1.1, directLdMap D sample.1.1 sample.2),
    76	      (sample.1.2, directLdMap D sample.1.2 sample.2))

    78	/-- The directly indexed question law is probabilistic. -/
    79	theorem directLdQuestionDistribution_isProbability (D : DirectLdParams) :
    80	    (directLdQuestionDistribution D).IsProbability := by
    81	  exact (uniformDistribution_isProbability
    82	    ((LdType × LdType) × DirectLdSpace D)).map _

    84	/-- The answer alphabet of the directly indexed game. -/
    85	inductive DirectLdAnswer (D : DirectLdParams) where
    86	  | pointVals (a : Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D)
    87	  | alinePolys (a : Fin D.k → Fin (D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)
    88	  | dlinePolys (a : Fin D.k → Fin (D.m * D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)
    89	  deriving DecidableEq

    91	/-- A finite code for the directly indexed answer alphabet. -/
    92	abbrev DirectLdAnswerCode (D : DirectLdParams) :=
    93	  (Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D) ⊕
    94	    ((Fin D.k → Fin (D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D) ⊕
    95	      (Fin D.k → Fin (D.m * D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D))
    96	
    97	/-- Constructor-preserving equivalence between the inductive answer type and
    98	its finite code. -/
    99	noncomputable def directLdAnswerEquiv (D : DirectLdParams) :
   100	    DirectLdAnswer D ≃ DirectLdAnswerCode D where
   101	  toFun
   102	    | .pointVals a => .inl a
   103	    | .alinePolys a => .inr (.inl a)
   104	    | .dlinePolys a => .inr (.inr a)
   105	  invFun
   106	    | .inl a => .pointVals a
   107	    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePolys a
   108	    | .inr (.inr a) => .dlinePolys a
   109	  left_inv := by intro answer; cases answer <;> rfl
   110	  right_inv := by
   111	    intro answer
   112	    rcases answer with a | a
   113	    · rfl
   114	    · rcases a with a | a <;> rfl

   122	/-- Check that a direct-game answer has the constructor required by its

   124	def validDirectLdAnswer {D : DirectLdParams} (t : LdType)
   125	    (answer : DirectLdAnswer D) : Bool :=
   126	  match t, answer with
   127	  | .point, .pointVals _ => true
   128	  | .aline, .alinePolys _ => true
   129	  | .dline, .dlinePolys _ => true

   132	/-- The directly indexed axis-line versus point acceptance relation. -/
   133	def directAlinePointCondition (D : DirectLdParams)
   134	    (line point : DirectLdSpace D)
   135	    (f : Fin D.k → Fin (D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)
   136	    (a : Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D) : Prop :=
   137	  ∀ t : DirectScalarQ D,
   138	    point.point = line.point + t • coordinateDirection line.index →
   139	      ∀ j : Fin D.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j

   141	/-- The directly indexed diagonal-line versus point acceptance relation. -/
   142	def directDlinePointCondition (D : DirectLdParams)
   143	    (line point : DirectLdSpace D)
   144	    (f : Fin D.k → Fin (D.m * D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)
   145	    (a : Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D) : Prop :=
   146	  ∀ t : DirectScalarQ D,
   147	    point.point = line.point + t • line.direction →
   148	      ∀ j : Fin D.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j

   150	/-- The directly indexed low-degree win predicate.  It differs from
   151	`ldWinPredicate` only by reading the coordinate index directly from each line
   152	question. -/
   153	noncomputable def directLdWinPredicate (D : DirectLdParams) :
   154	    DirectLdQuestion D → DirectLdQuestion D →
   155	      DirectLdAnswer D → DirectLdAnswer D → Bool :=
   156	  open Classical in
   157	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   158	    if validDirectLdAnswer tA a && validDirectLdAnswer tB b then
   159	      match tA, tB, a, b with
   160	      | .point, .point, .pointVals u, .pointVals v => decide (u = v)
   161	      | .aline, .point, .alinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   162	          decide (directAlinePointCondition D xA xB f u)
   163	      | .point, .aline, .pointVals u, .alinePolys f =>
   164	          decide (directAlinePointCondition D xB xA f u)
   165	      | .dline, .point, .dlinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   166	          decide (directDlinePointCondition D xA xB f u)
   167	      | .point, .dline, .pointVals u, .dlinePolys f =>
   168	          decide (directDlinePointCondition D xB xA f u)
   169	      | .aline, .aline, .alinePolys f, .alinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   170	      | .dline, .dline, .dlinePolys f, .dlinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   171	      | _, _, _, _ => true
   172	    else false

   182	  μ := directLdQuestionDistribution D

   222	The function $L_\ALine$ is the concatenation of the $1$-level CL function that

   230	Define $L_\DLine$ to be the following $3$-level CL function: for all $(u,s,v) \in

   234		L_\DLine(u,s,v) = (L^\lnf_{\pi_{i-1}(v)}(u),s,\pi_{i-1}(v))

   237	The function $L_\DLine$ is the concatenation of the following CL functions (again, see \Cref{lem:cl-concat} for definition of CL function concatenation): (i) the identity function on $V_{\coord}$ (which is a $1$-level CL function); (ii) for every $i \in \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$ the $1$-level CL function on $V_{\dir{}}$ that maps $v \mapsto \pi_{i-1}(v)$ (i.e.~it zeroes out the first $i-1$ coordinates of $v$), and (iii) for every pair $(s,v') \in V_\coord \oplus V_{\dir{}}$, the $1$-level CL function $L^\lnf_{v'}$ acting on $V_\xpt$.    240	The following two lemmas establish that the CL functions
   241	$L_\Point,L_\ALine,L_\DLine$ give rise to the axis-parallel line-versus-point and
   242	diagonal line-versus-point distributions.
   243	\begin{lemma}
   244		\label{lem:alnf}
   245		Consider the pair $(\line, u)$ sampled in the following way: first, sample the
   246	  tuple $((u_0,s,0),(u,0,0))$ from the CL distribution $\mu_{L_\ALine,L_\Point}$,
   247	  and let $\line = \line(u_0,e_i)$ where $i = \chi(s)$.
   248	  Then $u$ is a uniformly random point in $\F_q^m$ and $\line$ is a line that
   249	  goes through $u$ and is parallel to a uniformly random axis $i \in
   250	  \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$.
   251	\end{lemma}
   252	\begin{proof}
   253		Since $s$ is uniformly random in $\F_q$ and $m$ divides $q$ by assumption, we
   254	  have that $i$ is uniformly random between $\{1,2,\ldots,m\}$ and therefore
   255	  $(u_0,s)$ specifies a uniformly random axis-parallel line $\line(u_0,e_i)$.
   256	  Since $u_0 = L^{\lnf}_{e_i}(u)$, we have that $u \in \line(u_0,e_i)$.
   257	\end{proof}

   320	\paragraph{Decision procedure} The decision procedure $\decider^\ld$ for the
   321	game $\game^\ld$ is presented in Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider}.
   322	The table at the top specifies a parsing scheme for the questions and answers,
   323	depending on the type of question.
   324	For example, when a player receives a question with type $\Point$, the question
   325	content $x$, a bit string of length $m \log q$, should be interpreted by the
   326	decision procedure and the players as an element of the vector space $\F_q^m$,
   327	as indicated in Section~\ref{sec:ff-representations}.
   328	Similarly the answer to a question with type $\Point$ is expected to be a bit
   329	string of length $\ldc \log q$, and is interpreted as an element of $\F_q^\ldc$.
   330	For questions with type $\ALine$, the question content is a $(m \log q + \log
   331	q)$-bit string, which is parsed as a pair $(u_0, s) \in \F_q^m \times \F_q$,
   332	which in turn can be interpreted as a specification for an axis-parallel line
   333	$\line(u_0,e_i)$ in $\F_q^m$ where $i = \chi(s)$, as described in
   334	\Cref{lem:alnf}.
   335	The answer is interpreted as the description of $\ldc$ degree-$d$ univariate
   336	polynomials defined on the line $\line(u_0,e_i)$, each polynomial given by a
   337	list of $d+1$ coefficients.
   338	For questions with type $\DLine$, the question content is a $(2m \log q + \log
   339	q)$-bit string, which is parsed as a triple $(u_0, s, v) \in \F_q^m \times \F_q
   340	\times \F_q^m$ that specifies a diagonal line $\line(u_0,v')$ where $v' =
   341	\pi_{i-1}(v)$ as described in \Cref{lem:dlnf}.
   342	The answer is interpreted as the description of $\ldc$ degree-$md$ univariate
   343	polynomials defined on the line $\line(u_0,v')$.

   345	procedure rejects.

   394	We define a special class of measurements that are relevant to the soundness
   395	properties of the low-degree test.
   396	
   397	\begin{definition}[Low-degree polynomial measurements]
   398	  \label{def:ld-meas}
   399	  Define $\polymeas{m}{d}{q}$ to be the set of POVM measurements whose outcomes
   400	  correspond to (individual) degree-$d$ polynomials of $m$ variables over
   401	  $\F_q$.
   402	  More generally, for an integer $\ldc$ and tuples $m=(m_1, m_2, \ldots,
   403	  m_\ldc)$, $d=(d_1, d_2, \ldots, d_\ldc)$ and $q=(q_1, q_2, \ldots, q_\ldc)$,
   404	  we let $\simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ldc}$ be the set of measurements $G =
   405	  \{G_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots\,,\, g_\ldc}\}$ such that for $i\in\{1, 2, \ldots,
   406	  \ldc\}$, $g_i$ is a polynomial $g_i:\F_{q_i}^{m_i} \rightarrow
   407	  \F_{q_i}$ with individual degree $d_i$ (see \Cref{sec:ld-encoding} for a definition of individual degree). 
   408	\end{definition}
   409	
   410	Quantum soundness of a version of the classical low-degree test for polynomials of low \emph{total} degree was claimed
   411	in~\cite{natarajan2018low}, building on an analysis of a three-prover version of the test in~\cite{vidick2016three}. Unfortunately there is a gap in the soundness analysis of this test. For our construction we use the low individual degree test, whose quantum soundness is shown in~\cite{ML20} and generalized in~\cite{ji2021quantum}. We state the result in the form that is most directly useful for us, and show how the stated result follows from~\cite{ji2021quantum}.
   412	
   413	\begin{theorem}[Quantum soundness of the simultaneous classical low-degree test]
   414	  \label{lem:ld-soundness}
   415	  There exists a function $\delta_{\ld}(\eps, q, m, d, \ldc) = a (dm \ldc)^a (\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$ for universal constants $a\geq 1$ and $0<b\leq 1$ 
   416	such that the following
   417	  holds.
   418	  For all $\eps > 0$ and parameter tuple $\ldparams = (q, m, d, \ldc)$, for all
   419	  projective strategies $(\psi,A,B)$ that succeed with probability at least
   420	  $1-\eps$ in the game $\game^\ld_\ldparams$, there exists measurements
   421	  \[G^w \in \simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ldc}\] on $\mH_w$, for
   422	  $w\in\{\alice,\bob\}$, such that
   423	  \begin{equation*}

   291	\section{Candidate repairs}
   292	
   293	\paragraph{Direct index sampling (candidate direction, recommended).}
   294	Define, for arbitrary $m' \ge 1$, the line-point distribution over
   295	$\F_q^{m'}$ that samples the uniform point, the uniform axis index
   296	$i \in \{1,\ldots,m'\}$, and the diagonal direction with vanishing first
   297	$i-1$ coordinates, directly; define the \emph{directly indexed game} with
   298	this question distribution, whose line questions carry the index $i$ (and,
   299	for diagonal lines, the projected direction) in place of the seed
   300	$s \in \F_q$; and state the imported soundness theorem for that game
   301	(form~4 above).  This removes the divisibility obstruction and nothing
   302	else: the directly indexed game still asks for polynomials on revealed
   303	lines, has no pair questions, and weighs its branches as the present game
   304	does, so establishing form~4 carries the same two import obligations as
   305	the $\chi$-based import (Section~\ref{sec:import-obligations}), now at
   306	arbitrary dimension.
   307	
   308	The relation to the present game when $m' \mid q$ must moreover be proved
   309	at the level of games, not merely of question distributions, because the
   310	two games have different question alphabets: an $\mathsf{ALine}$ question
   311	of the $\chi$-based game is a pair $(u_0, s)$ and a $\mathsf{DLine}$
   312	question a triple $(u_0, s, v')$, so a strategy may select different
   313	measurements for seeds $s \ne s'$ with $\chi(s) = \chi(s')$, and equality
   314	of the induced laws of the geometric data does not by itself transport
   315	such a strategy.  The transport layer decomposes into the following
   316	obligations, none of which is carried out here.
   317	\begin{itemize}
   318	  \item \emph{Distribution lemma.}  When $m' \mid q$, the image of the
   319	  conditionally linear question distribution under the parsing map
   320	  $(u_0,s) \mapsto (u_0,\chi(s))$, $(u_0,s,v') \mapsto (u_0,\chi(s),v')$
   321	  is the direct distribution, and conditioned on the parsed question the
   322	  seed is uniform on the class $\chi^{-1}(i)$, independently of everything
   323	  else.
   324	  \item \emph{Parsing pullback.}  A strategy for the directly indexed game
   325	  composed with the parsing map is a seed-oblivious strategy for the
   326	  $\chi$-based game.  Since the win predicate depends on the question only
   327	  through the parsed data, and a seed-oblivious strategy answers
   328	  identically across each fiber --- in particular on the synchronicity
   329	  branches, where both players hold the same seed --- the value should be
   330	  preserved exactly on every branch, and projectivity is preserved.  This
   331	  is the direction the combining subtree needs.
   332	  \item \emph{Seed-fiber averaging: what it preserves and what it does
   333	  not.}  In the opposite direction, average each line measurement over its
   334	  seed fiber: attach to a direct question $(u_0,i)$, respectively
   335	  $(u_0,i,v')$, the average over uniform $s \in \chi^{-1}(i)$ of the
   336	  measurements attached to $(u_0,s)$, respectively $(u_0,s,v')$, leaving
   337	  the points measurements unchanged.  By the conditional uniformity of the
   338	  seed this preserves the value of every \emph{line-versus-point} branch
   339	  exactly: there the paired question carries no seed, so the branch value
   340	  is an average over the fiber of per-seed values, which the averaged
   341	  measurement computes.  It does \emph{not} preserve the synchronicity
   342	  branches.  There both players hold the same seed, so the $\chi$-based
   343	  branch value is the diagonal average
   344	  $\E_{s}\sum_f \langle M^{(u_0,s)}_f \ot \widetilde M^{(u_0,s)}_f
   345	  \rangle$, while the averaged strategy realizes the double average
   346	  $\E_{s,s'}\sum_f \langle M^{(u_0,s)}_f \ot \widetilde M^{(u_0,s')}_f
   347	  \rangle$ over independent seeds in the fiber; the two differ whenever
   348	  the players' measurements vary across a fiber in a correlated way (if
   349	  both apply a common seed-dependent relabelling, every diagonal term is
   350	  large and the cross terms are not), and neither quantity dominates the
   351	  other in general.  An earlier revision of this note claimed that the
   352	  averaging preserves the exact value, and with it synchronicity; that
   353	  claim was wrong and is withdrawn.  What needs proof is control of the
   354	  synchronicity branches under de-seeding.  Candidate approaches: show
   355	  that a strategy of value $1-\eps$ in the $\chi$-based game is, with
   356	  polynomial loss, close to a seed-oblivious one; or state form~4 with a
   357	  synchronicity hypothesis in the doubled-average form and re-derive it on
   358	  the tensor-code side.  Choosing and proving one of these is an open
   359	  obligation.
   360	  \item \emph{Projectivity round trip.}  The averaged strategy is a POVM
   361	  strategy even when the given one is projective, while the imported
   362	  theorem, like the present one, takes projective strategies.  The
   363	  intended round trip is: dilate the averaged strategy to a projective one
   364	  (Naimark preserves all product correlations
   365	  $\langle X \ot Y \rangle$ of the given strategy against the dilated
   366	  state --- hence the value of every branch the averaging preserved ---
   367	  but nothing restores the diagonal seed correlations once the averaging
   368	  has been performed); apply form~4; and compress the resulting polynomial
   369	  measurement along the dilation isometry back to a POVM in the required
   370	  measurement class on the original space.  That this compression
   371	  preserves the consistency conclusions must itself be proved; it is
   372	  stated here as an obligation, not established.  (Alternatively, form~4
   373	  may be stated for POVM strategies outright, moving the dilation inside
   374	  the import.)
   375	\end{itemize}

   399	\paragraph{Padding the dimension.}
   400	Alternatively, embed the combined polynomial into
   401	$\mathrm{ideg}_{d,\bar m}(\F_q)$ for $\bar m = 4m$, the least power of two
   402	with $\bar m \ge 2m+2$, ignoring the $2m-2$ dummy variables.  Then
   403	$\bar m \mid q$ holds whenever $q \ge 4m$, and the existing game applies at
   404	dimension $\bar m$.  In the complementary regime $m \in \{q/2,\, q\}$ the
   405	conclusion is vacuous: $md \ge q/2$ gives
   406	$\delta_S \ge a(md)^a q^{-b} \ge a\,2^{-a} q^{a-b} \ge a\,2^{-b} \ge 1$
   407	for $a \ge 2$, while the consistency quantities bounded by the theorem never
   408	exceed $1$.  This route stays inside the present definitions but reworks the
   409	sub-line distribution (a fourth coordinate block of dummies), the combining
   410	map, and the wrong-block Schwartz--Zippel analysis, and it moves the
   411	combining lemmas away from their source statements at dimension $2m+2$.
   412	
   413	\paragraph{Unequal index classes.}
   414	One could instead define an index function at dimension $2m+2$ with classes
   415	of sizes $\lfloor q/(2m+2)\rfloor$ and $\lceil q/(2m+2)\rceil$.  The index

   417	test fails exactly, and every distributional identity in the sub-line
   418	analysis acquires an error term; this amounts to re-proving the imported
   419	soundness theorem for a perturbed game and is not recommended.

    71	An important class of strategies are those which are \emph{symmetric}.

    88				For each $\ell$, $B^{\ell}$ is a projective measurement on~$\calH$.

    90				and univariate degree-$md$ polynomial $f:\ell\rightarrow \F_q$.

   313	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   314	-/
   315	noncomputable def ldWinPredicate (P : LdParams) :
   316	    LdQuestion P → LdQuestion P → LdAnswer P → LdAnswer P → Bool :=
   317	  open Classical in
   318	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   319	      if validLdAnswer tA a && validLdAnswer tB b then
   320	        match tA, tB, a, b with
   321	        | .point, .point, .pointVals u, .pointVals v => decide (u = v)
   322	        | .aline, .point, .alinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   323	            decide (alinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   324	        | .point, .aline, .pointVals u, .alinePolys f =>
   325	            decide (alinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   326	        | .dline, .point, .dlinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   327	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   328	        | .point, .dline, .pointVals u, .dlinePolys f =>
   329	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   330	        | .aline, .aline, .alinePolys f, .alinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   331	        | .dline, .dline, .dlinePolys f, .dlinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   332	        | _, _, _, _ => true
   333	      else false
   334	
   335	/-- The low-degree game packaged as a `Game`.  This is `def:ld-game` in
   336	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, paper origin
   337	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   338	-/
   339	noncomputable def ldGame (P : LdParams) : Game where
   340	  QuestionA := LdQuestion P
   341	  QuestionB := LdQuestion P
   342	  AnswerA := LdAnswer P
   343	  AnswerB := LdAnswer P
   344	  μ := ldQuestionDistribution P
   345	  μ_prob := by sorry
   346	  decide := ldWinPredicate P
   347	
   348	end

    29	/-- Regard direct-game parameters as parameters of the mature LDT interface.
    30	The field size, dimension, and degree are unchanged. -/
    31	@[reducible] def DirectLdParams.toLDTParameters (D : DirectLdParams) : Parameters where
    32	  m := D.m
    33	  q := D.q
    34	  d := D.d
    35	  hm := lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one D.hm
    36	  hq := by
    37	    obtain ⟨n, hn, hq⟩ := D.hq
    38	    rw [hq]
    39	    exact Nat.pow_pos (by decide)
    40	  hqPrimePower := by
    41	    obtain ⟨n, hn, hq⟩ := D.hq
    42	    exact ⟨2, n, Nat.prime_two, hn.pos, hq⟩

    44	/-- The fixed QPBT field model, viewed as the model used by the mature LDT

    50	/-- Coordinate coding from the direct scalar field to the mature LDT carrier. -/
    51	noncomputable def directScalarEquiv (D : DirectLdParams) :
    52	    DirectScalarQ D ≃ Fq D.toLDTParameters :=
    53	  binaryRepresentation D.model
    54	
    55	/-- Coordinate coding identifies direct points with mature LDT points, with
    56	the coordinate order reversed: direct coordinate `j` is mature coordinate
    57	`Fin.rev j`.  The direct game zeroes a *prefix* of a sampled diagonal
    58	direction (`directPrefixProjection`, paper equation `eq:cl-dlnf`), whereas
    59	the mature test zeroes a *suffix* (`extendRestrictedDirection`,
    60	`references/ldt-paper/test_definition.tex:49-65`).  Reversing the coordinate
    61	order aligns the two restriction conventions, as required by the game
    62	correspondence in `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`. -/
    63	noncomputable def directPointEquiv (D : DirectLdParams) :
    64	    (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) ≃ Point D.toLDTParameters where
    65	  toFun u i := directScalarEquiv D (u (Fin.rev i))
    66	  invFun u j := (directScalarEquiv D).symm (u (Fin.rev j))
    67	  left_inv u := by
    68	    funext j
    69	    simp
    70	  right_inv u := by
    71	    funext i
    72	    simp

    76	    directPointEquiv D u i = directScalarEquiv D (u (Fin.rev i)) :=

    80	    (u : Point D.toLDTParameters) (j : Fin D.m) :
    81	    (directPointEquiv D).symm u j =
    82	      (directScalarEquiv D).symm (u (Fin.rev j)) :=
    83	  rfl

    85	/-! ## Bounded coefficient vectors -/
    86	
    87	/-- Turn a coefficient vector into its polynomial of degree at most `n`. -/
    88	private noncomputable def coefficientPolynomial
    89	    {K : Type*} [Field K] (n : ℕ) (c : Fin (n + 1) → K) : Polynomial K :=
    90	  ((Polynomial.degreeLTEquiv K (n + 1)).symm c).1
    91	
    92	private theorem coefficientPolynomial_degree_le
    93	    {K : Type*} [Field K] (n : ℕ) (c : Fin (n + 1) → K) :
    94	    (coefficientPolynomial n c).natDegree ≤ n := by
    95	  let p := (Polynomial.degreeLTEquiv K (n + 1)).symm c
    96	  have hp : p.1 ∈ Polynomial.degreeLE K n := by
    97	    rw [← Polynomial.degreeLT_succ_eq_degreeLE]
    98	    exact p.2
    99	  have hdegree : p.1.degree ≤ n := Polynomial.mem_degreeLE.mp hp
   100	  by_cases hzero : p.1 = 0
   101	  · simp [coefficientPolynomial, p, hzero]
   102	  · exact Polynomial.natDegree_le_iff_degree_le.mpr hdegree
   103	
   104	@[simp] private theorem coefficientPolynomial_coeff
   105	    {K : Type*} [Field K] (n : ℕ) (c : Fin (n + 1) → K)
   106	    (i : Fin (n + 1)) :
   107	    (coefficientPolynomial n c).coeff i = c i := by
   108	  exact congrFun ((Polynomial.degreeLTEquiv K (n + 1)).apply_symm_apply c) i
   109	
   110	private theorem coefficientPolynomial_eval
   111	    {K : Type*} [Field K] (n : ℕ) (c : Fin (n + 1) → K) (t : K) :
   112	    (coefficientPolynomial n c).eval t = evalCoefficient c t := by
   113	  simpa [coefficientPolynomial, evalCoefficient] using
   114	    (Polynomial.eval_eq_sum_degreeLTEquiv
   115	      (((Polynomial.degreeLTEquiv K (n + 1)).symm c).2) t)
   116	
   117	/-- Direct axis-line coefficients are equivalent to mature bounded axis-line
   118	polynomials over the fixed field model. -/
   119	noncomputable def directAxisAnswerEquiv (D : DirectLdParams) :
   120	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   121	    DirectDegPoly D D.d ≃ AxisLinePolynomial D.toLDTParameters := by
   122	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   123	  refine
   124	    { toFun := fun c =>
   125	        { poly := coefficientPolynomial D.d c
   126	          degreeBounded := coefficientPolynomial_degree_le D.d c }
   127	      invFun := fun f i => f.poly.coeff i
   128	      left_inv := ?_
   129	      right_inv := ?_ }
   130	  · intro c
   131	    funext i
   132	    exact coefficientPolynomial_coeff D.d c i
   133	  · intro f
   134	    apply AxisLinePolynomial.ext
   135	    apply linePolynomial_coeff_fin_injective D.toLDTParameters
   136	      (coefficientPolynomial_degree_le D.d fun i => f.poly.coeff i)
   137	      f.degreeBounded
   138	    intro i
   139	    exact coefficientPolynomial_coeff D.d (fun j => f.poly.coeff j) i
   140	
   141	/-- Direct diagonal-line coefficients are equivalent to mature bounded
   142	diagonal-line polynomials over the fixed field model. -/
   143	noncomputable def directDiagonalAnswerEquiv (D : DirectLdParams) :
   144	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   145	    DirectDegPoly D (D.m * D.d) ≃ DiagonalLinePolynomial D.toLDTParameters := by
   146	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   147	  refine
   148	    { toFun := fun c =>
   149	        { poly := coefficientPolynomial (D.m * D.d) c
   150	          degreeBounded := coefficientPolynomial_degree_le (D.m * D.d) c }
   151	      invFun := fun f i => f.poly.coeff i
   152	      left_inv := ?_
   153	      right_inv := ?_ }
   154	  · intro c
   155	    funext i
   156	    exact coefficientPolynomial_coeff (D.m * D.d) c i
   157	  · intro f
   158	    apply DiagonalLinePolynomial.ext
   159	    apply linePolynomial_coeff_fin_injective D.toLDTParameters
   160	      (coefficientPolynomial_degree_le (D.m * D.d) fun i => f.poly.coeff i)
   161	      f.degreeBounded
   162	    intro i
   163	    exact coefficientPolynomial_coeff (D.m * D.d) (fun j => f.poly.coeff j) i
   164	
   165	/-- Coefficient evaluation agrees with evaluation of the corresponding mature
   166	axis-line polynomial. -/
   167	theorem directAxisAnswerEquiv_apply (D : DirectLdParams)
   168	    (c : DirectDegPoly D D.d) (t : DirectScalarQ D) :
   169	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   170	    directAxisAnswerEquiv D c (directScalarEquiv D t) =
   171	      directScalarEquiv D (evalCoefficient c t) := by
   172	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   173	  simp only [directAxisAnswerEquiv, AxisLinePolynomial.toFun,
   174	    evalLinePolynomialModel]
   175	  rw [show decodeScalar (directScalarEquiv D t) = t by
   176	    exact (FieldModel.equiv (q := D.q)).symm_apply_apply t]
   177	  change encodeScalar ((coefficientPolynomial D.d c).eval t) =
   178	    directScalarEquiv D (evalCoefficient c t)
   179	  exact congrArg (FieldModel.equiv (q := D.q))
   180	    (coefficientPolynomial_eval D.d c t)
   181	
   182	/-- Coefficient evaluation agrees with evaluation of the corresponding mature
   183	diagonal-line polynomial. -/
   184	theorem directDiagonalAnswerEquiv_apply (D : DirectLdParams)
   185	    (c : DirectDegPoly D (D.m * D.d)) (t : DirectScalarQ D) :
   186	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   187	    directDiagonalAnswerEquiv D c (directScalarEquiv D t) =
   188	      directScalarEquiv D (evalCoefficient c t) := by
   189	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   190	  simp only [directDiagonalAnswerEquiv, DiagonalLinePolynomial.toFun,
   191	    evalLinePolynomialModel]
   192	  rw [show decodeScalar (directScalarEquiv D t) = t by
   193	    exact (FieldModel.equiv (q := D.q)).symm_apply_apply t]
   194	  change encodeScalar ((coefficientPolynomial (D.m * D.d) c).eval t) =
   195	    directScalarEquiv D (evalCoefficient c t)
   196	  exact congrArg (FieldModel.equiv (q := D.q))
   197	    (coefficientPolynomial_eval (D.m * D.d) c t)

   201	/-- Forget the divisibility field and expose the directly indexed parameters. -/
   202	def LdParams.toDirectLdParams (L : LdParams) : DirectLdParams where
   203	  q := L.q
   204	  m := L.m
   205	  d := L.d
   206	  k := L.k
   207	  hm := L.hm
   208	  hd := L.hd
   209	  hk := L.hk
   210	  hq := L.hq

   212	@[simp] theorem LdParams.toDirectLdParams_model (L : LdParams) :
   213	    L.toDirectLdParams.model = L.model := by
   214	  unfold DirectLdParams.model LdParams.model LdParams.toDirectLdParams
   215	  congr
   216	
   217	/-- The positive cardinality of every seed-fiber residue type. -/
   218	theorem LdParams.seedFiberCard_pos (L : LdParams) : 0 < L.q / L.m := by
   219	  exact Nat.div_pos (Nat.le_of_dvd (by
   220	    obtain ⟨n, hn, hq⟩ := L.hq
   221	    rw [hq]
   222	    exact Nat.pow_pos (by decide)) L.hdvd) L.hm
   223	
   224	/-- Divisibility identifies the field cardinality with the product of the
   225	index cardinality and the common fiber cardinality. -/
   226	theorem LdParams.seedFiberProduct_eq (L : LdParams) :
   227	    L.q = L.m * (L.q / L.m) :=
   228	  (Nat.mul_div_cancel' L.hdvd).symm
   229	
   230	/-- Casting between equal finite cardinalities preserves the underlying
   231	natural-number representative. -/
   232	@[simp] private theorem equivCastFin_val {m n : ℕ} (h : m = n) (i : Fin m) :
   233	    (Equiv.cast (congrArg Fin h) i).val = i.val := by
   234	  subst n
   235	  rfl
   236	
   237	/-- A field seed is uniquely a coordinate index and a residue in its equal
   238	`chiIndex` fiber. -/
   239	noncomputable def seedFiberEquiv (L : LdParams) :
   240	    ScalarQ L ≃ Fin L.m × Fin (L.q / L.m) :=
   241	  (binaryRepresentation L.model).trans <|
   242	    (Equiv.cast <| congrArg Fin L.seedFiberProduct_eq).trans
   243	      finProdFinEquiv.symm
   244	
   245	@[simp] theorem seedFiberEquiv_fst (L : LdParams) (s : ScalarQ L) :
   246	    (seedFiberEquiv L s).1 = chiIndex L s := by
   247	  letI : NeZero L.m := ⟨Nat.ne_of_gt (lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one L.hm)⟩
   248	  have hquot : (binaryRepresentation L.model s).val / (L.q / L.m) < L.m := by
   249	    apply (Nat.div_lt_iff_lt_mul L.seedFiberCard_pos).mpr
   250	    rw [Nat.mul_div_cancel' L.hdvd]
   251	    exact (binaryRepresentation L.model s).isLt
   252	  simp only [seedFiberEquiv, Equiv.trans_apply]
   253	  apply Fin.ext
   254	  change
   255	    (Equiv.cast (congrArg Fin L.seedFiberProduct_eq)
   256	      (binaryRepresentation L.model s)).val / (L.q / L.m) =
   257	      (Fin.ofNat L.m ((binaryRepresentation L.model s).val / (L.q / L.m))).val
   258	  rw [equivCastFin_val]
   259	  · exact (Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hquot).symm
   260	  · exact L.seedFiberProduct_eq
   261	
   262	/-- Reconstruct the seed belonging to a coordinate and its fiber residue. -/
   263	noncomputable def seedOfIndexResidue (L : LdParams)
   264	    (i : Fin L.m) (r : Fin (L.q / L.m)) : ScalarQ L :=
   265	  (seedFiberEquiv L).symm (i, r)
   266	
   267	@[simp] theorem seedFiberEquiv_seedOfIndexResidue (L : LdParams)
   268	    (i : Fin L.m) (r : Fin (L.q / L.m)) :
   269	    seedFiberEquiv L (seedOfIndexResidue L i r) = (i, r) :=
   270	  (seedFiberEquiv L).apply_symm_apply (i, r)
   271	
   272	@[simp] theorem chiIndex_seedOfIndexResidue (L : LdParams)
   273	    (i : Fin L.m) (r : Fin (L.q / L.m)) :
   274	    chiIndex L (seedOfIndexResidue L i r) = i := by
   275	  rw [← seedFiberEquiv_fst]
   276	  simp

   278	/-- Constructor-preserving equivalence between answers of the seed-indexed
   279	and directly indexed QPBT games. -/
   280	noncomputable def ldDirectAnswerEquiv (L : LdParams) :
   281	    LdAnswer L ≃ DirectLdAnswer L.toDirectLdParams where
   282	  toFun
   283	    | .pointVals a => .pointVals a
   284	    | .alinePolys a => .alinePolys a
   285	    | .dlinePolys a => .dlinePolys a
   286	  invFun
   287	    | .pointVals a => .pointVals a
   288	    | .alinePolys a => .alinePolys a
   289	    | .dlinePolys a => .dlinePolys a
   290	  left_inv a := by cases a <;> rfl
   291	  right_inv a := by cases a <;> rfl

   293	/-! ## Parsing seed-indexed questions -/
   294	
   295	/-- Parse a seed-indexed question into the directly indexed question carrying
   296	the coordinate selected by `chiIndex`. -/
   297	noncomputable def parseLdQuestion (L : LdParams) :
   298	    LdQuestion L → DirectLdQuestion L.toDirectLdParams
   299	  | (.point, z) =>
   300	      (.point, ⟨z.point, L.toDirectLdParams.firstIndex, 0⟩)
   301	  | (.aline, z) =>
   302	      (.aline, ⟨z.point, chiIndex L z.seed, 0⟩)
   303	  | (.dline, z) =>
   304	      (.dline, ⟨z.point, chiIndex L z.seed, z.direction⟩)
   305	
   306	/-- Embed a direct sample into the seed-indexed ambient space using the
   307	specified residue in the selected seed fiber. -/
   308	noncomputable def ldSpaceOfDirectResidue (L : LdParams)
   309	    (sample : DirectLdSpace L.toDirectLdParams)
   310	    (residue : Fin (L.q / L.m)) : LdSpace L
   311	  | .inl (.inl i) => sample.point i
   312	  | .inl (.inr _) => seedOfIndexResidue L sample.index residue
   313	  | .inr i => sample.direction i
   314	
   315	@[simp] theorem ldSpaceOfDirectResidue_point (L : LdParams)
   316	    (sample : DirectLdSpace L.toDirectLdParams)
   317	    (residue : Fin (L.q / L.m)) :
   318	    (ldSpaceOfDirectResidue L sample residue).point = sample.point :=
   319	  rfl
   320	
   321	@[simp] theorem ldSpaceOfDirectResidue_seed (L : LdParams)
   322	    (sample : DirectLdSpace L.toDirectLdParams)
   323	    (residue : Fin (L.q / L.m)) :
   324	    (ldSpaceOfDirectResidue L sample residue).seed =
   325	      seedOfIndexResidue L sample.index residue :=
   326	  rfl
   327	
   328	@[simp] theorem ldSpaceOfDirectResidue_direction (L : LdParams)
   329	    (sample : DirectLdSpace L.toDirectLdParams)
   330	    (residue : Fin (L.q / L.m)) :
   331	    (ldSpaceOfDirectResidue L sample residue).direction = sample.direction :=
   332	  rfl
   333	
   334	/-- The ambient seed-indexed sample space is a direct sample together with a
   335	uniform residue in the selected seed fiber. -/
   336	noncomputable def ldSpaceSeedFiberEquiv (L : LdParams) :
   337	    LdSpace L ≃ DirectLdSpace L.toDirectLdParams × Fin (L.q / L.m) where
   338	  toFun z :=
   339	    (⟨z.point, (seedFiberEquiv L z.seed).1, z.direction⟩,
   340	      (seedFiberEquiv L z.seed).2)
   341	  invFun x := ldSpaceOfDirectResidue L x.1 x.2
   342	  left_inv z := by
   343	    funext i
   344	    rcases i with (i | i)
   345	    · rcases i with (i | i)
   346	      · rfl
   347	      · rcases i with ⟨⟩
   348	        change (seedFiberEquiv L).symm (seedFiberEquiv L z.seed) = z.seed
   349	        exact (seedFiberEquiv L).symm_apply_apply z.seed
   350	    · rfl
   351	  right_inv x := by
   352	    rcases x with ⟨sample, residue⟩
   353	    apply Prod.ext
   354	    · cases sample with
   355	      | mk point index direction =>
   356	          simp only [ldSpaceOfDirectResidue_point,
   357	            ldSpaceOfDirectResidue_seed, ldSpaceOfDirectResidue_direction]
   358	          rw [seedFiberEquiv_seedOfIndexResidue]
   359	    · simp [seedOfIndexResidue]

   361	/-- Parsing a canonical seed-indexed question reconstructed from a direct
   362	sample gives exactly the corresponding direct canonical question. -/
   363	theorem parseLdQuestion_ldCL_ofDirectResidue (L : LdParams)
   364	    (t : LdType) (sample : DirectLdSpace L.toDirectLdParams)
   365	    (residue : Fin (L.q / L.m)) :
   366	    parseLdQuestion L
   367	        (t, ldCL L t (ldSpaceOfDirectResidue L sample residue)) =
   368	      (t, directLdMap L.toDirectLdParams t sample) := by
   369	  cases t with
   370	  | point =>
   371	    rfl
   372	  | aline =>
   373	      ext <;>
   374	        simp only [parseLdQuestion, ldCL, ldALineCL, directLdMap,
   375	          ldSpaceOfDirectResidue, ldSpaceOfDirectResidue_point, LdSpace.seed,
   376	          chiIndex_seedOfIndexResidue]
   377	      congr 1
   378	  | dline =>
   379	      ext <;>
   380	        simp only [parseLdQuestion, ldCL, ldDLineCL, directLdMap,
   381	          ldSpaceOfDirectResidue, ldSpaceOfDirectResidue_point,
   382	          ldSpaceOfDirectResidue_direction, LdSpace.seed,
   383	          LdSpace.direction, chiIndex_seedOfIndexResidue,
   384	          prefixProjection]
   385	      rfl

   387	/-- The seed-indexed and direct predicates agree after parsing questions and
   388	transporting answers. -/
   389	theorem ldWinPredicate_parse (L : LdParams)
   390	    (x y : LdQuestion L) (a b : LdAnswer L) :
   391	    directLdWinPredicate L.toDirectLdParams
   392	        (parseLdQuestion L x) (parseLdQuestion L y)
   393	        (ldDirectAnswerEquiv L a) (ldDirectAnswerEquiv L b) =
   394	      ldWinPredicate L x y a b := by
   395	  rcases x with ⟨tx, x⟩
   396	  rcases y with ⟨ty, y⟩
   397	  cases tx <;> cases ty <;> cases a <;> cases b <;> rfl

   399	/-! ## Exact question-law transport -/
   400	
   401	/-- The common source sample is a direct common sample together with its
   402	uniform seed-fiber residue. -/
   403	noncomputable def ldQuestionSeedFiberEquiv (L : LdParams) :
   404	    ((LdType × LdType) × LdSpace L) ≃
   405	      (((LdType × LdType) × DirectLdSpace L.toDirectLdParams) ×
   406	        Fin (L.q / L.m)) :=
   407	  (Equiv.prodCongr (Equiv.refl (LdType × LdType))

   104	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]

   106	    (M : block → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota)
   107	    (hM : ∀ r, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (M r)) :
   108	    MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (blockDiagonalMeasurement M) := by
   109	  intro a
   110	  constructor
   111	  · change Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun r => (M r).effect a) *
   112	        Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun r => (M r).effect a) =
   113	      Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun r => (M r).effect a)
   114	    rw [← Matrix.blockDiagonal_mul]
   115	    congr 1
   116	    funext r
   117	    exact (hM r a).isIdempotentElem.eq
   118	  · change (Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun r => (M r).effect a))ᴴ =
   119	      Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun r => (M r).effect a)
   120	    rw [Matrix.blockDiagonal_conjTranspose]
   121	    congr 1
   122	    funext r
   123	    exact (hM r a).isSelfAdjoint.star_eq
   124	
   125	/-! ## The correlated residue state -/
   126	
   127	/-- The normalized maximally correlated state on the common seed-fiber
   128	residue. -/
   129	noncomputable def seedResidueAncilla (L : LdParams) :
   130	    EuclideanSpace ℂ
   131	      (Fin (L.q / L.m) × Fin (L.q / L.m)) := by
   132	  letI : Nonempty (Fin (L.q / L.m)) :=
   133	    Fin.pos_iff_nonempty.mp L.seedFiberCard_pos
   134	  exact eprState (Fin (L.q / L.m))
   135	
   136	/-- The seed-residue ancilla has unit norm. -/
   137	theorem seedResidueAncilla_norm (L : LdParams) :
   138	    ‖seedResidueAncilla L‖ = 1 := by
   139	  letI : Nonempty (Fin (L.q / L.m)) :=
   140	    Fin.pos_iff_nonempty.mp L.seedFiberCard_pos
   141	  exact eprState_norm (Fin (L.q / L.m))
   142	
   143	/-- Reindexing Euclidean coordinates along an equivalence preserves norm. -/
   144	theorem reindexState_norm_eq
   145	    {iota kappa : Type*}
   146	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   147	    [Fintype kappa] [DecidableEq kappa]
   148	    (e : iota ≃ kappa) (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ iota) :
   149	    ‖reindexState e psi‖ = ‖psi‖ := by
   150	  rw [← sq_eq_sq₀ (norm_nonneg _) (norm_nonneg _)]
   151	  rw [EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq, EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq]
   152	  change (∑ j : kappa, ‖psi (e.symm j)‖ ^ 2) = ∑ i : iota, ‖psi i‖ ^ 2
   153	  exact e.symm.sum_comp (fun i => ‖psi i‖ ^ 2)
   154	
   155	/-- The coordinate tensor of two Euclidean vectors has the product norm. -/
   156	theorem vecTensor_norm_eq
   157	    {iota kappa : Type*}
   158	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   159	    [Fintype kappa] [DecidableEq kappa]
   160	    (u : EuclideanSpace ℂ iota) (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ kappa) :
   161	    ‖vecTensor u v‖ = ‖u‖ * ‖v‖ := by
   162	  rw [← sq_eq_sq₀ (norm_nonneg _) (mul_nonneg (norm_nonneg _) (norm_nonneg _))]
   163	  rw [EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq, mul_pow, EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq,
   164	    EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq]
   165	  change (∑ p : iota × kappa, ‖u p.1 * v p.2‖ ^ 2) =
   166	    (∑ i : iota, ‖u i‖ ^ 2) * ∑ j : kappa, ‖v j‖ ^ 2
   167	  simp only [norm_mul, mul_pow]
   168	  rw [← Finset.univ_product_univ, Finset.sum_product, Finset.sum_mul]
   169	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   170	  intro i hi
   171	  rw [Finset.mul_sum]
   172	
   173	/-- Tensor the original strategy state with the maximally correlated residue
   174	state and shuffle the factors back into the two local carriers. -/
   175	noncomputable def seedFiberLiftedState
   176	    {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) (L : LdParams) :
   177	    EuclideanSpace ℂ
   178	      ((S.ιA × Fin (L.q / L.m)) × (S.ιB × Fin (L.q / L.m))) :=
   179	  reindexState prodShuffle (vecTensor S.ψ (seedResidueAncilla L))
   180	
   181	/-- The correlated seed-fiber lift preserves normalization of the strategy
   182	state. -/
   183	theorem seedFiberLiftedState_norm
   184	    {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) (L : LdParams) :
   185	    ‖seedFiberLiftedState S L‖ = 1 := by
   186	  rw [seedFiberLiftedState, reindexState_norm_eq, vecTensor_norm_eq,
   187	    S.ψ_norm, seedResidueAncilla_norm, one_mul]
   188	
   189	/-! ## From the seed-indexed game to the direct game -/
   190	
   191	/-- The seed-indexed question selected in one residue block of a direct
   192	question.  Applying `ldCL` ensures that irrelevant ambient coordinates are
   193	canonicalized exactly as in the source game. -/
   194	noncomputable def seededLdQuestion (L : LdParams)
   195	    (q : DirectLdQuestion L.toDirectLdParams)
   196	    (residue : Fin (L.q / L.m)) : LdQuestion L :=
   197	  (q.1, ldCL L q.1 (ldSpaceOfDirectResidue L q.2 residue))
   198	
   199	/-- Dilate a strategy for the seed-indexed low-degree game to the directly
   200	indexed game.  The two local carriers receive correlated copies of the seed
   201	residue, and each measurement is block diagonal in that residue. -/
   202	noncomputable def ldStrategyToDirect (L : LdParams)
   203	    (S : Strategy (ldGame L)) : Strategy (directLdGame L.toDirectLdParams) where
   204	  ιA := S.ιA × Fin (L.q / L.m)
   205	  ιB := S.ιB × Fin (L.q / L.m)
   206	  ψ := seedFiberLiftedState S L
   207	  ψ_norm := seedFiberLiftedState_norm S L
   208	  A q := blockDiagonalMeasurement fun residue =>
   209	    matrixMeasurementTransport (ldDirectAnswerEquiv L)
   210	      (S.A (seededLdQuestion L q residue))
   211	  B q := blockDiagonalMeasurement fun residue =>
   212	    matrixMeasurementTransport (ldDirectAnswerEquiv L)
   213	      (S.B (seededLdQuestion L q residue))
   214	
   215	/-- Projectivity is preserved by the correlated seed-fiber dilation. -/
   216	theorem ldStrategyToDirect_isProjective (L : LdParams)
   217	    (S : Strategy (ldGame L)) (hS : S.IsProjective) :
   218	    (ldStrategyToDirect L S).IsProjective := by
   219	  constructor
   220	  · intro q
   221	    apply blockDiagonalMeasurement_isProjective
   222	    intro residue
   223	    apply matrixMeasurementTransport_isProjective
   224	    exact hS.1 (seededLdQuestion L q residue)
   225	  · intro q
   226	    apply blockDiagonalMeasurement_isProjective
   227	    intro residue
   228	    apply matrixMeasurementTransport_isProjective
   229	    exact hS.2 (seededLdQuestion L q residue)
   230	
   231	@[simp] theorem ldStrategyToDirect_A_effect (L : LdParams)
   232	    (S : Strategy (ldGame L))
   233	    (q : DirectLdQuestion L.toDirectLdParams)
   234	    (answer : DirectLdAnswer L.toDirectLdParams) :
   235	    ((ldStrategyToDirect L S).A q).effect answer =
   236	      Matrix.blockDiagonal fun residue =>
   237	        (S.A (seededLdQuestion L q residue)).effect
   238	          ((ldDirectAnswerEquiv L).symm answer) :=
   239	  rfl
   240	
   241	@[simp] theorem ldStrategyToDirect_B_effect (L : LdParams)
   242	    (S : Strategy (ldGame L))
   243	    (q : DirectLdQuestion L.toDirectLdParams)
   244	    (answer : DirectLdAnswer L.toDirectLdParams) :
   245	    ((ldStrategyToDirect L S).B q).effect answer =
   246	      Matrix.blockDiagonal fun residue =>
   247	        (S.B (seededLdQuestion L q residue)).effect
   248	          ((ldDirectAnswerEquiv L).symm answer) :=
   249	  rfl
   250	
   251	/-- A direct question reconstructed in a residue block parses back to its
   252	canonical direct form. -/
   253	theorem parse_seededLdQuestion (L : LdParams)
   254	    (q : DirectLdQuestion L.toDirectLdParams)
   255	    (residue : Fin (L.q / L.m)) :
   256	    parseLdQuestion L (seededLdQuestion L q residue) =
   257	      (q.1, directLdMap L.toDirectLdParams q.1 q.2) := by
   258	  exact parseLdQuestion_ldCL_ofDirectResidue L q.1 q.2 residue
   259	
   260	/-- Coordinate formula for the correlated residue lift. -/
   261	theorem seedFiberLiftedState_apply
   262	    {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) (L : LdParams)
   263	    (i : S.ιA) (j : S.ιB)
   264	    (r s : Fin (L.q / L.m)) :
   265	    seedFiberLiftedState S L ((i, r), (j, s)) =
   266	      if r = s then
   267	        S.ψ (i, j) * (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card (Fin (L.q / L.m)) : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹
   268	      else 0 := by
   269	  letI : Nonempty (Fin (L.q / L.m)) :=
   270	    Fin.pos_iff_nonempty.mp L.seedFiberCard_pos
   271	  simp [seedFiberLiftedState, reindexState, vecTensor, seedResidueAncilla,
   272	    eprState, prodShuffle]
   273	
   274	end

     4	/-!
     5	# Strategy transport for the directly indexed low-degree game
     6	
     7	This module reads one coordinate of a projective directly indexed strategy as
     8	a two-space mature low individual degree strategy.  The question and answer
     9	transport of `Transport.Questions` supplies the canonical direct question of
    10	every mature line, with the reversed coordinate order and the leading index
    11	of the decoded diagonal direction, together with answer readouts that are
    12	covariant under line rebasing; this establishes all four covariance
    13	conditions of `ProjStrat`.  The module also records exact Born-weight
    14	formulas for both directions of strategy transport.
    15	
    16	## References
    17	
    18	- `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-458`
    19	- `references/ldt-paper/test_definition.tex:49-151`
    20	- `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`
    21	-/

    34	/-- Regard a matrix-valued projective measurement as a projective measurement
    35	in the mature LDT interface. -/
    36	noncomputable def matrixMeasurementToLDTProjMeas
    37	    {alpha iota : Type*} [Fintype alpha] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    38	    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota)
    39	    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M) :
    40	    MIPStarRE.LDT.ProjMeas alpha iota where
    41	  toMeasurement := {
    42	    toSubMeas := {
    43	      outcome := M.effect
    44	      total := 1
    45	      outcome_pos := M.pos
    46	      sum_eq_total := M.sum_eq_one
    47	      total_le_one := le_rfl
    48	    }
    49	    total_eq_one := rfl
    50	  }
    51	  proj a := (hM a).isIdempotentElem.eq

    56	    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M) (a : alpha) :

    58	  rfl

    60	/-- Point measurements obtained by querying the direct strategy and reading

   113	/-- The coordinate axis-line family is independent of the chosen affine
   114	parametrization of a mature line. -/
   115	theorem directCoordinateAxisMeasurement_reparam
   116	    (D : DirectLdParams) (r : Fin D.k)
   117	    {iota : Type*} [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   118	    (M : DirectLdQuestion D →
   119	      MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement (DirectLdAnswer D) iota)
   120	    (hM : ∀ q, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (M q)) :
   121	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   122	    AxisParallelMeasurementReparamInvariant D.toLDTParameters
   123	      (directCoordinateAxisMeasurement D r M hM) := by
   124	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   125	  classical
   126	  intro line t f
   127	  simp only [directCoordinateAxisMeasurement, ProjMeas.postprocess,
   128	    SubMeas.postprocess_outcome, matrixMeasurementToLDTProjMeas_outcome]
   129	  rw [directAxisQuestionOf_rebase]
   130	  have hfiber :
   131	      Finset.univ.filter (fun answer =>
   132	        directAxisAnswerReadout D r (line.rebaseAt t) answer =
   133	          AxisLinePolynomial.reparamAt f t) =
   134	        Finset.univ.filter (fun answer =>
   135	          directAxisAnswerReadout D r line answer = f) := by
   136	    ext answer
   137	    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
   138	    rw [directAxisAnswerReadout_rebase]
   139	    exact (AxisLinePolynomial.reparamAtEquiv t).injective.eq_iff
   140	  rw [hfiber]

   142	/-- The coordinate diagonal-line family is independent of the chosen affine
   143	parametrization, including the zero-direction convention. -/
   144	theorem directCoordinateDiagonalMeasurement_reparam
   145	    (D : DirectLdParams) (r : Fin D.k)

   171	private theorem strategy_carrier_nonempty {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) :
   172	    Nonempty (S.ιA × S.ιB) := by

   176	  have hzero : S.ψ = 0 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
   177	  have hnorm := S.ψ_norm
   178	  rw [hzero, norm_zero] at hnorm
   179	  exact zero_ne_one hnorm

   204	/-- The complex Born amplitude of a vector and two local effects. -/
   205	private noncomputable def vectorBornAmplitude
   206	    {iotaA iotaB : Type*}
   207	    [Fintype iotaA] [DecidableEq iotaA]
   208	    [Fintype iotaB] [DecidableEq iotaB]
   209	    (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ (iotaA × iotaB))
   210	    (A : Op iotaA) (B : Op iotaB) : ℂ :=
   211	  inner ℂ psi (applyOperatorToState (heteroKron A B) psi)

   213	/-- The real Born quadratic form of a vector and two local effects. -/
   214	private noncomputable def vectorBornWeight
   215	    {iotaA iotaB : Type*}
   216	    [Fintype iotaA] [DecidableEq iotaA]
   217	    [Fintype iotaB] [DecidableEq iotaB]
   218	    (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ (iotaA × iotaB))
   219	    (A : Op iotaA) (B : Op iotaB) : ℝ :=
   220	  (vectorBornAmplitude psi A B).re

220	  (vectorBornAmplitude psi A B).re

   223	    {iotaA iotaB : Type*}
   224	    [Fintype iotaA] [DecidableEq iotaA]
   225	    [Fintype iotaB] [DecidableEq iotaB]
   226	    (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ (iotaA × iotaB))

   228	    vectorBornAmplitude psi (A₁ + A₂) B =

   230	  unfold vectorBornAmplitude applyOperatorToState heteroKron Matrix.kronecker
   231	  rw [Matrix.add_kronecker]
   232	  simp

   266	private theorem vectorBornWeight_add_left
   267	    {iotaA iotaB : Type*}
   268	    [Fintype iotaA] [DecidableEq iotaA]
   269	    [Fintype iotaB] [DecidableEq iotaB]
   270	    (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ (iotaA × iotaB))
   271	    (A₁ A₂ : Op iotaA) (B : Op iotaB) :
   272	    vectorBornWeight psi (A₁ + A₂) B =
   273	      vectorBornWeight psi A₁ B + vectorBornWeight psi A₂ B := by
   274	  unfold vectorBornWeight
   275	  rw [vectorBornAmplitude_add_left, Complex.add_re]
   276	
   277	private theorem vectorBornWeight_add_right
   278	    {iotaA iotaB : Type*}
   279	    [Fintype iotaA] [DecidableEq iotaA]
   280	    [Fintype iotaB] [DecidableEq iotaB]
   281	    (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ (iotaA × iotaB))
   282	    (A : Op iotaA) (B₁ B₂ : Op iotaB) :
   283	    vectorBornWeight psi A (B₁ + B₂) =
   284	      vectorBornWeight psi A B₁ + vectorBornWeight psi A B₂ := by
   285	  unfold vectorBornWeight
   286	  rw [vectorBornAmplitude_add_right, Complex.add_re]
   287	
   288	private theorem vectorBornWeight_finset_sum_left
   289	    {alpha iotaA iotaB : Type*}
   290	    [Fintype iotaA] [DecidableEq iotaA]
   291	    [Fintype iotaB] [DecidableEq iotaB]
   292	    (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ (iotaA × iotaB))
   293	    (s : Finset alpha) (A : alpha → Op iotaA) (B : Op iotaB) :
   294	    vectorBornWeight psi (∑ a ∈ s, A a) B =
   295	      ∑ a ∈ s, vectorBornWeight psi (A a) B := by
   296	  classical
   297	  induction s using Finset.induction_on with
   298	  | empty =>
   299	      simp [vectorBornWeight, vectorBornAmplitude_zero_left]
   300	  | @insert a s ha ih =>
   301	      rw [Finset.sum_insert ha, Finset.sum_insert ha,
   302	        vectorBornWeight_add_left, ih]
   303	
   304	private theorem vectorBornWeight_finset_sum_right
   305	    {beta iotaA iotaB : Type*}
   306	    [Fintype iotaA] [DecidableEq iotaA]
   307	    [Fintype iotaB] [DecidableEq iotaB]
   308	    (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ (iotaA × iotaB))
   309	    (A : Op iotaA) (s : Finset beta) (B : beta → Op iotaB) :
   310	    vectorBornWeight psi A (∑ b ∈ s, B b) =
   311	      ∑ b ∈ s, vectorBornWeight psi A (B b) := by
   312	  classical
   313	  induction s using Finset.induction_on with
   314	  | empty =>
   315	      simp [vectorBornWeight, vectorBornAmplitude_zero_right]
   316	  | @insert b s hb ih =>
   317	      rw [Finset.sum_insert hb, Finset.sum_insert hb,
   318	        vectorBornWeight_add_right, ih]

   320	/-- Expectations in the density state associated with a strategy agree with
   321	the strategy's vector Born quadratic form. -/
   322	private theorem strategyQuantumState_ev_eq_vectorBornWeight
   323	    {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) (A : Op S.ιA) (B : Op S.ιB) :
   324	    ev (strategyQuantumState S) (opTensor A B) =
   325	      vectorBornWeight S.ψ A B := by
   326	  letI : Nonempty (S.ιA × S.ιB) := strategy_carrier_nonempty S
   327	  rw [show strategyQuantumState S =
   328	      PureState.toQuantumState (strategyPureState S) by
   329	        simp [strategyQuantumState],
   330	    PureState.ev_eq_re_inner]
   331	  unfold vectorBornWeight vectorBornAmplitude applyOperatorToState heteroKron opTensor
   332	  simp_rw [EuclideanSpace.inner_eq_star_dotProduct]
   333	  change (star S.ψ ⬝ᵥ
   334	      (Matrix.kronecker A B *ᵥ S.ψ)).re =
   335	    ((Matrix.kronecker A B *ᵥ S.ψ) ⬝ᵥ star S.ψ).re
   336	  rw [dotProduct_comm]

   338	/-- Postprocessing both local measurements gives the exact double sum of the
   339	original Born weights over the two answer fibers. -/
   340	theorem directPostprocessBornWeight
   341	    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
   342	    (hS : S.IsProjective)
   343	    {alpha beta : Type*} [Fintype alpha] [DecidableEq alpha]
   344	    [Fintype beta] [DecidableEq beta]
   345	    (x y : DirectLdQuestion D)
   346	    (readA : DirectLdAnswer D → alpha)
   347	    (readB : DirectLdAnswer D → beta)
   348	    (a : alpha) (b : beta) :
   349	    ev (strategyQuantumState S)
   350	        (opTensor
   351	          ((ProjMeas.postprocess
   352	            (matrixMeasurementToLDTProjMeas (S.A x) (hS.1 x)) readA).outcome a)
   353	          ((ProjMeas.postprocess
   354	            (matrixMeasurementToLDTProjMeas (S.B y) (hS.2 y)) readB).outcome b)) =
   355	      ∑ directA ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun answer => readA answer = a),
   356	        ∑ directB ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun answer => readB answer = b),
   357	          outcomeWeight S x y directA directB := by
   358	  rw [strategyQuantumState_ev_eq_vectorBornWeight]
   359	  simp only [ProjMeas.postprocess, SubMeas.postprocess_outcome,
   360	    matrixMeasurementToLDTProjMeas_outcome]
   361	  rw [vectorBornWeight_finset_sum_left]
   362	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   363	  intro directA _
   364	  rw [vectorBornWeight_finset_sum_right]
   365	  rfl

   367	/-- Correlated residue registers turn two block-diagonal effects into the
   368	uniform average of their matching source-block Born weights. -/
   369	private theorem seedFiberBlockBornAmplitude
   370	    {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) (L : LdParams)
   371	    (A : Fin (L.q / L.m) → Op S.ιA)
   372	    (B : Fin (L.q / L.m) → Op S.ιB) :
   373	    vectorBornAmplitude (seedFiberLiftedState S L)
   374	        (Matrix.blockDiagonal A) (Matrix.blockDiagonal B) =
   375	      (Fintype.card (Fin (L.q / L.m)) : ℂ)⁻¹ *
   376	        ∑ residue, vectorBornAmplitude S.ψ (A residue) (B residue) := by
   377	  classical
   378	  letI : Nonempty (Fin (L.q / L.m)) :=
   379	    Fin.pos_iff_nonempty.mp L.seedFiberCard_pos
   380	  unfold vectorBornAmplitude applyOperatorToState heteroKron Matrix.kronecker
   381	  simp_rw [EuclideanSpace.inner_eq_star_dotProduct]
   382	  simp only [Matrix.toEuclideanLin, Matrix.toLpLin_apply,
   383	    dotProduct, Matrix.mulVec]
   384	  simp_rw [← Finset.univ_product_univ, Finset.sum_product]
   385	  simp [seedFiberLiftedState_apply, Matrix.blockDiagonal_apply,
   386	    mul_assoc, mul_comm]
   387	  ring_nf
   388	  simp_rw [mul_assoc, ← Finset.mul_sum]
   389	  ring_nf
   390	  simp_rw [mul_assoc, ← Finset.mul_sum]
   391	  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   392	  rw [← mul_assoc]
   393	  congr 1
   394	  rw [← pow_two, inv_pow, ← Complex.ofReal_pow,
   395	    Real.sq_sqrt (Nat.cast_nonneg (L.q / L.m))]
   396	  norm_cast
   397	  exact Complex.ofReal_inv _
   398	
   399	/-- Correlated residue registers give the uniform average of the source-block
   400	Born weights. -/
   401	private theorem seedFiberBlockBornWeight
   402	    {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) (L : LdParams)
   403	    (A : Fin (L.q / L.m) → Op S.ιA)
   404	    (B : Fin (L.q / L.m) → Op S.ιB) :
   405	    vectorBornWeight (seedFiberLiftedState S L)
   406	        (Matrix.blockDiagonal A) (Matrix.blockDiagonal B) =
   407	      (Fintype.card (Fin (L.q / L.m)) : ℝ)⁻¹ *
   408	        ∑ residue, vectorBornWeight S.ψ (A residue) (B residue) := by
   409	  unfold vectorBornWeight
   410	  rw [seedFiberBlockBornAmplitude]
   411	  simp [Complex.mul_re, Complex.inv_re, Complex.inv_im]
   412	
   413	/-- The Born weight of the seed-bearing direct adapter is the uniform average
   414	of the original seed-dependent Born weights over the correlated residue. -/
   415	theorem ldStrategyToDirect_bornWeight
   416	    (L : LdParams) (S : Strategy (ldGame L))
   417	    (x y : DirectLdQuestion L.toDirectLdParams)
   418	    (a b : DirectLdAnswer L.toDirectLdParams) :
   419	    outcomeWeight (ldStrategyToDirect L S) x y a b =
   420	      (Fintype.card (Fin (L.q / L.m)) : ℝ)⁻¹ *
   421	        ∑ residue,
   422	          outcomeWeight S
   423	            (seededLdQuestion L x residue)
   424	            (seededLdQuestion L y residue)
   425	            ((ldDirectAnswerEquiv L).symm a)
   426	            ((ldDirectAnswerEquiv L).symm b) := by
   427	  change vectorBornWeight (seedFiberLiftedState S L)
   428	      (Matrix.blockDiagonal fun residue =>
   429	        (S.A (seededLdQuestion L x residue)).effect
   430	          ((ldDirectAnswerEquiv L).symm a))
   431	      (Matrix.blockDiagonal fun residue =>
   432	        (S.B (seededLdQuestion L y residue)).effect
   433	          ((ldDirectAnswerEquiv L).symm b)) = _
   434	  exact seedFiberBlockBornWeight S L _ _

   436	/-- Read coordinate `r` of a projective direct-game strategy as a two-space
   437	projective strategy for the mature low individual degree interface. -/
   438	noncomputable def directCoordinateProjStrat
   439	    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
   440	    (hS : S.IsProjective) (r : Fin D.k) :
   441	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   442	    ProjStrat D.toLDTParameters S.ιA S.ιB := by
   443	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   444	  exact {
   445	    state := strategyQuantumState S
   446	    isNormalized := strategyQuantumState_isNormalized S
   447	    pointMeasurementA := directCoordinatePointMeasurement D r S.A hS.1
   448	    axisParallelMeasurementA := directCoordinateAxisMeasurement D r S.A hS.1
   449	    axisParallelReparamInvariantA :=
   450	      directCoordinateAxisMeasurement_reparam D r S.A hS.1
   451	    diagonalMeasurementA := directCoordinateDiagonalMeasurement D r S.A hS.1
   452	    diagonalReparamInvariantA :=
   453	      directCoordinateDiagonalMeasurement_reparam D r S.A hS.1
   454	    pointMeasurementB := directCoordinatePointMeasurement D r S.B hS.2
   455	    axisParallelMeasurementB := directCoordinateAxisMeasurement D r S.B hS.2
   456	    axisParallelReparamInvariantB :=
   457	      directCoordinateAxisMeasurement_reparam D r S.B hS.2
   458	    diagonalMeasurementB := directCoordinateDiagonalMeasurement D r S.B hS.2
   459	    diagonalReparamInvariantB :=
   460	      directCoordinateDiagonalMeasurement_reparam D r S.B hS.2
   461	  }

   463	/-- Point Born weights of the coordinate strategy are exactly the sums over
   464	the corresponding direct-answer readout fibers. -/
   465	theorem directCoordinateProjStrat_point_bornWeight
   466	    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
   467	    (hS : S.IsProjective) (r : Fin D.k)
   468	    (u v : Point D.toLDTParameters)
   469	    (a b : Fq D.toLDTParameters) :
   470	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   471	    ev (directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).state
   472	        (opTensor
   473	          (((directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).pointMeasurementA u).outcome a)
   474	          (((directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).pointMeasurementB v).outcome b)) =
   475	      ∑ directA ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun answer =>
   476	          directPointAnswerReadout D r answer = a),
   477	        ∑ directB ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun answer =>
   478	            directPointAnswerReadout D r answer = b),
   479	          outcomeWeight S (directPointQuestionOf D u)
   480	            (directPointQuestionOf D v) directA directB := by
   481	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   482	  change ev (strategyQuantumState S)
   483	      (opTensor
   484	        ((ProjMeas.postprocess
   485	          (matrixMeasurementToLDTProjMeas
   486	            (S.A (directPointQuestionOf D u))
   487	            (hS.1 (directPointQuestionOf D u)))
   488	          (directPointAnswerReadout D r)).outcome a)
   489	        ((ProjMeas.postprocess
   490	          (matrixMeasurementToLDTProjMeas
   491	            (S.B (directPointQuestionOf D v))
   492	            (hS.2 (directPointQuestionOf D v)))
   493	          (directPointAnswerReadout D r)).outcome b)) = _
   494	  exact directPostprocessBornWeight D S hS
   495	    (directPointQuestionOf D u) (directPointQuestionOf D v)
   496	    (directPointAnswerReadout D r) (directPointAnswerReadout D r) a b
   497	
   498	/-- Axis-line Born weights of the coordinate strategy are exactly the sums
   499	over the corresponding rebased direct-answer fibers. -/

   501	    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))

   515	            directAxisAnswerReadout D r lineB answer = g),

    16	/-- A genuinely affine diagonal line in `F_q^m`. -/
